original_text: And the Philistines came up yet again, and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim.

translated_text:
And when David enquired of the LORD, he said, Thou shalt not go up;
but fetch a compass behind them, and come upon them over against the mulberry trees.
original_text:
And when David enquired of the LORD, he said, Thou shalt not go up;
but fetch a compass behind them, and come upon them over against the mulberry trees.

translated_text: And let it be, when thou hearest the sound of a going in the tops of the mulberry trees, that then thou shalt bestir thyself: for then shall the LORD go out before thee, to smite the host of the Philistines.
original_text: And let it be, when thou hearest the sound of a going in the tops of the mulberry trees, that then thou shalt bestir thyself: for then shall the LORD go out before thee, to smite the host of the Philistines.

translated_text: And David did so, as the LORD had commanded him; and smote the Philistines from Geba until thou come to Gazer.
original_text: And David did so, as the LORD had commanded him; and smote the Philistines from Geba until thou come to Gazer.

translated_text: And when Saul’s son heard that Abner was dead in Hebron, his hands were feeble, and all the Israelites were troubled.
original_text: And when Saul’s son heard that Abner was dead in Hebron, his hands were feeble, and all the Israelites were troubled.

translated_text:
And Saul’s son had two men
that were captains of bands: the name of the one
was Baanah, and the name of the other Rechab, the sons of Rimmon a Beerothite, of the children of Benjamin: (for Beeroth also was reckoned to Benjamin:
original_text:
And Saul’s son had two men
that were captains of bands: the name of the one
was Baanah, and the name of the other Rechab, the sons of Rimmon a Beerothite, of the children of Benjamin: (for Beeroth also was reckoned to Benjamin:

translated_text: And the Beerothites fled to Gittaim, and were sojourners there until this day.)
original_text: And the Beerothites fled to Gittaim, and were sojourners there until this day.)

translated_text:
And Jonathan, Saul’s son, had a son
that was lame of
his feet. He was five years old when the tidings came of Saul and Jonathan out of Jezreel, and his nurse took him up, and fled: and it came to pass, as she made haste to flee, that he fell, and became lame. And his name
was Mephibosheth.
original_text:
And Jonathan, Saul’s son, had a son
that was lame of
his feet. He was five years old when the tidings came of Saul and Jonathan out of Jezreel, and his nurse took him up, and fled: and it came to pass, as she made haste to flee, that he fell, and became lame. And his name
was Mephibosheth.

translated_text: And the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, went, and came about the heat of the day to the house of Ish-bosheth, who lay on a bed at noon.
original_text: And the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, went, and came about the heat of the day to the house of Ish-bosheth, who lay on a bed at noon.

translated_text:
And they came thither into the midst of the house,
as though
 they would have fetched wheat; and they smote him under the fifth
rib: and Rechab and Baanah his brother escaped.
original_text:
And they came thither into the midst of the house,
as though
 they would have fetched wheat; and they smote him under the fifth
rib: and Rechab and Baanah his brother escaped.

translated_text: For when they came into the house, he lay on his bed in his bedchamber, and they smote him, and slew him, and beheaded him, and took his head, and gat them away through the plain all night.
original_text: For when they came into the house, he lay on his bed in his bedchamber, and they smote him, and slew him, and beheaded him, and took his head, and gat them away through the plain all night.

translated_text: And they brought the head of Ish-bosheth unto David to Hebron, and said to the king, Behold the head of Ish-bosheth the son of Saul thine enemy, which sought thy life; and the LORD hath avenged my lord the king this day of Saul, and of his seed.
original_text: And they brought the head of Ish-bosheth unto David to Hebron, and said to the king, Behold the head of Ish-bosheth the son of Saul thine enemy, which sought thy life; and the LORD hath avenged my lord the king this day of Saul, and of his seed.

translated_text: And David answered Rechab and Baanah his brother, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and said unto them, As the LORD liveth, who hath redeemed my soul out of all adversity,
original_text: And David answered Rechab and Baanah his brother, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and said unto them, As the LORD liveth, who hath redeemed my soul out of all adversity,

translated_text:
When one told me, saying, Behold, Saul is dead, thinking to have brought good tidings, I took hold of him, and slew him in Ziklag, who
thought
 that I would have given him a reward for his tidings:
original_text:
When one told me, saying, Behold, Saul is dead, thinking to have brought good tidings, I took hold of him, and slew him in Ziklag, who
thought
 that I would have given him a reward for his tidings:

translated_text: How much more, when wicked men have slain a righteous person in his own house upon his bed? shall I not therefore now require his blood of your hand, and take you away from the earth?
original_text: How much more, when wicked men have slain a righteous person in his own house upon his bed? shall I not therefore now require his blood of your hand, and take you away from the earth?

translated_text:
And David commanded his young men, and they slew them, and cut off their hands and their feet, and hanged
them up over the pool in Hebron. But they took the head of Ish-bosheth, and buried
it in the sepulchre of Abner in Hebron.
original_text:
And David commanded his young men, and they slew them, and cut off their hands and their feet, and hanged
them up over the pool in Hebron. But they took the head of Ish-bosheth, and buried
it in the sepulchre of Abner in Hebron.

translated_text: And it came to pass, when the king sat in his house, and the LORD had given him rest round about from all his enemies;
original_text: And it came to pass, when the king sat in his house, and the LORD had given him rest round about from all his enemies;

translated_text: That the king said unto Nathan the prophet, See now, I dwell in an house of cedar, but the ark of God dwelleth within curtains.
original_text: That the king said unto Nathan the prophet, See now, I dwell in an house of cedar, but the ark of God dwelleth within curtains.

translated_text:
And Nathan said to the king, Go, do all that
is in thine heart; for the LORD
is with thee.
original_text:
And Nathan said to the king, Go, do all that
is in thine heart; for the LORD
is with thee.

translated_text: And it came to pass that night, that the word of the LORD came unto Nathan, saying,
original_text: And it came to pass that night, that the word of the LORD came unto Nathan, saying,

translated_text: Go and tell my servant David, Thus saith the LORD, Shalt thou build me an house for me to dwell in?
original_text: Go and tell my servant David, Thus saith the LORD, Shalt thou build me an house for me to dwell in?

translated_text:
Whereas I have not dwelt in
any house since the time that I brought up the children of Israel out of Egypt, even to this day, but have walked in a tent and in a tabernacle.
original_text:
Whereas I have not dwelt in
any house since the time that I brought up the children of Israel out of Egypt, even to this day, but have walked in a tent and in a tabernacle.

translated_text:
In all
the places wherein I have walked with all the children of Israel spake I a word with any of the tribes of Israel, whom I commanded to feed my people Israel, saying, Why build ye not me an house of cedar?
original_text:
In all
the places wherein I have walked with all the children of Israel spake I a word with any of the tribes of Israel, whom I commanded to feed my people Israel, saying, Why build ye not me an house of cedar?

translated_text: Now therefore so shalt thou say unto my servant David, Thus saith the LORD of hosts, I took thee from the sheepcote, from following the sheep, to be ruler over my people, over Israel:
original_text: Now therefore so shalt thou say unto my servant David, Thus saith the LORD of hosts, I took thee from the sheepcote, from following the sheep, to be ruler over my people, over Israel:

translated_text:
And I was with thee whithersoever thou wentest, and have cut off all thine enemies out of thy sight, and have made thee a great name, like unto the name of the great
men that
are in the earth.
original_text:
And I was with thee whithersoever thou wentest, and have cut off all thine enemies out of thy sight, and have made thee a great name, like unto the name of the great
men that
are in the earth.

translated_text: Moreover I will appoint a place for my people Israel, and will plant them, that they may dwell in a place of their own, and move no more; neither shall the children of wickedness afflict them any more, as beforetime,
original_text: Moreover I will appoint a place for my people Israel, and will plant them, that they may dwell in a place of their own, and move no more; neither shall the children of wickedness afflict them any more, as beforetime,

translated_text:
And as since the time that I commanded judges
to be over my people Israel, and have caused thee to rest from all thine enemies. Also the LORD telleth thee that he will make thee an house.
original_text:
And as since the time that I commanded judges
to be over my people Israel, and have caused thee to rest from all thine enemies. Also the LORD telleth thee that he will make thee an house.

translated_text: And when thy days be fulfilled, and thou shalt sleep with thy fathers, I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom.
original_text: And when thy days be fulfilled, and thou shalt sleep with thy fathers, I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom.

translated_text: He shall build an house for my name, and I will stablish the throne of his kingdom for ever.
original_text: He shall build an house for my name, and I will stablish the throne of his kingdom for ever.

translated_text: I will be his father, and he shall be my son. If he commit iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the children of men:
original_text: I will be his father, and he shall be my son. If he commit iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the children of men:

translated_text:
But my mercy shall not depart away from him, as I took
it
 from Saul, whom I put away before thee.
original_text:
But my mercy shall not depart away from him, as I took
it
 from Saul, whom I put away before thee.

translated_text: And thine house and thy kingdom shall be established for ever before thee: thy throne shall be established for ever.
original_text: And thine house and thy kingdom shall be established for ever before thee: thy throne shall be established for ever.

translated_text: According to all these words, and according to all this vision, so did Nathan speak unto David.
original_text: According to all these words, and according to all this vision, so did Nathan speak unto David.

translated_text:
Then went king David in, and sat before the LORD, and he said, Who
am I, O Lord GOD? and what
is my house, that thou hast brought me hitherto?
original_text:
Then went king David in, and sat before the LORD, and he said, Who
am I, O Lord GOD? and what
is my house, that thou hast brought me hitherto?

translated_text:
And this was yet a small thing in thy sight, O Lord GOD; but thou hast spoken also of thy servant’s house for a great while to come. And
is
 this the manner of man, O Lord GOD?
original_text:
And this was yet a small thing in thy sight, O Lord GOD; but thou hast spoken also of thy servant’s house for a great while to come. And
is
 this the manner of man, O Lord GOD?

translated_text: And what can David say more unto thee? for thou, Lord GOD, knowest thy servant.
original_text: And what can David say more unto thee? for thou, Lord GOD, knowest thy servant.

translated_text:
For thy word’s sake, and according to thine own heart, hast thou done all these great things, to make thy servant know
them.
original_text:
For thy word’s sake, and according to thine own heart, hast thou done all these great things, to make thy servant know
them.

translated_text:
Wherefore thou art great, O LORD God: for
there is none like thee, neither
is there any God beside thee, according to all that we have heard with our ears.
original_text:
Wherefore thou art great, O LORD God: for
there is none like thee, neither
is there any God beside thee, according to all that we have heard with our ears.

translated_text:
And what one nation in the earth
is like thy people,
even like Israel, whom God went to redeem for a people to himself, and to make him a name, and to do for you great things and terrible, for thy land, before thy people, which thou redeemedst to thee from Egypt,
from
 the nations and their gods?
original_text:
And what one nation in the earth
is like thy people,
even like Israel, whom God went to redeem for a people to himself, and to make him a name, and to do for you great things and terrible, for thy land, before thy people, which thou redeemedst to thee from Egypt,
from
 the nations and their gods?

translated_text:
For thou hast confirmed to thyself thy people Israel
to be
 a people unto thee for ever: and thou, LORD, art become their God.
original_text:
For thou hast confirmed to thyself thy people Israel
to be
 a people unto thee for ever: and thou, LORD, art become their God.

translated_text:
And now, O LORD God, the word that thou hast spoken concerning thy servant, and concerning his house, establish
it for ever, and do as thou hast said.
original_text:
And now, O LORD God, the word that thou hast spoken concerning thy servant, and concerning his house, establish
it for ever, and do as thou hast said.

translated_text:
And let thy name be magnified for ever, saying, The LORD of hosts
is the God over Israel: and let the house of thy servant David be established before thee.
original_text:
And let thy name be magnified for ever, saying, The LORD of hosts
is the God over Israel: and let the house of thy servant David be established before thee.

translated_text: For thou, O LORD of hosts, God of Israel, hast revealed to thy servant, saying, I will build thee an house: therefore hath thy servant found in his heart to pray this prayer unto thee.
original_text: For thou, O LORD of hosts, God of Israel, hast revealed to thy servant, saying, I will build thee an house: therefore hath thy servant found in his heart to pray this prayer unto thee.

translated_text:
And now, O Lord GOD, thou
art that God, and thy words be true, and thou hast promised this goodness unto thy servant:
original_text:
And now, O Lord GOD, thou
art that God, and thy words be true, and thou hast promised this goodness unto thy servant:

translated_text:
Therefore now let it please thee to bless the house of thy servant, that it may continue for ever before thee: for thou, O Lord GOD, hast spoken
it: and with thy blessing let the house of thy servant be blessed for ever.
original_text:
Therefore now let it please thee to bless the house of thy servant, that it may continue for ever before thee: for thou, O Lord GOD, hast spoken
it: and with thy blessing let the house of thy servant be blessed for ever.

translated_text:
Again, David gathered together all
the chosen
men
 of Israel, thirty thousand.
original_text:
Again, David gathered together all
the chosen
men
 of Israel, thirty thousand.

translated_text:
And David arose, and went with all the people that
were with him from Baale of Judah, to bring up from thence the ark of God, whose name is called by the name of the LORD of hosts that dwelleth
between the cherubims.
original_text:
And David arose, and went with all the people that
were with him from Baale of Judah, to bring up from thence the ark of God, whose name is called by the name of the LORD of hosts that dwelleth
between the cherubims.

translated_text:
And they set the ark of God upon a new cart, and brought it out of the house of Abinadab that
was in Gibeah: and Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, drave the new cart.
original_text:
And they set the ark of God upon a new cart, and brought it out of the house of Abinadab that
was in Gibeah: and Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, drave the new cart.

translated_text:
And they brought it out of the house of Abinadab which
was
 at Gibeah, accompanying the ark of God: and Ahio went before the ark.
original_text:
And they brought it out of the house of Abinadab which
was
 at Gibeah, accompanying the ark of God: and Ahio went before the ark.

translated_text:
And David and all the house of Israel played before the LORD on all manner of
instruments made of fir wood, even on harps, and on psalteries, and on timbrels, and on cornets, and on cymbals.
original_text:
And David and all the house of Israel played before the LORD on all manner of
instruments made of fir wood, even on harps, and on psalteries, and on timbrels, and on cornets, and on cymbals.

translated_text:
And when they came to Nachon’s threshingfloor, Uzzah put forth
his hand to the ark of God, and took hold of it; for the oxen shook
it.
original_text:
And when they came to Nachon’s threshingfloor, Uzzah put forth
his hand to the ark of God, and took hold of it; for the oxen shook
it.

translated_text:
And the anger of the LORD was kindled against Uzzah; and God smote him there for
his error; and there he died by the ark of God.
original_text:
And the anger of the LORD was kindled against Uzzah; and God smote him there for
his error; and there he died by the ark of God.

translated_text: And David was displeased, because the LORD had made a breach upon Uzzah: and he called the name of the place Perez-uzzah to this day.
original_text: And David was displeased, because the LORD had made a breach upon Uzzah: and he called the name of the place Perez-uzzah to this day.

translated_text: And David was afraid of the LORD that day, and said, How shall the ark of the LORD come to me?
original_text: And David was afraid of the LORD that day, and said, How shall the ark of the LORD come to me?

translated_text: So David would not remove the ark of the LORD unto him into the city of David: but David carried it aside into the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.
original_text: So David would not remove the ark of the LORD unto him into the city of David: but David carried it aside into the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.

translated_text: And the ark of the LORD continued in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite three months: and the LORD blessed Obed-edom, and all his household.
original_text: And the ark of the LORD continued in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite three months: and the LORD blessed Obed-edom, and all his household.

translated_text:
And it was told king David, saying, The LORD hath blessed the house of Obed-edom, and all that
pertaineth unto him, because of the ark of God. So David went and brought up the ark of God from the house of Obed-edom into the city of David with gladness.
original_text:
And it was told king David, saying, The LORD hath blessed the house of Obed-edom, and all that
pertaineth unto him, because of the ark of God. So David went and brought up the ark of God from the house of Obed-edom into the city of David with gladness.

translated_text:
And it was
so, that when they that bare the ark of the LORD had gone six paces, he sacrificed oxen and fatlings.
original_text:
And it was
so, that when they that bare the ark of the LORD had gone six paces, he sacrificed oxen and fatlings.

translated_text:
And David danced before the LORD with all
his might; and David
was girded with a linen ephod.
original_text:
And David danced before the LORD with all
his might; and David
was girded with a linen ephod.

translated_text: So David and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of the LORD with shouting, and with the sound of the trumpet.
original_text: So David and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of the LORD with shouting, and with the sound of the trumpet.

translated_text: And as the ark of the LORD came into the city of David, Michal Saul’s daughter looked through a window, and saw king David leaping and dancing before the LORD; and she despised him in her heart.
original_text: And as the ark of the LORD came into the city of David, Michal Saul’s daughter looked through a window, and saw king David leaping and dancing before the LORD; and she despised him in her heart.

translated_text: And they brought in the ark of the LORD, and set it in his place, in the midst of the tabernacle that David had pitched for it: and David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD.
original_text: And they brought in the ark of the LORD, and set it in his place, in the midst of the tabernacle that David had pitched for it: and David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD.

translated_text: And as soon as David had made an end of offering burnt offerings and peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD of hosts.
original_text: And as soon as David had made an end of offering burnt offerings and peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD of hosts.

translated_text:
And he dealt among all the people,
even among the whole multitude of Israel, as well to the women as men, to every one a cake of bread, and a good piece
of flesh, and a flagon
of wine.
 So all the people departed every one to his house.
original_text:
And he dealt among all the people,
even among the whole multitude of Israel, as well to the women as men, to every one a cake of bread, and a good piece
of flesh, and a flagon
of wine.
 So all the people departed every one to his house.

translated_text: Then David returned to bless his household. And Michal the daughter of Saul came out to meet David, and said, How glorious was the king of Israel today, who uncovered himself to day in the eyes of the handmaids of his servants, as one of the vain fellows shamelessly uncovereth himself!
original_text: Then David returned to bless his household. And Michal the daughter of Saul came out to meet David, and said, How glorious was the king of Israel today, who uncovered himself to day in the eyes of the handmaids of his servants, as one of the vain fellows shamelessly uncovereth himself!

translated_text:
And David said unto Michal,
It was before the LORD, which chose me before thy father, and before all his house, to appoint me ruler over the people of the LORD, over Israel: therefore will I play before the LORD.
original_text:
And David said unto Michal,
It was before the LORD, which chose me before thy father, and before all his house, to appoint me ruler over the people of the LORD, over Israel: therefore will I play before the LORD.

translated_text: And I will yet be more vile than thus, and will be base in mine own sight: and of the maidservants which thou hast spoken of, of them shall I be had in honour.
original_text: And I will yet be more vile than thus, and will be base in mine own sight: and of the maidservants which thou hast spoken of, of them shall I be had in honour.

translated_text: Therefore Michal the daughter of Saul had no child unto the day of her death.
original_text: Therefore Michal the daughter of Saul had no child unto the day of her death.

translated_text: And David said, Is there yet any that is left of the house of Saul, that I may shew him kindness for Jonathan’s sake?
original_text: And David said, Is there yet any that is left of the house of Saul, that I may shew him kindness for Jonathan’s sake?

translated_text:
And
there was of the house of Saul a servant whose name
was Ziba. And when they had called him unto David, the king said unto him,
Art thou Ziba? And he said, Thy servant
is he.
original_text:
And
there was of the house of Saul a servant whose name
was Ziba. And when they had called him unto David, the king said unto him,
Art thou Ziba? And he said, Thy servant
is he.

translated_text:
And the king said,
Is there not yet any of the house of Saul, that I may shew the kindness of God unto him? And Ziba said unto the king, Jonathan hath yet a son,
which is lame on
his feet.
original_text:
And the king said,
Is there not yet any of the house of Saul, that I may shew the kindness of God unto him? And Ziba said unto the king, Jonathan hath yet a son,
which is lame on
his feet.

translated_text:
And the king said unto him, Where
is he? And Ziba said unto the king, Behold, he
is in the house of Machir, the son of Ammiel, in Lo-debar.
original_text:
And the king said unto him, Where
is he? And Ziba said unto the king, Behold, he
is in the house of Machir, the son of Ammiel, in Lo-debar.

translated_text: Then king David sent, and fetched him out of the house of Machir, the son of Ammiel, from Lo-debar.
original_text: Then king David sent, and fetched him out of the house of Machir, the son of Ammiel, from Lo-debar.

translated_text: Now when Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, was come unto David, he fell on his face, and did reverence. And David said, Mephibosheth. And he answered, Behold thy servant!
original_text: Now when Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, was come unto David, he fell on his face, and did reverence. And David said, Mephibosheth. And he answered, Behold thy servant!

translated_text: And David said unto him, Fear not: for I will surely shew thee kindness for Jonathan thy father’s sake, and will restore thee all the land of Saul thy father; and thou shalt eat bread at my table continually.
original_text: And David said unto him, Fear not: for I will surely shew thee kindness for Jonathan thy father’s sake, and will restore thee all the land of Saul thy father; and thou shalt eat bread at my table continually.

translated_text:
And he bowed himself, and said, What is thy servant, that thou shouldest look upon such a dead dog as I
am?
original_text:
And he bowed himself, and said, What is thy servant, that thou shouldest look upon such a dead dog as I
am?

translated_text: Then the king called to Ziba, Saul’s servant, and said unto him, I have given unto thy master’s son all that pertained to Saul and to all his house.
original_text: Then the king called to Ziba, Saul’s servant, and said unto him, I have given unto thy master’s son all that pertained to Saul and to all his house.

translated_text:
Thou therefore, and thy sons, and thy servants, shall till the land for him, and thou shalt bring in
the fruits, that thy master’s son may have food to eat: but Mephibosheth thy master’s son shall eat bread alway at my table. Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.
original_text:
Thou therefore, and thy sons, and thy servants, shall till the land for him, and thou shalt bring in
the fruits, that thy master’s son may have food to eat: but Mephibosheth thy master’s son shall eat bread alway at my table. Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.

translated_text:
Then said Ziba unto the king, According to all that my lord the king hath commanded his servant, so shall thy servant do. As for Mephibosheth,
said the king, he shall eat at my table, as one of the king’s sons.
original_text:
Then said Ziba unto the king, According to all that my lord the king hath commanded his servant, so shall thy servant do. As for Mephibosheth,
said the king, he shall eat at my table, as one of the king’s sons.

translated_text:
And Mephibosheth had a young son, whose name
was Micha. And all that dwelt in the house of Ziba
were servants unto Mephibosheth.
original_text:
And Mephibosheth had a young son, whose name
was Micha. And all that dwelt in the house of Ziba
were servants unto Mephibosheth.

translated_text: So Mephibosheth dwelt in Jerusalem: for he did eat continually at the king’s table; and was lame on both his feet.
original_text: So Mephibosheth dwelt in Jerusalem: for he did eat continually at the king’s table; and was lame on both his feet.

translated_text: And after this it came to pass, that David smote the Philistines, and subdued them: and David took Metheg-ammah out of the hand of the Philistines.
original_text: And after this it came to pass, that David smote the Philistines, and subdued them: and David took Metheg-ammah out of the hand of the Philistines.

translated_text:
And he smote Moab, and measured them with a line, casting them down to the ground; even with two lines measured he to put to death, and with one full line to keep alive. And so the Moabites became David’s servants,
and
 brought gifts.
original_text:
And he smote Moab, and measured them with a line, casting them down to the ground; even with two lines measured he to put to death, and with one full line to keep alive. And so the Moabites became David’s servants,
and
 brought gifts.

translated_text: David smote also Hadadezer, the son of Rehob, king of Zobah, as he went to recover his border at the river Euphrates.
original_text: David smote also Hadadezer, the son of Rehob, king of Zobah, as he went to recover his border at the river Euphrates.

translated_text:
And David took from him a thousand
chariots, and seven hundred horsemen, and twenty thousand footmen: and David houghed all the chariot
horses, but reserved of them
for an hundred chariots.
original_text:
And David took from him a thousand
chariots, and seven hundred horsemen, and twenty thousand footmen: and David houghed all the chariot
horses, but reserved of them
for an hundred chariots.

translated_text: And when the Syrians of Damascus came to succour Hadadezer king of Zobah, David slew of the Syrians two and twenty thousand men.
original_text: And when the Syrians of Damascus came to succour Hadadezer king of Zobah, David slew of the Syrians two and twenty thousand men.

translated_text:
Then David put garrisons in Syria of Damascus: and the Syrians became servants to David,
and brought gifts. And the LORD preserved David whithersoever he went.
original_text:
Then David put garrisons in Syria of Damascus: and the Syrians became servants to David,
and brought gifts. And the LORD preserved David whithersoever he went.

translated_text: And David took the shields of gold that were on the servants of Hadadezer, and brought them to Jerusalem.
original_text: And David took the shields of gold that were on the servants of Hadadezer, and brought them to Jerusalem.

translated_text: And from Betah, and from Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, king David took exceeding much brass.
original_text: And from Betah, and from Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, king David took exceeding much brass.

translated_text: When Toi king of Hamath heard that David had smitten all the host of Hadadezer,
original_text: When Toi king of Hamath heard that David had smitten all the host of Hadadezer,

translated_text:
Then Toi sent Joram his son unto king David, to salute him, and to bless him, because he had fought against Hadadezer, and smitten him: for Hadadezer had wars with Toi. And
Joram brought with him vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and vessels of brass:
original_text:
Then Toi sent Joram his son unto king David, to salute him, and to bless him, because he had fought against Hadadezer, and smitten him: for Hadadezer had wars with Toi. And
Joram brought with him vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and vessels of brass:

translated_text: Which also king David did dedicate unto the LORD, with the silver and gold that he had dedicated of all nations which he subdued;
original_text: Which also king David did dedicate unto the LORD, with the silver and gold that he had dedicated of all nations which he subdued;

translated_text: Of Syria, and of Moab, and of the children of Ammon, and of the Philistines, and of Amalek, and of the spoil of Hadadezer, son of Rehob, king of Zobah.
original_text: Of Syria, and of Moab, and of the children of Ammon, and of the Philistines, and of Amalek, and of the spoil of Hadadezer, son of Rehob, king of Zobah.

translated_text:
And David gat
him a name when he returned from smiting of the Syrians in the valley of salt,
being eighteen thousand
men.
original_text:
And David gat
him a name when he returned from smiting of the Syrians in the valley of salt,
being eighteen thousand
men.

translated_text: And he put garrisons in Edom; throughout all Edom put he garrisons, and all they of Edom became David’s servants. And the LORD preserved David whithersoever he went.
original_text: And he put garrisons in Edom; throughout all Edom put he garrisons, and all they of Edom became David’s servants. And the LORD preserved David whithersoever he went.

translated_text: And David reigned over all Israel; and David executed judgment and justice unto all his people.
original_text: And David reigned over all Israel; and David executed judgment and justice unto all his people.

translated_text:
And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada
was over both the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and David’s sons were chief rulers.
original_text:
And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada
was over both the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and David’s sons were chief rulers.

translated_text:
And David numbered the people that
were with him, and set captains of thousands and captains of hundreds over them.
original_text:
And David numbered the people that
were with him, and set captains of thousands and captains of hundreds over them.

translated_text: And David sent forth a third part of the people under the hand of Joab, and a third part under the hand of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, Joab’s brother, and a third part under the hand of Ittai the Gittite. And the king said unto the people, I will surely go forth with you myself also.
original_text: And David sent forth a third part of the people under the hand of Joab, and a third part under the hand of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, Joab’s brother, and a third part under the hand of Ittai the Gittite. And the king said unto the people, I will surely go forth with you myself also.

translated_text:
But the people answered, Thou shalt not go forth: for if we flee away, they will not care for us; neither if half of us die, will they care for us: but now
thou art worth ten thousand of us: therefore now
it is
 better that thou succour us out of the city.
original_text:
But the people answered, Thou shalt not go forth: for if we flee away, they will not care for us; neither if half of us die, will they care for us: but now
thou art worth ten thousand of us: therefore now
it is
 better that thou succour us out of the city.

translated_text: And the king said unto them, What seemeth you best I will do. And the king stood by the gate side, and all the people came out by hundreds and by thousands.
original_text: And the king said unto them, What seemeth you best I will do. And the king stood by the gate side, and all the people came out by hundreds and by thousands.

translated_text:
And the king commanded Joab and Abishai and Ittai, saying,
Deal
 gently for my sake with the young man,
even with Absalom. And all the people heard when the king gave all the captains charge concerning Absalom.
original_text:
And the king commanded Joab and Abishai and Ittai, saying,
Deal
 gently for my sake with the young man,
even with Absalom. And all the people heard when the king gave all the captains charge concerning Absalom.

translated_text: So the people went out into the field against Israel: and the battle was in the wood of Ephraim;
original_text: So the people went out into the field against Israel: and the battle was in the wood of Ephraim;

translated_text:
Where the people of Israel were slain before the servants of David, and there was there a great slaughter that day of twenty thousand
men.
original_text:
Where the people of Israel were slain before the servants of David, and there was there a great slaughter that day of twenty thousand
men.

translated_text: For the battle was there scattered over the face of all the country: and the wood devoured more people that day than the sword devoured.
original_text: For the battle was there scattered over the face of all the country: and the wood devoured more people that day than the sword devoured.

translated_text:
And Absalom met the servants of David. And Absalom rode upon a mule, and the mule went under the thick boughs of a great oak, and his head caught hold of the oak, and he was taken up between the heaven and the earth; and the mule that
was under him went away.
original_text:
And Absalom met the servants of David. And Absalom rode upon a mule, and the mule went under the thick boughs of a great oak, and his head caught hold of the oak, and he was taken up between the heaven and the earth; and the mule that
was under him went away.

translated_text: And a certain man saw it, and told Joab, and said, Behold, I saw Absalom hanged in an oak.
original_text: And a certain man saw it, and told Joab, and said, Behold, I saw Absalom hanged in an oak.

translated_text:
And Joab said unto the man that told him, And, behold, thou sawest
him, and why didst thou not smite him there to the ground? and I would have given thee ten
shekels of silver, and a girdle.
original_text:
And Joab said unto the man that told him, And, behold, thou sawest
him, and why didst thou not smite him there to the ground? and I would have given thee ten
shekels of silver, and a girdle.

translated_text:
And the man said unto Joab, Though I should receive a thousand
shekels of silver in mine hand, yet would I not put forth mine hand against the king’s son: for in our hearing the king charged thee and Abishai and Ittai, saying, Beware that none
touch the young man Absalom.
original_text:
And the man said unto Joab, Though I should receive a thousand
shekels of silver in mine hand, yet would I not put forth mine hand against the king’s son: for in our hearing the king charged thee and Abishai and Ittai, saying, Beware that none
touch the young man Absalom.

translated_text:
Otherwise I should have wrought falsehood against mine own life: for there is no matter hid from the king, and thou thyself wouldest have set thyself against
me.
original_text:
Otherwise I should have wrought falsehood against mine own life: for there is no matter hid from the king, and thou thyself wouldest have set thyself against
me.

translated_text:
Then said Joab, I may not tarry thus with thee. And he took three darts in his hand, and thrust them through the heart of Absalom, while he
was yet alive in the midst of the oak.
original_text:
Then said Joab, I may not tarry thus with thee. And he took three darts in his hand, and thrust them through the heart of Absalom, while he
was yet alive in the midst of the oak.

translated_text: And ten young men that bare Joab’s armour compassed about and smote Absalom, and slew him.
original_text: And ten young men that bare Joab’s armour compassed about and smote Absalom, and slew him.

translated_text: And Joab blew the trumpet, and the people returned from pursuing after Israel: for Joab held back the people.
original_text: And Joab blew the trumpet, and the people returned from pursuing after Israel: for Joab held back the people.

translated_text: And they took Absalom, and cast him into a great pit in the wood, and laid a very great heap of stones upon him: and all Israel fled every one to his tent.
original_text: And they took Absalom, and cast him into a great pit in the wood, and laid a very great heap of stones upon him: and all Israel fled every one to his tent.

translated_text:
Now Absalom in his lifetime had taken and reared up for himself a pillar, which
is in the king’s dale: for he said, I have no son to keep my name in remembrance: and he called the pillar after his own name: and it is called unto this day, Absalom’s place.
original_text:
Now Absalom in his lifetime had taken and reared up for himself a pillar, which
is in the king’s dale: for he said, I have no son to keep my name in remembrance: and he called the pillar after his own name: and it is called unto this day, Absalom’s place.

translated_text: Then said Ahimaaz the son of Zadok, Let me now run, and bear the king tidings, how that the LORD hath avenged him of his enemies.
original_text: Then said Ahimaaz the son of Zadok, Let me now run, and bear the king tidings, how that the LORD hath avenged him of his enemies.

translated_text: And Joab said unto him, Thou shalt not bear tidings this day, but thou shalt bear tidings another day: but this day thou shalt bear no tidings, because the king’s son is dead.
original_text: And Joab said unto him, Thou shalt not bear tidings this day, but thou shalt bear tidings another day: but this day thou shalt bear no tidings, because the king’s son is dead.

translated_text: Then said Joab to Cushi, Go tell the king what thou hast seen. And Cushi bowed himself unto Joab, and ran.
original_text: Then said Joab to Cushi, Go tell the king what thou hast seen. And Cushi bowed himself unto Joab, and ran.

translated_text: Then said Ahimaaz the son of Zadok yet again to Joab, But howsoever, let me, I pray thee, also run after Cushi. And Joab said, Wherefore wilt thou run, my son, seeing that thou hast no tidings ready?
original_text: Then said Ahimaaz the son of Zadok yet again to Joab, But howsoever, let me, I pray thee, also run after Cushi. And Joab said, Wherefore wilt thou run, my son, seeing that thou hast no tidings ready?

translated_text:
But howsoever,
said he, let me run. And he said unto him, Run. Then Ahimaaz ran by the way of the plain, and overran Cushi.
original_text:
But howsoever,
said he, let me run. And he said unto him, Run. Then Ahimaaz ran by the way of the plain, and overran Cushi.

translated_text: And David sat between the two gates: and the watchman went up to the roof over the gate unto the wall, and lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold a man running alone.
original_text: And David sat between the two gates: and the watchman went up to the roof over the gate unto the wall, and lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold a man running alone.

translated_text:
And the watchman cried, and told the king. And the king said, If he
be alone,
there is tidings in his mouth. And he came apace, and drew near.
original_text:
And the watchman cried, and told the king. And the king said, If he
be alone,
there is tidings in his mouth. And he came apace, and drew near.

translated_text:
And the watchman saw another man running: and the watchman called unto the porter, and said, Behold
another man running alone. And the king said, He also bringeth tidings.
original_text:
And the watchman saw another man running: and the watchman called unto the porter, and said, Behold
another man running alone. And the king said, He also bringeth tidings.

translated_text:
And the watchman said, Me thinketh the running of the foremost is like the running of Ahimaaz the son of Zadok. And the king said, He
is
 a good man, and cometh with good tidings.
original_text:
And the watchman said, Me thinketh the running of the foremost is like the running of Ahimaaz the son of Zadok. And the king said, He
is
 a good man, and cometh with good tidings.

translated_text:
And Ahimaaz called, and said unto the king, All is well. And he fell down to the earth upon his face before the king, and said, Blessed
be
 the LORD thy God, which hath delivered up the men that lifted up their hand against my lord the king.
original_text:
And Ahimaaz called, and said unto the king, All is well. And he fell down to the earth upon his face before the king, and said, Blessed
be
 the LORD thy God, which hath delivered up the men that lifted up their hand against my lord the king.

translated_text:
And the king said, Is the young man Absalom safe? And Ahimaaz answered, When Joab sent the king’s servant, and
me thy servant, I saw a great tumult, but I knew not what
it was.
original_text:
And the king said, Is the young man Absalom safe? And Ahimaaz answered, When Joab sent the king’s servant, and
me thy servant, I saw a great tumult, but I knew not what
it was.

translated_text:
And the king said
unto him, Turn aside,
and stand here. And he turned aside, and stood still.
original_text:
And the king said
unto him, Turn aside,
and stand here. And he turned aside, and stood still.

translated_text: And, behold, Cushi came; and Cushi said, Tidings, my lord the king: for the LORD hath avenged thee this day of all them that rose up against thee.
original_text: And, behold, Cushi came; and Cushi said, Tidings, my lord the king: for the LORD hath avenged thee this day of all them that rose up against thee.

translated_text:
And the king said unto Cushi, Is the young man Absalom safe? And Cushi answered, The enemies of my lord the king, and all that rise against thee to do
thee hurt, be as
that young man
is.
original_text:
And the king said unto Cushi, Is the young man Absalom safe? And Cushi answered, The enemies of my lord the king, and all that rise against thee to do
thee hurt, be as
that young man
is.

translated_text: And the king was much moved, and went up to the chamber over the gate, and wept: and as he went, thus he said, O my son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! would God I had died for thee, O Absalom, my son, my son!
original_text: And the king was much moved, and went up to the chamber over the gate, and wept: and as he went, thus he said, O my son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! would God I had died for thee, O Absalom, my son, my son!

translated_text: Moreover Ahithophel said unto Absalom, Let me now choose out twelve thousand men, and I will arise and pursue after David this night:
original_text: Moreover Ahithophel said unto Absalom, Let me now choose out twelve thousand men, and I will arise and pursue after David this night:

translated_text:
And I will come upon him while he
is weary and weak handed, and will make him afraid: and all the people that
are with him shall flee; and I will smite the king only:
original_text:
And I will come upon him while he
is weary and weak handed, and will make him afraid: and all the people that
are with him shall flee; and I will smite the king only:

translated_text:
And I will bring back all the people unto thee: the man whom thou seekest
is as if all returned:
so all the people shall be in peace.
original_text:
And I will bring back all the people unto thee: the man whom thou seekest
is as if all returned:
so all the people shall be in peace.

translated_text: And the saying pleased Absalom well, and all the elders of Israel.
original_text: And the saying pleased Absalom well, and all the elders of Israel.

translated_text: Then said Absalom, Call now Hushai the Archite also, and let us hear likewise what he saith.
original_text: Then said Absalom, Call now Hushai the Archite also, and let us hear likewise what he saith.

translated_text:
And when Hushai was come to Absalom, Absalom spake unto him, saying, Ahithophel hath spoken after this manner: shall we do
after his saying? if not; speak thou.
original_text:
And when Hushai was come to Absalom, Absalom spake unto him, saying, Ahithophel hath spoken after this manner: shall we do
after his saying? if not; speak thou.

translated_text:
And Hushai said unto Absalom, The counsel that Ahithophel hath given
is not good at this time.
original_text:
And Hushai said unto Absalom, The counsel that Ahithophel hath given
is not good at this time.

translated_text:
For, said Hushai, thou knowest thy father and his men, that they
be mighty men, and they
be chafed in their minds, as a bear robbed of her whelps in the field: and thy father
is a man of war, and will not lodge with the people.
original_text:
For, said Hushai, thou knowest thy father and his men, that they
be mighty men, and they
be chafed in their minds, as a bear robbed of her whelps in the field: and thy father
is a man of war, and will not lodge with the people.

translated_text:
Behold, he is hid now in some pit, or in some
other place: and it will come to pass, when some of them be overthrown at the first, that whosoever heareth it will say, There is a slaughter among the people that follow Absalom.
original_text:
Behold, he is hid now in some pit, or in some
other place: and it will come to pass, when some of them be overthrown at the first, that whosoever heareth it will say, There is a slaughter among the people that follow Absalom.

translated_text:
And he also
that is valiant, whose heart
is as the heart of a lion, shall utterly melt: for all Israel knoweth that thy father
is a mighty man, and
they which
be with him
are valiant men.
original_text:
And he also
that is valiant, whose heart
is as the heart of a lion, shall utterly melt: for all Israel knoweth that thy father
is a mighty man, and
they which
be with him
are valiant men.

translated_text:
Therefore I counsel that all Israel be generally gathered unto thee, from Dan even to Beer-sheba, as the sand that
is by the sea for multitude; and that thou go to battle in thine own person.
original_text:
Therefore I counsel that all Israel be generally gathered unto thee, from Dan even to Beer-sheba, as the sand that
is by the sea for multitude; and that thou go to battle in thine own person.

translated_text:
So shall we come upon him in some place where he shall be found, and we will light upon him as the dew falleth on the ground: and of him and of all the men that
are with him there shall not be left so much as one.
original_text:
So shall we come upon him in some place where he shall be found, and we will light upon him as the dew falleth on the ground: and of him and of all the men that
are with him there shall not be left so much as one.

translated_text: Moreover, if he be gotten into a city, then shall all Israel bring ropes to that city, and we will draw it into the river, until there be not one small stone found there.
original_text: Moreover, if he be gotten into a city, then shall all Israel bring ropes to that city, and we will draw it into the river, until there be not one small stone found there.

translated_text:
And Absalom and all the men of Israel said, The counsel of Hushai the Archite
is better than the counsel of Ahithophel. For the LORD had appointed to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, to the intent that the LORD might bring evil upon Absalom.
original_text:
And Absalom and all the men of Israel said, The counsel of Hushai the Archite
is better than the counsel of Ahithophel. For the LORD had appointed to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, to the intent that the LORD might bring evil upon Absalom.

translated_text: Then said Hushai unto Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, Thus and thus did Ahithophel counsel Absalom and the elders of Israel; and thus and thus have I counselled.
original_text: Then said Hushai unto Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, Thus and thus did Ahithophel counsel Absalom and the elders of Israel; and thus and thus have I counselled.

translated_text:
Now therefore send quickly, and tell David, saying, Lodge not this night in the plains of the wilderness, but speedily pass over; lest the king be swallowed up, and all the people that
are with him.
original_text:
Now therefore send quickly, and tell David, saying, Lodge not this night in the plains of the wilderness, but speedily pass over; lest the king be swallowed up, and all the people that
are with him.

translated_text: Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz stayed by En-rogel; for they might not be seen to come into the city: and a wench went and told them; and they went and told king David.
original_text: Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz stayed by En-rogel; for they might not be seen to come into the city: and a wench went and told them; and they went and told king David.

translated_text: Nevertheless a lad saw them, and told Absalom: but they went both of them away quickly, and came to a man’s house in Bahurim, which had a well in his court; whither they went down.
original_text: Nevertheless a lad saw them, and told Absalom: but they went both of them away quickly, and came to a man’s house in Bahurim, which had a well in his court; whither they went down.

translated_text: And the woman took and spread a covering over the well’s mouth, and spread ground corn thereon; and the thing was not known.
original_text: And the woman took and spread a covering over the well’s mouth, and spread ground corn thereon; and the thing was not known.

translated_text:
And when Absalom’s servants came to the woman to the house, they said, Where is Ahimaaz and Jonathan? And the woman said unto them, They be gone over the brook of water. And when they had sought and could not find
them,
 they returned to Jerusalem.
original_text:
And when Absalom’s servants came to the woman to the house, they said, Where is Ahimaaz and Jonathan? And the woman said unto them, They be gone over the brook of water. And when they had sought and could not find
them,
 they returned to Jerusalem.

translated_text: And it came to pass, after they were departed, that they came up out of the well, and went and told king David, and said unto David, Arise, and pass quickly over the water: for thus hath Ahithophel counselled against you.
original_text: And it came to pass, after they were departed, that they came up out of the well, and went and told king David, and said unto David, Arise, and pass quickly over the water: for thus hath Ahithophel counselled against you.

translated_text:
Then David arose, and all the people that
were with him, and they passed over Jordan: by the morning light there lacked not one of them that was not gone over Jordan.
original_text:
Then David arose, and all the people that
were with him, and they passed over Jordan: by the morning light there lacked not one of them that was not gone over Jordan.

translated_text:
And when Ahithophel saw that his counsel was not followed, he saddled
his ass, and arose, and gat him home to his house, to his city, and put his household in order, and hanged himself, and died, and was buried in the sepulchre of his father.
original_text:
And when Ahithophel saw that his counsel was not followed, he saddled
his ass, and arose, and gat him home to his house, to his city, and put his household in order, and hanged himself, and died, and was buried in the sepulchre of his father.

translated_text: Then David came to Mahanaim. And Absalom passed over Jordan, he and all the men of Israel with him.
original_text: Then David came to Mahanaim. And Absalom passed over Jordan, he and all the men of Israel with him.

translated_text:
And Absalom made Amasa captain of the host instead of Joab: which Amasa was a man’s son, whose name
was Ithra an Israelite, that went in to Abigail the daughter of Nahash, sister to Zeruiah Joab’s mother.
original_text:
And Absalom made Amasa captain of the host instead of Joab: which Amasa was a man’s son, whose name
was Ithra an Israelite, that went in to Abigail the daughter of Nahash, sister to Zeruiah Joab’s mother.

translated_text: So Israel and Absalom pitched in the land of Gilead.
original_text: So Israel and Absalom pitched in the land of Gilead.

translated_text: And it came to pass, when David was come to Mahanaim, that Shobi the son of Nahash of Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and Machir the son of Ammiel of Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite of Rogelim,
original_text: And it came to pass, when David was come to Mahanaim, that Shobi the son of Nahash of Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and Machir the son of Ammiel of Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite of Rogelim,

translated_text:
Brought beds, and basons, and earthen vessels, and wheat, and barley, and flour, and parched
corn, and beans, and lentiles, and parched
pulse,
original_text:
Brought beds, and basons, and earthen vessels, and wheat, and barley, and flour, and parched
corn, and beans, and lentiles, and parched
pulse,

translated_text:
And honey, and butter, and sheep, and cheese of kine, for David, and for the people that
were with him, to eat: for they said, The people
is hungry, and weary, and thirsty, in the wilderness.
original_text:
And honey, and butter, and sheep, and cheese of kine, for David, and for the people that
were with him, to eat: for they said, The people
is hungry, and weary, and thirsty, in the wilderness.

translated_text:
And when David was a little past the top
of the hill, behold, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth met him, with a couple of asses saddled, and upon them two hundred
loaves of bread, and an hundred bunches of raisins, and an hundred of summer fruits, and a bottle of wine.
original_text:
And when David was a little past the top
of the hill, behold, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth met him, with a couple of asses saddled, and upon them two hundred
loaves of bread, and an hundred bunches of raisins, and an hundred of summer fruits, and a bottle of wine.

translated_text:
And the king said unto Ziba, What meanest thou by these? And Ziba said, The asses
be for the king’s household to ride on; and the bread and summer fruit for the young men to eat; and the wine, that such as be faint in the wilderness may drink.
original_text:
And the king said unto Ziba, What meanest thou by these? And Ziba said, The asses
be for the king’s household to ride on; and the bread and summer fruit for the young men to eat; and the wine, that such as be faint in the wilderness may drink.

translated_text:
And the king said, And where
is thy master’s son? And Ziba said unto the king, Behold, he abideth at Jerusalem: for he said, Today shall the house of Israel restore me the kingdom of my father.
original_text:
And the king said, And where
is thy master’s son? And Ziba said unto the king, Behold, he abideth at Jerusalem: for he said, Today shall the house of Israel restore me the kingdom of my father.

translated_text:
Then said the king to Ziba, Behold, thine
are all that
pertained unto Mephibosheth. And Ziba said, I humbly beseech thee
that I may find grace in thy sight, my lord, O king.
original_text:
Then said the king to Ziba, Behold, thine
are all that
pertained unto Mephibosheth. And Ziba said, I humbly beseech thee
that I may find grace in thy sight, my lord, O king.

translated_text:
And when king David came to Bahurim, behold, thence came out a man of the family of the house of Saul, whose name
was Shimei, the son of Gera: he came forth, and cursed still as he came.
original_text:
And when king David came to Bahurim, behold, thence came out a man of the family of the house of Saul, whose name
was Shimei, the son of Gera: he came forth, and cursed still as he came.

translated_text:
And he cast stones at David, and at all the servants of king David: and all the people and all the mighty men
were on his right hand and on his left.
original_text:
And he cast stones at David, and at all the servants of king David: and all the people and all the mighty men
were on his right hand and on his left.

translated_text: And thus said Shimei when he cursed, Come out, come out, thou bloody man, and thou man of Belial:
original_text: And thus said Shimei when he cursed, Come out, come out, thou bloody man, and thou man of Belial:

translated_text:
The LORD hath returned upon thee all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose stead thou hast reigned; and the LORD hath delivered the kingdom into the hand of Absalom thy son: and, behold, thou
art taken in thy mischief, because thou
art a bloody man.
original_text:
The LORD hath returned upon thee all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose stead thou hast reigned; and the LORD hath delivered the kingdom into the hand of Absalom thy son: and, behold, thou
art taken in thy mischief, because thou
art a bloody man.

translated_text: Then said Abishai the son of Zeruiah unto the king, Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? let me go over, I pray thee, and take off his head.
original_text: Then said Abishai the son of Zeruiah unto the king, Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? let me go over, I pray thee, and take off his head.

translated_text: And the king said, What have I to do with you, ye sons of Zeruiah? so let him curse, because the LORD hath said unto him, Curse David. Who shall then say, Wherefore hast thou done so?
original_text: And the king said, What have I to do with you, ye sons of Zeruiah? so let him curse, because the LORD hath said unto him, Curse David. Who shall then say, Wherefore hast thou done so?

translated_text:
And David said to Abishai, and to all his servants, Behold, my son, which came forth of my bowels, seeketh my life: how much more now
may this Benjamite
do it? let him alone, and let him curse; for the LORD hath bidden him.
original_text:
And David said to Abishai, and to all his servants, Behold, my son, which came forth of my bowels, seeketh my life: how much more now
may this Benjamite
do it? let him alone, and let him curse; for the LORD hath bidden him.

translated_text: It may be that the LORD will look on mine affliction, and that the LORD will requite me good for his cursing this day.
original_text: It may be that the LORD will look on mine affliction, and that the LORD will requite me good for his cursing this day.

translated_text: And as David and his men went by the way, Shimei went along on the hill’s side over against him, and cursed as he went, and threw stones at him, and cast dust.
original_text: And as David and his men went by the way, Shimei went along on the hill’s side over against him, and cursed as he went, and threw stones at him, and cast dust.

translated_text:
And the king, and all the people that
were with him, came weary, and refreshed themselves there.
original_text:
And the king, and all the people that
were with him, came weary, and refreshed themselves there.

translated_text: And Absalom, and all the people the men of Israel, came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel with him.
original_text: And Absalom, and all the people the men of Israel, came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel with him.

translated_text: And it came to pass, when Hushai the Archite, David’s friend, was come unto Absalom, that Hushai said unto Absalom, God save the king, God save the king.
original_text: And it came to pass, when Hushai the Archite, David’s friend, was come unto Absalom, that Hushai said unto Absalom, God save the king, God save the king.

translated_text:
And Absalom said to Hushai,
Is this thy kindness to thy friend? why wentest thou not with thy friend?
original_text:
And Absalom said to Hushai,
Is this thy kindness to thy friend? why wentest thou not with thy friend?

translated_text: And Hushai said unto Absalom, Nay; but whom the LORD, and this people, and all the men of Israel, choose, his will I be, and with him will I abide.
original_text: And Hushai said unto Absalom, Nay; but whom the LORD, and this people, and all the men of Israel, choose, his will I be, and with him will I abide.

translated_text:
And again, whom should I serve?
should I not
serve
 in the presence of his son? as I have served in thy father’s presence, so will I be in thy presence.
original_text:
And again, whom should I serve?
should I not
serve
 in the presence of his son? as I have served in thy father’s presence, so will I be in thy presence.

translated_text: Then said Absalom to Ahithophel, Give counsel among you what we shall do.
original_text: Then said Absalom to Ahithophel, Give counsel among you what we shall do.

translated_text:
And Ahithophel said unto Absalom, Go in unto thy father’s concubines, which he hath left to keep the house; and all Israel shall hear that thou art abhorred of thy father: then shall the hands of all that
are with thee be strong.
original_text:
And Ahithophel said unto Absalom, Go in unto thy father’s concubines, which he hath left to keep the house; and all Israel shall hear that thou art abhorred of thy father: then shall the hands of all that
are with thee be strong.

translated_text: So they spread Absalom a tent upon the top of the house; and Absalom went in unto his father’s concubines in the sight of all Israel.
original_text: So they spread Absalom a tent upon the top of the house; and Absalom went in unto his father’s concubines in the sight of all Israel.

translated_text:
And the counsel of Ahithophel, which he counselled in those days,
was as if a man had enquired at the oracle of God: so
was
 all the counsel of Ahithophel both with David and with Absalom.
original_text:
And the counsel of Ahithophel, which he counselled in those days,
was as if a man had enquired at the oracle of God: so
was
 all the counsel of Ahithophel both with David and with Absalom.

translated_text: And it came to pass after this, that Absalom prepared him chariots and horses, and fifty men to run before him.
original_text: And it came to pass after this, that Absalom prepared him chariots and horses, and fifty men to run before him.

translated_text:
And Absalom rose up early, and stood beside the way of the gate: and it was so, that when any man that had a controversy came to the king for judgment, then Absalom called unto him, and said, Of what city
art
 thou? And he said, Thy servant is of one of the tribes of Israel.
original_text:
And Absalom rose up early, and stood beside the way of the gate: and it was so, that when any man that had a controversy came to the king for judgment, then Absalom called unto him, and said, Of what city
art
 thou? And he said, Thy servant is of one of the tribes of Israel.

translated_text:
And Absalom said unto him, See, thy matters
are good and right; but
there is no man
deputed of the king to hear thee.
original_text:
And Absalom said unto him, See, thy matters
are good and right; but
there is no man
deputed of the king to hear thee.

translated_text: Absalom said moreover, Oh that I were made judge in the land, that every man which hath any suit or cause might come unto me, and I would do him justice!
original_text: Absalom said moreover, Oh that I were made judge in the land, that every man which hath any suit or cause might come unto me, and I would do him justice!

translated_text:
And it was
so, that when any man came nigh
to him
 to do him obeisance, he put forth his hand, and took him, and kissed him.
original_text:
And it was
so, that when any man came nigh
to him
 to do him obeisance, he put forth his hand, and took him, and kissed him.

translated_text: And on this manner did Absalom to all Israel that came to the king for judgment: so Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.
original_text: And on this manner did Absalom to all Israel that came to the king for judgment: so Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.

translated_text: And it came to pass after forty years, that Absalom said unto the king, I pray thee, let me go and pay my vow, which I have vowed unto the LORD, in Hebron.
original_text: And it came to pass after forty years, that Absalom said unto the king, I pray thee, let me go and pay my vow, which I have vowed unto the LORD, in Hebron.

translated_text: For thy servant vowed a vow while I abode at Geshur in Syria, saying, If the LORD shall bring me again indeed to Jerusalem, then I will serve the LORD.
original_text: For thy servant vowed a vow while I abode at Geshur in Syria, saying, If the LORD shall bring me again indeed to Jerusalem, then I will serve the LORD.

translated_text: And the king said unto him, Go in peace. So he arose, and went to Hebron.
original_text: And the king said unto him, Go in peace. So he arose, and went to Hebron.

translated_text: But Absalom sent spies throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, As soon as ye hear the sound of the trumpet, then ye shall say, Absalom reigneth in Hebron.
original_text: But Absalom sent spies throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, As soon as ye hear the sound of the trumpet, then ye shall say, Absalom reigneth in Hebron.

translated_text:
And with Absalom went two hundred men out of Jerusalem,
that were
 called; and they went in their simplicity, and they knew not any thing.
original_text:
And with Absalom went two hundred men out of Jerusalem,
that were
 called; and they went in their simplicity, and they knew not any thing.

translated_text:
And Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David’s counsellor, from his city,
even from Giloh, while he offered sacrifices. And the conspiracy was strong; for the people increased continually with Absalom.
original_text:
And Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David’s counsellor, from his city,
even from Giloh, while he offered sacrifices. And the conspiracy was strong; for the people increased continually with Absalom.

translated_text: And there came a messenger to David, saying, The hearts of the men of Israel are after Absalom.
original_text: And there came a messenger to David, saying, The hearts of the men of Israel are after Absalom.

translated_text:
And David said unto all his servants that
were with him at Jerusalem, Arise, and let us flee; for we shall not
else escape from Absalom: make speed to depart, lest he overtake us suddenly, and bring evil upon us, and smite the city with the edge of the sword.
original_text:
And David said unto all his servants that
were with him at Jerusalem, Arise, and let us flee; for we shall not
else escape from Absalom: make speed to depart, lest he overtake us suddenly, and bring evil upon us, and smite the city with the edge of the sword.

translated_text:
And the king’s servants said unto the king, Behold, thy servants
are ready to do whatsoever my lord the king shall appoint.
original_text:
And the king’s servants said unto the king, Behold, thy servants
are ready to do whatsoever my lord the king shall appoint.

translated_text:
And the king went forth, and all his household after him. And the king left ten women,
which were concubines, to keep the house.
original_text:
And the king went forth, and all his household after him. And the king left ten women,
which were concubines, to keep the house.

translated_text: And the king went forth, and all the people after him, and tarried in a place that was far off.
original_text: And the king went forth, and all the people after him, and tarried in a place that was far off.

translated_text: And all his servants passed on beside him; and all the Cherethites, and all the Pelethites, and all the Gittites, six hundred men which came after him from Gath, passed on before the king.
original_text: And all his servants passed on beside him; and all the Cherethites, and all the Pelethites, and all the Gittites, six hundred men which came after him from Gath, passed on before the king.

translated_text:
Then said the king to Ittai the Gittite, Wherefore goest thou also with us? return to thy place, and abide with the king: for thou
art
 a stranger, and also an exile.
original_text:
Then said the king to Ittai the Gittite, Wherefore goest thou also with us? return to thy place, and abide with the king: for thou
art
 a stranger, and also an exile.

translated_text:
Whereas thou camest
but yesterday, should I this day make thee go up and down with us? seeing I go whither I may, return thou, and take back thy brethren: mercy and truth
be with thee.
original_text:
Whereas thou camest
but yesterday, should I this day make thee go up and down with us? seeing I go whither I may, return thou, and take back thy brethren: mercy and truth
be with thee.

translated_text:
And Ittai answered the king, and said,
As the LORD liveth, and
as my lord the king liveth, surely in what place my lord the king shall be, whether in death or life, even there also will thy servant be.
original_text:
And Ittai answered the king, and said,
As the LORD liveth, and
as my lord the king liveth, surely in what place my lord the king shall be, whether in death or life, even there also will thy servant be.

translated_text:
And David said to Ittai, Go and pass over. And Ittai the Gittite passed over, and all his men, and all the little ones that
were with him.
original_text:
And David said to Ittai, Go and pass over. And Ittai the Gittite passed over, and all his men, and all the little ones that
were with him.

translated_text: And all the country wept with a loud voice, and all the people passed over: the king also himself passed over the brook Kidron, and all the people passed over, toward the way of the wilderness.
original_text: And all the country wept with a loud voice, and all the people passed over: the king also himself passed over the brook Kidron, and all the people passed over, toward the way of the wilderness.

translated_text:
And lo Zadok also, and all the Levites
were with him, bearing the ark of the covenant of God: and they set down the ark of God; and Abiathar went up, until all the people had done passing out of the city.
original_text:
And lo Zadok also, and all the Levites
were with him, bearing the ark of the covenant of God: and they set down the ark of God; and Abiathar went up, until all the people had done passing out of the city.

translated_text:
And the king said unto Zadok, Carry back the ark of God into the city: if I shall find favour in the eyes of the LORD, he will bring me again, and shew me
both it, and his habitation:
original_text:
And the king said unto Zadok, Carry back the ark of God into the city: if I shall find favour in the eyes of the LORD, he will bring me again, and shew me
both it, and his habitation:

translated_text:
But if he thus say, I have no delight in thee; behold,
here am
 I, let him do to me as seemeth good unto him.
original_text:
But if he thus say, I have no delight in thee; behold,
here am
 I, let him do to me as seemeth good unto him.

translated_text:
The king said also unto Zadok the priest,
Art not thou a seer? return into the city in peace, and your two sons with you, Ahimaaz thy son, and Jonathan the son of Abiathar.
original_text:
The king said also unto Zadok the priest,
Art not thou a seer? return into the city in peace, and your two sons with you, Ahimaaz thy son, and Jonathan the son of Abiathar.

translated_text: See, I will tarry in the plain of the wilderness, until there come word from you to certify me.
original_text: See, I will tarry in the plain of the wilderness, until there come word from you to certify me.

translated_text: Zadok therefore and Abiathar carried the ark of God again to Jerusalem: and they tarried there.
original_text: Zadok therefore and Abiathar carried the ark of God again to Jerusalem: and they tarried there.

translated_text:
And David went up by the ascent of
mount Olivet, and wept as he went up, and had his head covered, and he went barefoot: and all the people that
was with him covered every man his head, and they went up, weeping as they went up.
original_text:
And David went up by the ascent of
mount Olivet, and wept as he went up, and had his head covered, and he went barefoot: and all the people that
was with him covered every man his head, and they went up, weeping as they went up.

translated_text:
And
one told David, saying, Ahithophel
is among the conspirators with Absalom. And David said, O LORD, I pray thee, turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness.
original_text:
And
one told David, saying, Ahithophel
is among the conspirators with Absalom. And David said, O LORD, I pray thee, turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness.

translated_text:
And it came to pass, that
when David was come to the top
of the mount, where he worshipped God, behold, Hushai the Archite came to meet him with his coat rent, and earth upon his head:
original_text:
And it came to pass, that
when David was come to the top
of the mount, where he worshipped God, behold, Hushai the Archite came to meet him with his coat rent, and earth upon his head:

translated_text: Unto whom David said, If thou passest on with me, then thou shalt be a burden unto me:
original_text: Unto whom David said, If thou passest on with me, then thou shalt be a burden unto me:

translated_text:
But if thou return to the city, and say unto Absalom, I will be thy servant, O king;
as I
have been thy father’s servant hitherto, so
will I now also
be thy servant: then mayest thou for me defeat the counsel of Ahithophel.
original_text:
But if thou return to the city, and say unto Absalom, I will be thy servant, O king;
as I
have been thy father’s servant hitherto, so
will I now also
be thy servant: then mayest thou for me defeat the counsel of Ahithophel.

translated_text:
And
hast thou not there with thee Zadok and Abiathar the priests? therefore it shall be,
that what thing soever thou shalt hear out of the king’s house, thou shalt tell
it to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.
original_text:
And
hast thou not there with thee Zadok and Abiathar the priests? therefore it shall be,
that what thing soever thou shalt hear out of the king’s house, thou shalt tell
it to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.

translated_text:
Behold,
they have there with them their two sons, Ahimaaz Zadok’s
son, and Jonathan Abiathar’s
son; and by them ye shall send unto me every thing that ye can hear.
original_text:
Behold,
they have there with them their two sons, Ahimaaz Zadok’s
son, and Jonathan Abiathar’s
son; and by them ye shall send unto me every thing that ye can hear.

translated_text: So Hushai David’s friend came into the city, and Absalom came into Jerusalem.
original_text: So Hushai David’s friend came into the city, and Absalom came into Jerusalem.

translated_text:
Now Joab the son of Zeruiah perceived that the king’s heart
was
 toward Absalom.
original_text:
Now Joab the son of Zeruiah perceived that the king’s heart
was
 toward Absalom.

translated_text: And Joab sent to Tekoah, and fetched thence a wise woman, and said unto her, I pray thee, feign thyself to be a mourner, and put on now mourning apparel, and anoint not thyself with oil, but be as a woman that had a long time mourned for the dead:
original_text: And Joab sent to Tekoah, and fetched thence a wise woman, and said unto her, I pray thee, feign thyself to be a mourner, and put on now mourning apparel, and anoint not thyself with oil, but be as a woman that had a long time mourned for the dead:

translated_text: And come to the king, and speak on this manner unto him. So Joab put the words in her mouth.
original_text: And come to the king, and speak on this manner unto him. So Joab put the words in her mouth.

translated_text: And when the woman of Tekoah spake to the king, she fell on her face to the ground, and did obeisance, and said, Help, O king.
original_text: And when the woman of Tekoah spake to the king, she fell on her face to the ground, and did obeisance, and said, Help, O king.

translated_text:
And the king said unto her, What aileth thee? And she answered, I
am indeed a widow woman, and mine husband is dead.
original_text:
And the king said unto her, What aileth thee? And she answered, I
am indeed a widow woman, and mine husband is dead.

translated_text:
And thy handmaid had two sons, and they two strove together in the field, and
there was none to part them, but the one smote the other, and slew him.
original_text:
And thy handmaid had two sons, and they two strove together in the field, and
there was none to part them, but the one smote the other, and slew him.

translated_text:
