And, behold, the whole family is risen against thine handmaid, and they said, Deliver him that smote his brother, that we may kill him, for the life of his brother whom he slew; and we will destroy the heir also: and so they shall quench my coal which is left, and shall not leave to my husband
neither name nor remainder upon the earth.
original_text:
And, behold, the whole family is risen against thine handmaid, and they said, Deliver him that smote his brother, that we may kill him, for the life of his brother whom he slew; and we will destroy the heir also: and so they shall quench my coal which is left, and shall not leave to my husband
neither name nor remainder upon the earth.

translated_text: And the king said unto the woman, Go to thine house, and I will give charge concerning thee.
original_text: And the king said unto the woman, Go to thine house, and I will give charge concerning thee.

translated_text:
And the woman of Tekoah said unto the king, My lord, O king, the iniquity
be on me, and on my father’s house: and the king and his throne
be guiltless.
original_text:
And the woman of Tekoah said unto the king, My lord, O king, the iniquity
be on me, and on my father’s house: and the king and his throne
be guiltless.

translated_text:
And the king said, Whosoever saith
ought unto thee, bring him to me, and he shall not touch thee any more.
original_text:
And the king said, Whosoever saith
ought unto thee, bring him to me, and he shall not touch thee any more.

translated_text: Then said she, I pray thee, let the king remember the LORD thy God, that thou wouldest not suffer the revengers of blood to destroy any more, lest they destroy my son. And he said, As the LORD liveth, there shall not one hair of thy son fall to the earth.
original_text: Then said she, I pray thee, let the king remember the LORD thy God, that thou wouldest not suffer the revengers of blood to destroy any more, lest they destroy my son. And he said, As the LORD liveth, there shall not one hair of thy son fall to the earth.

translated_text:
Then the woman said, Let thine handmaid, I pray thee, speak
one
 word unto my lord the king. And he said, Say on.
original_text:
Then the woman said, Let thine handmaid, I pray thee, speak
one
 word unto my lord the king. And he said, Say on.

translated_text: And the woman said, Wherefore then hast thou thought such a thing against the people of God? for the king doth speak this thing as one which is faulty, in that the king doth not fetch home again his banished.
original_text: And the woman said, Wherefore then hast thou thought such a thing against the people of God? for the king doth speak this thing as one which is faulty, in that the king doth not fetch home again his banished.

translated_text:
For we must needs die, and
are as water spilt on the ground, which cannot be gathered up again; neither doth God respect
any
 person: yet doth he devise means, that his banished be not expelled from him.
original_text:
For we must needs die, and
are as water spilt on the ground, which cannot be gathered up again; neither doth God respect
any
 person: yet doth he devise means, that his banished be not expelled from him.

translated_text:
Now therefore that I am come to speak of this thing unto my lord the king,
it is because the people have made me afraid: and thy handmaid said, I will now speak unto the king; it may be that the king will perform the request of his handmaid.
original_text:
Now therefore that I am come to speak of this thing unto my lord the king,
it is because the people have made me afraid: and thy handmaid said, I will now speak unto the king; it may be that the king will perform the request of his handmaid.

translated_text:
For the king will hear, to deliver his handmaid out of the hand of the man
that would destroy me and my son together out of the inheritance of God.
original_text:
For the king will hear, to deliver his handmaid out of the hand of the man
that would destroy me and my son together out of the inheritance of God.

translated_text:
Then thine handmaid said, The word of my lord the king shall now be comfortable: for as an angel of God, so
is my lord the king to discern good and bad: therefore the LORD thy God will be with thee.
original_text:
Then thine handmaid said, The word of my lord the king shall now be comfortable: for as an angel of God, so
is my lord the king to discern good and bad: therefore the LORD thy God will be with thee.

translated_text: Then the king answered and said unto the woman, Hide not from me, I pray thee, the thing that I shall ask thee. And the woman said, Let my lord the king now speak.
original_text: Then the king answered and said unto the woman, Hide not from me, I pray thee, the thing that I shall ask thee. And the woman said, Let my lord the king now speak.

translated_text:
And the king said,
Is not the hand of Joab with thee in all this? And the woman answered and said,
As thy soul liveth, my lord the king, none can turn to the right hand or to the left from ought that my lord the king hath spoken: for thy servant Joab, he bade me, and he put all these words in the mouth of thine handmaid:
original_text:
And the king said,
Is not the hand of Joab with thee in all this? And the woman answered and said,
As thy soul liveth, my lord the king, none can turn to the right hand or to the left from ought that my lord the king hath spoken: for thy servant Joab, he bade me, and he put all these words in the mouth of thine handmaid:

translated_text:
To fetch about this form of speech hath thy servant Joab done this thing: and my lord
is wise, according to the wisdom of an angel of God, to know all
things that
are in the earth.
original_text:
To fetch about this form of speech hath thy servant Joab done this thing: and my lord
is wise, according to the wisdom of an angel of God, to know all
things that
are in the earth.

translated_text: And the king said unto Joab, Behold now, I have done this thing: go therefore, bring the young man Absalom again.
original_text: And the king said unto Joab, Behold now, I have done this thing: go therefore, bring the young man Absalom again.

translated_text: And Joab fell to the ground on his face, and bowed himself, and thanked the king: and Joab said, Today thy servant knoweth that I have found grace in thy sight, my lord, O king, in that the king hath fulfilled the request of his servant.
original_text: And Joab fell to the ground on his face, and bowed himself, and thanked the king: and Joab said, Today thy servant knoweth that I have found grace in thy sight, my lord, O king, in that the king hath fulfilled the request of his servant.

translated_text: So Joab arose and went to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.
original_text: So Joab arose and went to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.

translated_text: And the king said, Let him turn to his own house, and let him not see my face. So Absalom returned to his own house, and saw not the king’s face.
original_text: And the king said, Let him turn to his own house, and let him not see my face. So Absalom returned to his own house, and saw not the king’s face.

translated_text: But in all Israel there was none to be so much praised as Absalom for his beauty: from the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him.
original_text: But in all Israel there was none to be so much praised as Absalom for his beauty: from the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him.

translated_text:
And when he polled his head, (for it was at every year’s end that he polled
it: because
the hair was heavy on him, therefore he polled it:) he weighed the hair of his head at two hundred shekels after the king’s weight.
original_text:
And when he polled his head, (for it was at every year’s end that he polled
it: because
the hair was heavy on him, therefore he polled it:) he weighed the hair of his head at two hundred shekels after the king’s weight.

translated_text:
And unto Absalom there were born three sons, and one daughter, whose name
was Tamar: she was a woman of a fair countenance.
original_text:
And unto Absalom there were born three sons, and one daughter, whose name
was Tamar: she was a woman of a fair countenance.

translated_text: So Absalom dwelt two full years in Jerusalem, and saw not the king’s face.
original_text: So Absalom dwelt two full years in Jerusalem, and saw not the king’s face.

translated_text: Therefore Absalom sent for Joab, to have sent him to the king; but he would not come to him: and when he sent again the second time, he would not come.
original_text: Therefore Absalom sent for Joab, to have sent him to the king; but he would not come to him: and when he sent again the second time, he would not come.

translated_text: Therefore he said unto his servants, See, Joab’s field is near mine, and he hath barley there; go and set it on fire. And Absalom’s servants set the field on fire.
original_text: Therefore he said unto his servants, See, Joab’s field is near mine, and he hath barley there; go and set it on fire. And Absalom’s servants set the field on fire.

translated_text:
Then Joab arose, and came to Absalom unto
his house, and said unto him, Wherefore have thy servants set my field on fire?
original_text:
Then Joab arose, and came to Absalom unto
his house, and said unto him, Wherefore have thy servants set my field on fire?

translated_text:
And Absalom answered Joab, Behold, I sent unto thee, saying, Come hither, that I may send thee to the king, to say, Wherefore am I come from Geshur?
it had been good for me
to have been there still: now therefore let me see the king’s face; and if there be
any iniquity in me, let him kill me.
original_text:
And Absalom answered Joab, Behold, I sent unto thee, saying, Come hither, that I may send thee to the king, to say, Wherefore am I come from Geshur?
it had been good for me
to have been there still: now therefore let me see the king’s face; and if there be
any iniquity in me, let him kill me.

translated_text: So Joab came to the king, and told him: and when he had called for Absalom, he came to the king, and bowed himself on his face to the ground before the king: and the king kissed Absalom.
original_text: So Joab came to the king, and told him: and when he had called for Absalom, he came to the king, and bowed himself on his face to the ground before the king: and the king kissed Absalom.

translated_text:
And it came to pass after this, that Absalom the son of David had a fair sister, whose name
was Tamar; and Amnon the son of David loved her.
original_text:
And it came to pass after this, that Absalom the son of David had a fair sister, whose name
was Tamar; and Amnon the son of David loved her.

translated_text:
And Amnon was so vexed, that he fell sick for his sister Tamar; for she
was a virgin; and Amnon thought it hard for him to do any thing to her.
original_text:
And Amnon was so vexed, that he fell sick for his sister Tamar; for she
was a virgin; and Amnon thought it hard for him to do any thing to her.

translated_text:
But Amnon had a friend, whose name
was Jonadab, the son of Shimeah David’s brother: and Jonadab
was a very subtil man.
original_text:
But Amnon had a friend, whose name
was Jonadab, the son of Shimeah David’s brother: and Jonadab
was a very subtil man.

translated_text:
And he said unto him, Why
art thou,
being the king’s son, lean from day to day? wilt thou not tell me? And Amnon said unto him, I love Tamar, my brother Absalom’s sister.
original_text:
And he said unto him, Why
art thou,
being the king’s son, lean from day to day? wilt thou not tell me? And Amnon said unto him, I love Tamar, my brother Absalom’s sister.

translated_text:
And Jonadab said unto him, Lay thee down on thy bed, and make thyself sick: and when thy father cometh to see thee, say unto him, I pray thee, let my sister Tamar come, and give me meat, and dress the meat in my sight, that I may see
it, and eat
it at her hand.
original_text:
And Jonadab said unto him, Lay thee down on thy bed, and make thyself sick: and when thy father cometh to see thee, say unto him, I pray thee, let my sister Tamar come, and give me meat, and dress the meat in my sight, that I may see
it, and eat
it at her hand.

translated_text: So Amnon lay down, and made himself sick: and when the king was come to see him, Amnon said unto the king, I pray thee, let Tamar my sister come, and make me a couple of cakes in my sight, that I may eat at her hand.
original_text: So Amnon lay down, and made himself sick: and when the king was come to see him, Amnon said unto the king, I pray thee, let Tamar my sister come, and make me a couple of cakes in my sight, that I may eat at her hand.

translated_text: Then David sent home to Tamar, saying, Go now to thy brother Amnon’s house, and dress him meat.
original_text: Then David sent home to Tamar, saying, Go now to thy brother Amnon’s house, and dress him meat.

translated_text:
So Tamar went to her brother Amnon’s house; and he was laid down. And she took flour, and kneaded
it, and made cakes in his sight, and did bake the cakes.
original_text:
So Tamar went to her brother Amnon’s house; and he was laid down. And she took flour, and kneaded
it, and made cakes in his sight, and did bake the cakes.

translated_text:
And she took a pan, and poured
them out before him; but he refused to eat. And Amnon said, Have out all men from me. And they went out every man from him.
original_text:
And she took a pan, and poured
them out before him; but he refused to eat. And Amnon said, Have out all men from me. And they went out every man from him.

translated_text:
And Amnon said unto Tamar, Bring the meat into the chamber, that I may eat of thine hand. And Tamar took the cakes which she had made, and brought
them into the chamber to Amnon her brother.
original_text:
And Amnon said unto Tamar, Bring the meat into the chamber, that I may eat of thine hand. And Tamar took the cakes which she had made, and brought
them into the chamber to Amnon her brother.

translated_text:
And when she had brought
them unto him to eat, he took hold of her, and said unto her, Come lie with me, my sister.
original_text:
And when she had brought
them unto him to eat, he took hold of her, and said unto her, Come lie with me, my sister.

translated_text: And she answered him, Nay, my brother, do not force me; for no such thing ought to be done in Israel: do not thou this folly.
original_text: And she answered him, Nay, my brother, do not force me; for no such thing ought to be done in Israel: do not thou this folly.

translated_text: And I, whither shall I cause my shame to go? and as for thee, thou shalt be as one of the fools in Israel. Now therefore, I pray thee, speak unto the king; for he will not withhold me from thee.
original_text: And I, whither shall I cause my shame to go? and as for thee, thou shalt be as one of the fools in Israel. Now therefore, I pray thee, speak unto the king; for he will not withhold me from thee.

translated_text: Howbeit he would not hearken unto her voice: but, being stronger than she, forced her, and lay with her.
original_text: Howbeit he would not hearken unto her voice: but, being stronger than she, forced her, and lay with her.

translated_text:
Then Amnon hated her exceedingly; so that the hatred wherewith he hated her
was greater than the love wherewith he had loved her. And Amnon said unto her, Arise, be gone.
original_text:
Then Amnon hated her exceedingly; so that the hatred wherewith he hated her
was greater than the love wherewith he had loved her. And Amnon said unto her, Arise, be gone.

translated_text:
And she said unto him,
There is no cause: this evil in sending me away
is greater than the other that thou didst unto me. But he would not hearken unto her.
original_text:
And she said unto him,
There is no cause: this evil in sending me away
is greater than the other that thou didst unto me. But he would not hearken unto her.

translated_text:
Then he called his servant that ministered unto him, and said, Put now this
woman out from me, and bolt the door after her.
original_text:
Then he called his servant that ministered unto him, and said, Put now this
woman out from me, and bolt the door after her.

translated_text:
And
she had a garment of divers colours upon her: for with such robes were the king’s daughters
that were virgins apparelled. Then his servant brought her out, and bolted the door after her.
original_text:
And
she had a garment of divers colours upon her: for with such robes were the king’s daughters
that were virgins apparelled. Then his servant brought her out, and bolted the door after her.

translated_text:
And Tamar put ashes on her head, and rent her garment of divers colours that
was on her, and laid her hand on her head, and went on crying.
original_text:
And Tamar put ashes on her head, and rent her garment of divers colours that
was on her, and laid her hand on her head, and went on crying.

translated_text:
And Absalom her brother said unto her, Hath Amnon thy brother been with thee? but hold now thy peace, my sister: he
is thy brother; regard not this thing. So Tamar remained desolate in her brother Absalom’s house.
original_text:
And Absalom her brother said unto her, Hath Amnon thy brother been with thee? but hold now thy peace, my sister: he
is thy brother; regard not this thing. So Tamar remained desolate in her brother Absalom’s house.

translated_text: But when king David heard of all these things, he was very wroth.
original_text: But when king David heard of all these things, he was very wroth.

translated_text: And Absalom spake unto his brother Amnon neither good nor bad: for Absalom hated Amnon, because he had forced his sister Tamar.
original_text: And Absalom spake unto his brother Amnon neither good nor bad: for Absalom hated Amnon, because he had forced his sister Tamar.

translated_text:
And it came to pass after two full years, that Absalom had sheepshearers in Baal-hazor, which
is beside Ephraim: and Absalom invited all the king’s sons.
original_text:
And it came to pass after two full years, that Absalom had sheepshearers in Baal-hazor, which
is beside Ephraim: and Absalom invited all the king’s sons.

translated_text: And Absalom came to the king, and said, Behold now, thy servant hath sheepshearers; let the king, I beseech thee, and his servants go with thy servant.
original_text: And Absalom came to the king, and said, Behold now, thy servant hath sheepshearers; let the king, I beseech thee, and his servants go with thy servant.

translated_text: And the king said to Absalom, Nay, my son, let us not all now go, lest we be chargeable unto thee. And he pressed him: howbeit he would not go, but blessed him.
original_text: And the king said to Absalom, Nay, my son, let us not all now go, lest we be chargeable unto thee. And he pressed him: howbeit he would not go, but blessed him.

translated_text: Then said Absalom, If not, I pray thee, let my brother Amnon go with us. And the king said unto him, Why should he go with thee?
original_text: Then said Absalom, If not, I pray thee, let my brother Amnon go with us. And the king said unto him, Why should he go with thee?

translated_text: But Absalom pressed him, that he let Amnon and all the king’s sons go with him.
original_text: But Absalom pressed him, that he let Amnon and all the king’s sons go with him.

translated_text: Now Absalom had commanded his servants, saying, Mark ye now when Amnon’s heart is merry with wine, and when I say unto you, Smite Amnon; then kill him, fear not: have not I commanded you? be courageous and be valiant.
original_text: Now Absalom had commanded his servants, saying, Mark ye now when Amnon’s heart is merry with wine, and when I say unto you, Smite Amnon; then kill him, fear not: have not I commanded you? be courageous and be valiant.

translated_text: And the servants of Absalom did unto Amnon as Absalom had commanded. Then all the king’s sons arose, and every man gat him up upon his mule, and fled.
original_text: And the servants of Absalom did unto Amnon as Absalom had commanded. Then all the king’s sons arose, and every man gat him up upon his mule, and fled.

translated_text: And it came to pass, while they were in the way, that tidings came to David, saying, Absalom hath slain all the king’s sons, and there is not one of them left.
original_text: And it came to pass, while they were in the way, that tidings came to David, saying, Absalom hath slain all the king’s sons, and there is not one of them left.

translated_text: Then the king arose, and tare his garments, and lay on the earth; and all his servants stood by with their clothes rent.
original_text: Then the king arose, and tare his garments, and lay on the earth; and all his servants stood by with their clothes rent.

translated_text:
And Jonadab, the son of Shimeah David’s brother, answered and said, Let not my lord suppose
that they have slain all the young men the king’s sons; for Amnon only is dead: for by the appointment of Absalom this hath been determined from the day that he forced his sister Tamar.
original_text:
And Jonadab, the son of Shimeah David’s brother, answered and said, Let not my lord suppose
that they have slain all the young men the king’s sons; for Amnon only is dead: for by the appointment of Absalom this hath been determined from the day that he forced his sister Tamar.

translated_text: Now therefore let not my lord the king take the thing to his heart, to think that all the king’s sons are dead: for Amnon only is dead.
original_text: Now therefore let not my lord the king take the thing to his heart, to think that all the king’s sons are dead: for Amnon only is dead.

translated_text: But Absalom fled. And the young man that kept the watch lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, behold, there came much people by the way of the hill side behind him.
original_text: But Absalom fled. And the young man that kept the watch lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, behold, there came much people by the way of the hill side behind him.

translated_text: And Jonadab said unto the king, Behold, the king’s sons come: as thy servant said, so it is.
original_text: And Jonadab said unto the king, Behold, the king’s sons come: as thy servant said, so it is.

translated_text: And it came to pass, as soon as he had made an end of speaking, that, behold, the king’s sons came, and lifted up their voice and wept: and the king also and all his servants wept very sore.
original_text: And it came to pass, as soon as he had made an end of speaking, that, behold, the king’s sons came, and lifted up their voice and wept: and the king also and all his servants wept very sore.

translated_text:
But Absalom fled, and went to Talmai, the son of Ammihud, king of Geshur. And
David mourned for his son every day.
original_text:
But Absalom fled, and went to Talmai, the son of Ammihud, king of Geshur. And
David mourned for his son every day.

translated_text: So Absalom fled, and went to Geshur, and was there three years.
original_text: So Absalom fled, and went to Geshur, and was there three years.

translated_text:
And
the soul of king David longed to go forth unto Absalom: for he was comforted concerning Amnon, seeing he was dead.
original_text:
And
the soul of king David longed to go forth unto Absalom: for he was comforted concerning Amnon, seeing he was dead.

translated_text: And the LORD sent Nathan unto David. And he came unto him, and said unto him, There were two men in one city; the one rich, and the other poor.
original_text: And the LORD sent Nathan unto David. And he came unto him, and said unto him, There were two men in one city; the one rich, and the other poor.

translated_text:
The rich
man had exceeding many flocks and herds:
original_text:
The rich
man had exceeding many flocks and herds:

translated_text:
But the poor
man had nothing, save one little ewe lamb, which he had bought and nourished up: and it grew up together with him, and with his children; it did eat of his own meat, and drank of his own cup, and lay in his bosom, and was unto him as a daughter.
original_text:
But the poor
man had nothing, save one little ewe lamb, which he had bought and nourished up: and it grew up together with him, and with his children; it did eat of his own meat, and drank of his own cup, and lay in his bosom, and was unto him as a daughter.

translated_text: And there came a traveller unto the rich man, and he spared to take of his own flock and of his own herd, to dress for the wayfaring man that was come unto him; but took the poor man’s lamb, and dressed it for the man that was come to him.
original_text: And there came a traveller unto the rich man, and he spared to take of his own flock and of his own herd, to dress for the wayfaring man that was come unto him; but took the poor man’s lamb, and dressed it for the man that was come to him.

translated_text:
And David’s anger was greatly kindled against the man; and he said to Nathan, As the LORD liveth, the man that hath done this
thing shall surely die:
original_text:
And David’s anger was greatly kindled against the man; and he said to Nathan, As the LORD liveth, the man that hath done this
thing shall surely die:

translated_text: And he shall restore the lamb fourfold, because he did this thing, and because he had no pity.
original_text: And he shall restore the lamb fourfold, because he did this thing, and because he had no pity.

translated_text:
And Nathan said to David, Thou
art the man. Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, I anointed thee king over Israel, and I delivered thee out of the hand of Saul;
original_text:
And Nathan said to David, Thou
art the man. Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, I anointed thee king over Israel, and I delivered thee out of the hand of Saul;

translated_text:
And I gave thee thy master’s house, and thy master’s wives into thy bosom, and gave thee the house of Israel and of Judah; and if
that had been too little, I would moreover have given unto thee such and such things.
original_text:
And I gave thee thy master’s house, and thy master’s wives into thy bosom, and gave thee the house of Israel and of Judah; and if
that had been too little, I would moreover have given unto thee such and such things.

translated_text:
Wherefore hast thou despised the commandment of the LORD, to do evil in his sight? thou hast killed Uriah the Hittite with the sword, and hast taken his wife
to be thy wife, and hast slain him with the sword of the children of Ammon.
original_text:
Wherefore hast thou despised the commandment of the LORD, to do evil in his sight? thou hast killed Uriah the Hittite with the sword, and hast taken his wife
to be thy wife, and hast slain him with the sword of the children of Ammon.

translated_text: Now therefore the sword shall never depart from thine house; because thou hast despised me, and hast taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be thy wife.
original_text: Now therefore the sword shall never depart from thine house; because thou hast despised me, and hast taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be thy wife.

translated_text:
Thus saith the LORD, Behold, I will raise up evil against thee out of thine own house, and I will take thy wives before thine eyes, and give
them unto thy neighbour, and he shall lie with thy wives in the sight of this sun.
original_text:
Thus saith the LORD, Behold, I will raise up evil against thee out of thine own house, and I will take thy wives before thine eyes, and give
them unto thy neighbour, and he shall lie with thy wives in the sight of this sun.

translated_text:
For thou didst
it secretly: but I will do this thing before all Israel, and before the sun.
original_text:
For thou didst
it secretly: but I will do this thing before all Israel, and before the sun.

translated_text: And David said unto Nathan, I have sinned against the LORD. And Nathan said unto David, The LORD also hath put away thy sin; thou shalt not die.
original_text: And David said unto Nathan, I have sinned against the LORD. And Nathan said unto David, The LORD also hath put away thy sin; thou shalt not die.

translated_text:
Howbeit, because by this deed thou hast given great occasion to the enemies of the LORD to blaspheme, the child also
that is born unto thee shall surely die.
original_text:
Howbeit, because by this deed thou hast given great occasion to the enemies of the LORD to blaspheme, the child also
that is born unto thee shall surely die.

translated_text: And Nathan departed unto his house. And the LORD struck the child that Uriah’s wife bare unto David, and it was very sick.
original_text: And Nathan departed unto his house. And the LORD struck the child that Uriah’s wife bare unto David, and it was very sick.

translated_text: David therefore besought God for the child; and David fasted, and went in, and lay all night upon the earth.
original_text: David therefore besought God for the child; and David fasted, and went in, and lay all night upon the earth.

translated_text:
And the elders of his house arose,
and went to him, to raise him up from the earth: but he would not, neither did he eat bread with them.
original_text:
And the elders of his house arose,
and went to him, to raise him up from the earth: but he would not, neither did he eat bread with them.

translated_text: And it came to pass on the seventh day, that the child died. And the servants of David feared to tell him that the child was dead: for they said, Behold, while the child was yet alive, we spake unto him, and he would not hearken unto our voice: how will he then vex himself, if we tell him that the child is dead?
original_text: And it came to pass on the seventh day, that the child died. And the servants of David feared to tell him that the child was dead: for they said, Behold, while the child was yet alive, we spake unto him, and he would not hearken unto our voice: how will he then vex himself, if we tell him that the child is dead?

translated_text: But when David saw that his servants whispered, David perceived that the child was dead: therefore David said unto his servants, Is the child dead? And they said, He is dead.
original_text: But when David saw that his servants whispered, David perceived that the child was dead: therefore David said unto his servants, Is the child dead? And they said, He is dead.

translated_text:
Then David arose from the earth, and washed, and anointed
himself,
 and changed his apparel, and came into the house of the LORD, and worshipped: then he came to his own house; and when he required, they set bread before him, and he did eat.
original_text:
Then David arose from the earth, and washed, and anointed
himself,
 and changed his apparel, and came into the house of the LORD, and worshipped: then he came to his own house; and when he required, they set bread before him, and he did eat.

translated_text:
Then said his servants unto him, What thing
is this that thou hast done? thou didst fast and weep for the child,
while it was
 alive; but when the child was dead, thou didst rise and eat bread.
original_text:
Then said his servants unto him, What thing
is this that thou hast done? thou didst fast and weep for the child,
while it was
 alive; but when the child was dead, thou didst rise and eat bread.

translated_text:
And he said, While the child was yet alive, I fasted and wept: for I said, Who can tell
whether GOD will be gracious to me, that the child may live?
original_text:
And he said, While the child was yet alive, I fasted and wept: for I said, Who can tell
whether GOD will be gracious to me, that the child may live?

translated_text: But now he is dead, wherefore should I fast? can I bring him back again? I shall go to him, but he shall not return to me.
original_text: But now he is dead, wherefore should I fast? can I bring him back again? I shall go to him, but he shall not return to me.

translated_text: And David comforted Bath-sheba his wife, and went in unto her, and lay with her: and she bare a son, and he called his name Solomon: and the LORD loved him.
original_text: And David comforted Bath-sheba his wife, and went in unto her, and lay with her: and she bare a son, and he called his name Solomon: and the LORD loved him.

translated_text: And he sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet; and he called his name Jedidiah, because of the LORD.
original_text: And he sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet; and he called his name Jedidiah, because of the LORD.

translated_text: And Joab fought against Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and took the royal city.
original_text: And Joab fought against Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and took the royal city.

translated_text: And Joab sent messengers to David, and said, I have fought against Rabbah, and have taken the city of waters.
original_text: And Joab sent messengers to David, and said, I have fought against Rabbah, and have taken the city of waters.

translated_text: Now therefore gather the rest of the people together, and encamp against the city, and take it: lest I take the city, and it be called after my name.
original_text: Now therefore gather the rest of the people together, and encamp against the city, and take it: lest I take the city, and it be called after my name.

translated_text: And David gathered all the people together, and went to Rabbah, and fought against it, and took it.
original_text: And David gathered all the people together, and went to Rabbah, and fought against it, and took it.

translated_text:
And he took their king’s crown from off his head, the weight whereof
was a talent of gold with the precious stones: and it was
set on David’s head. And he brought forth the spoil of the city in great abundance.
original_text:
And he took their king’s crown from off his head, the weight whereof
was a talent of gold with the precious stones: and it was
set on David’s head. And he brought forth the spoil of the city in great abundance.

translated_text:
And he brought forth the people that
were therein, and put
them under saws, and under harrows of iron, and under axes of iron, and made them pass through the brickkiln: and thus did he unto all the cities of the children of Ammon. So David and all the people returned unto Jerusalem.
original_text:
And he brought forth the people that
were therein, and put
them under saws, and under harrows of iron, and under axes of iron, and made them pass through the brickkiln: and thus did he unto all the cities of the children of Ammon. So David and all the people returned unto Jerusalem.

translated_text:
And it came to pass, after the year was expired, at the time when kings go forth
to battle, that David sent Joab, and his servants with him, and all Israel; and they destroyed the children of Ammon, and besieged Rabbah. But David tarried still at Jerusalem.
original_text:
And it came to pass, after the year was expired, at the time when kings go forth
to battle, that David sent Joab, and his servants with him, and all Israel; and they destroyed the children of Ammon, and besieged Rabbah. But David tarried still at Jerusalem.

translated_text:
And it came to pass in an eveningtide, that David arose from off his bed, and walked upon the roof of the king’s house: and from the roof he saw a woman washing herself; and the woman
was very beautiful to look upon.
original_text:
And it came to pass in an eveningtide, that David arose from off his bed, and walked upon the roof of the king’s house: and from the roof he saw a woman washing herself; and the woman
was very beautiful to look upon.

translated_text:
And David sent and enquired after the woman. And
one said,
Is not this Bath-sheba, the daughter of Eliam, the wife of Uriah the Hittite?
original_text:
And David sent and enquired after the woman. And
one said,
Is not this Bath-sheba, the daughter of Eliam, the wife of Uriah the Hittite?

translated_text: And David sent messengers, and took her; and she came in unto him, and he lay with her; for she was purified from her uncleanness: and she returned unto her house.
original_text: And David sent messengers, and took her; and she came in unto him, and he lay with her; for she was purified from her uncleanness: and she returned unto her house.

translated_text:
And the woman conceived, and sent and told David, and said, I
am
 with child.
original_text:
And the woman conceived, and sent and told David, and said, I
am
 with child.

translated_text:
And David sent to Joab,
saying, Send me Uriah the Hittite. And Joab sent Uriah to David.
original_text:
And David sent to Joab,
saying, Send me Uriah the Hittite. And Joab sent Uriah to David.

translated_text:
And when Uriah was come unto him, David demanded
of him how Joab did, and how the people did, and how the war prospered.
original_text:
And when Uriah was come unto him, David demanded
of him how Joab did, and how the people did, and how the war prospered.

translated_text:
And David said to Uriah, Go down to thy house, and wash thy feet. And Uriah departed out of the king’s house, and there followed him a mess
of meat from the king.
original_text:
And David said to Uriah, Go down to thy house, and wash thy feet. And Uriah departed out of the king’s house, and there followed him a mess
of meat from the king.

translated_text: But Uriah slept at the door of the king’s house with all the servants of his lord, and went not down to his house.
original_text: But Uriah slept at the door of the king’s house with all the servants of his lord, and went not down to his house.

translated_text:
And when they had told David, saying, Uriah went not down unto his house, David said unto Uriah, Camest thou not from
thy journey? why
then didst thou not go down unto thine house?
original_text:
And when they had told David, saying, Uriah went not down unto his house, David said unto Uriah, Camest thou not from
thy journey? why
then didst thou not go down unto thine house?

translated_text:
And Uriah said unto David, The ark, and Israel, and Judah, abide in tents; and my lord Joab, and the servants of my lord, are encamped in the open fields; shall I then go into mine house, to eat and to drink, and to lie with my wife?
as thou livest, and
as thy soul liveth, I will not do this thing.
original_text:
And Uriah said unto David, The ark, and Israel, and Judah, abide in tents; and my lord Joab, and the servants of my lord, are encamped in the open fields; shall I then go into mine house, to eat and to drink, and to lie with my wife?
as thou livest, and
as thy soul liveth, I will not do this thing.

translated_text: And David said to Uriah, Tarry here to day also, and to morrow I will let thee depart. So Uriah abode in Jerusalem that day, and the morrow.
original_text: And David said to Uriah, Tarry here to day also, and to morrow I will let thee depart. So Uriah abode in Jerusalem that day, and the morrow.

translated_text: And when David had called him, he did eat and drink before him; and he made him drunk: and at even he went out to lie on his bed with the servants of his lord, but went not down to his house.
original_text: And when David had called him, he did eat and drink before him; and he made him drunk: and at even he went out to lie on his bed with the servants of his lord, but went not down to his house.

translated_text:
And it came to pass in the morning, that David wrote a letter to Joab, and sent
it by the hand of Uriah.
original_text:
And it came to pass in the morning, that David wrote a letter to Joab, and sent
it by the hand of Uriah.

translated_text: And he wrote in the letter, saying, Set ye Uriah in the forefront of the hottest battle, and retire ye from him, that he may be smitten, and die.
original_text: And he wrote in the letter, saying, Set ye Uriah in the forefront of the hottest battle, and retire ye from him, that he may be smitten, and die.

translated_text:
And it came to pass, when Joab observed the city, that he assigned Uriah unto a place where he knew that valiant men
were.
original_text:
And it came to pass, when Joab observed the city, that he assigned Uriah unto a place where he knew that valiant men
were.

translated_text:
And the men of the city went out, and fought with Joab: and there fell
some of the people of the servants of David; and Uriah the Hittite died also.
original_text:
And the men of the city went out, and fought with Joab: and there fell
some of the people of the servants of David; and Uriah the Hittite died also.

translated_text: Then Joab sent and told David all the things concerning the war;
original_text: Then Joab sent and told David all the things concerning the war;

translated_text: And charged the messenger, saying, When thou hast made an end of telling the matters of the war unto the king,
original_text: And charged the messenger, saying, When thou hast made an end of telling the matters of the war unto the king,

translated_text: And if so be that the king’s wrath arise, and he say unto thee, Wherefore approached ye so nigh unto the city when ye did fight? knew ye not that they would shoot from the wall?
original_text: And if so be that the king’s wrath arise, and he say unto thee, Wherefore approached ye so nigh unto the city when ye did fight? knew ye not that they would shoot from the wall?

translated_text: Who smote Abimelech the son of Jerubbesheth? did not a woman cast a piece of a millstone upon him from the wall, that he died in Thebez? why went ye nigh the wall? then say thou, Thy servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.
original_text: Who smote Abimelech the son of Jerubbesheth? did not a woman cast a piece of a millstone upon him from the wall, that he died in Thebez? why went ye nigh the wall? then say thou, Thy servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.

translated_text: So the messenger went, and came and shewed David all that Joab had sent him for.
original_text: So the messenger went, and came and shewed David all that Joab had sent him for.

translated_text: And the messenger said unto David, Surely the men prevailed against us, and came out unto us into the field, and we were upon them even unto the entering of the gate.
original_text: And the messenger said unto David, Surely the men prevailed against us, and came out unto us into the field, and we were upon them even unto the entering of the gate.

translated_text:
And the shooters shot from off the wall upon thy servants; and
some of the king’s servants be dead, and thy servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.
original_text:
And the shooters shot from off the wall upon thy servants; and
some of the king’s servants be dead, and thy servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also.

translated_text: Then David said unto the messenger, Thus shalt thou say unto Joab, Let not this thing displease thee, for the sword devoureth one as well as another: make thy battle more strong against the city, and overthrow it: and encourage thou him.
original_text: Then David said unto the messenger, Thus shalt thou say unto Joab, Let not this thing displease thee, for the sword devoureth one as well as another: make thy battle more strong against the city, and overthrow it: and encourage thou him.

translated_text: And when the wife of Uriah heard that Uriah her husband was dead, she mourned for her husband.
original_text: And when the wife of Uriah heard that Uriah her husband was dead, she mourned for her husband.

translated_text: And when the mourning was past, David sent and fetched her to his house, and she became his wife, and bare him a son. But the thing that David had done displeased the LORD.
original_text: And when the mourning was past, David sent and fetched her to his house, and she became his wife, and bare him a son. But the thing that David had done displeased the LORD.

translated_text: And it was told Joab, Behold, the king weepeth and mourneth for Absalom.
original_text: And it was told Joab, Behold, the king weepeth and mourneth for Absalom.

translated_text:
And the victory that day was
turned into mourning unto all the people: for the people heard say that day how the king was grieved for his son.
original_text:
And the victory that day was
turned into mourning unto all the people: for the people heard say that day how the king was grieved for his son.

translated_text: And the people gat them by stealth that day into the city, as people being ashamed steal away when they flee in battle.
original_text: And the people gat them by stealth that day into the city, as people being ashamed steal away when they flee in battle.

translated_text: But the king covered his face, and the king cried with a loud voice, O my son Absalom, O Absalom, my son, my son!
original_text: But the king covered his face, and the king cried with a loud voice, O my son Absalom, O Absalom, my son, my son!

translated_text: And Joab came into the house to the king, and said, Thou hast shamed this day the faces of all thy servants, which this day have saved thy life, and the lives of thy sons and of thy daughters, and the lives of thy wives, and the lives of thy concubines;
original_text: And Joab came into the house to the king, and said, Thou hast shamed this day the faces of all thy servants, which this day have saved thy life, and the lives of thy sons and of thy daughters, and the lives of thy wives, and the lives of thy concubines;

translated_text: In that thou lovest thine enemies, and hatest thy friends. For thou hast declared this day, that thou regardest neither princes nor servants: for this day I perceive, that if Absalom had lived, and all we had died this day, then it had pleased thee well.
original_text: In that thou lovest thine enemies, and hatest thy friends. For thou hast declared this day, that thou regardest neither princes nor servants: for this day I perceive, that if Absalom had lived, and all we had died this day, then it had pleased thee well.

translated_text: Now therefore arise, go forth, and speak comfortably unto thy servants: for I swear by the LORD, if thou go not forth, there will not tarry one with thee this night: and that will be worse unto thee than all the evil that befell thee from thy youth until now.
original_text: Now therefore arise, go forth, and speak comfortably unto thy servants: for I swear by the LORD, if thou go not forth, there will not tarry one with thee this night: and that will be worse unto thee than all the evil that befell thee from thy youth until now.

translated_text: Then the king arose, and sat in the gate. And they told unto all the people, saying, Behold, the king doth sit in the gate. And all the people came before the king: for Israel had fled every man to his tent.
original_text: Then the king arose, and sat in the gate. And they told unto all the people, saying, Behold, the king doth sit in the gate. And all the people came before the king: for Israel had fled every man to his tent.

translated_text: And all the people were at strife throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, The king saved us out of the hand of our enemies, and he delivered us out of the hand of the Philistines; and now he is fled out of the land for Absalom.
original_text: And all the people were at strife throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, The king saved us out of the hand of our enemies, and he delivered us out of the hand of the Philistines; and now he is fled out of the land for Absalom.

translated_text: And Absalom, whom we anointed over us, is dead in battle. Now therefore why speak ye not a word of bringing the king back?
original_text: And Absalom, whom we anointed over us, is dead in battle. Now therefore why speak ye not a word of bringing the king back?

translated_text:
And king David sent to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, saying, Speak unto the elders of Judah, saying, Why are ye the last to bring the king back to his house? seeing the speech of all Israel is come to the king,
even
 to his house.
original_text:
And king David sent to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, saying, Speak unto the elders of Judah, saying, Why are ye the last to bring the king back to his house? seeing the speech of all Israel is come to the king,
even
 to his house.

translated_text:
Ye
are my brethren, ye
are my bones and my flesh: wherefore then are ye the last to bring back the king?
original_text:
Ye
are my brethren, ye
are my bones and my flesh: wherefore then are ye the last to bring back the king?

translated_text:
And say ye to Amasa,
Art thou not of my bone, and of my flesh? God do so to me, and more also, if thou be not captain of the host before me continually in the room of Joab.
original_text:
And say ye to Amasa,
Art thou not of my bone, and of my flesh? God do so to me, and more also, if thou be not captain of the host before me continually in the room of Joab.

translated_text:
And he bowed the heart of all the men of Judah, even as
the heart of one man; so that they sent
this word unto the king, Return thou, and all thy servants.
original_text:
And he bowed the heart of all the men of Judah, even as
the heart of one man; so that they sent
this word unto the king, Return thou, and all thy servants.

translated_text: So the king returned, and came to Jordan. And Judah came to Gilgal, to go to meet the king, to conduct the king over Jordan.
original_text: So the king returned, and came to Jordan. And Judah came to Gilgal, to go to meet the king, to conduct the king over Jordan.

translated_text:
And Shimei the son of Gera, a Benjamite, which
was of Bahurim, hasted and came down with the men of Judah to meet king David.
original_text:
And Shimei the son of Gera, a Benjamite, which
was of Bahurim, hasted and came down with the men of Judah to meet king David.

translated_text:
And
there were a thousand men of Benjamin with him, and Ziba the servant of the house of Saul, and his fifteen sons and his twenty servants with him; and they went over Jordan before the king.
original_text:
And
there were a thousand men of Benjamin with him, and Ziba the servant of the house of Saul, and his fifteen sons and his twenty servants with him; and they went over Jordan before the king.

translated_text: And there went over a ferry boat to carry over the king’s household, and to do what he thought good. And Shimei the son of Gera fell down before the king, as he was come over Jordan;
original_text: And there went over a ferry boat to carry over the king’s household, and to do what he thought good. And Shimei the son of Gera fell down before the king, as he was come over Jordan;

translated_text: And said unto the king, Let not my lord impute iniquity unto me, neither do thou remember that which thy servant did perversely the day that my lord the king went out of Jerusalem, that the king should take it to his heart.
original_text: And said unto the king, Let not my lord impute iniquity unto me, neither do thou remember that which thy servant did perversely the day that my lord the king went out of Jerusalem, that the king should take it to his heart.

translated_text: For thy servant doth know that I have sinned: therefore, behold, I am come the first this day of all the house of Joseph to go down to meet my lord the king.
original_text: For thy servant doth know that I have sinned: therefore, behold, I am come the first this day of all the house of Joseph to go down to meet my lord the king.

translated_text: But Abishai the son of Zeruiah answered and said, Shall not Shimei be put to death for this, because he cursed the LORD’S anointed?
original_text: But Abishai the son of Zeruiah answered and said, Shall not Shimei be put to death for this, because he cursed the LORD’S anointed?

translated_text:
And David said, What have I to do with you, ye sons of Zeruiah, that ye should this day be adversaries unto me? shall there any man be put to death this day in Israel? for do not I know that I
am this day king over Israel?
original_text:
And David said, What have I to do with you, ye sons of Zeruiah, that ye should this day be adversaries unto me? shall there any man be put to death this day in Israel? for do not I know that I
am this day king over Israel?

translated_text: Therefore the king said unto Shimei, Thou shalt not die. And the king sware unto him.
original_text: Therefore the king said unto Shimei, Thou shalt not die. And the king sware unto him.

translated_text:
And Mephibosheth the son of Saul came down to meet the king, and had neither dressed his feet, nor trimmed his beard, nor washed his clothes, from the day the king departed until the day he came
again in peace.
original_text:
And Mephibosheth the son of Saul came down to meet the king, and had neither dressed his feet, nor trimmed his beard, nor washed his clothes, from the day the king departed until the day he came
again in peace.

translated_text: And it came to pass, when he was come to Jerusalem to meet the king, that the king said unto him, Wherefore wentest not thou with me, Mephibosheth?
original_text: And it came to pass, when he was come to Jerusalem to meet the king, that the king said unto him, Wherefore wentest not thou with me, Mephibosheth?

translated_text:
And he answered, My lord, O king, my servant deceived me: for thy servant said, I will saddle me an ass, that I may ride thereon, and go to the king; because thy servant
is lame.
original_text:
And he answered, My lord, O king, my servant deceived me: for thy servant said, I will saddle me an ass, that I may ride thereon, and go to the king; because thy servant
is lame.

translated_text:
And he hath slandered thy servant unto my lord the king; but my lord the king
is as an angel of God: do therefore
what is good in thine eyes.
original_text:
And he hath slandered thy servant unto my lord the king; but my lord the king
is as an angel of God: do therefore
what is good in thine eyes.

translated_text:
For all
of my father’s house were but dead men before my lord the king: yet didst thou set thy servant among them that did eat at thine own table. What right therefore have I yet to cry any more unto the king?
original_text:
For all
of my father’s house were but dead men before my lord the king: yet didst thou set thy servant among them that did eat at thine own table. What right therefore have I yet to cry any more unto the king?

translated_text: And the king said unto him, Why speakest thou any more of thy matters? I have said, Thou and Ziba divide the land.
original_text: And the king said unto him, Why speakest thou any more of thy matters? I have said, Thou and Ziba divide the land.

translated_text: And Mephibosheth said unto the king, Yea, let him take all, forasmuch as my lord the king is come again in peace unto his own house.
original_text: And Mephibosheth said unto the king, Yea, let him take all, forasmuch as my lord the king is come again in peace unto his own house.

translated_text: And Barzillai the Gileadite came down from Rogelim, and went over Jordan with the king, to conduct him over Jordan.
original_text: And Barzillai the Gileadite came down from Rogelim, and went over Jordan with the king, to conduct him over Jordan.

translated_text:
Now Barzillai was a very aged man,
even fourscore years old: and he had provided the king of sustenance while he lay at Mahanaim; for he
was a very great man.
original_text:
Now Barzillai was a very aged man,
even fourscore years old: and he had provided the king of sustenance while he lay at Mahanaim; for he
was a very great man.

translated_text: And the king said unto Barzillai, Come thou over with me, and I will feed thee with me in Jerusalem.
original_text: And the king said unto Barzillai, Come thou over with me, and I will feed thee with me in Jerusalem.

translated_text: And Barzillai said unto the king, How long have I to live, that I should go up with the king unto Jerusalem?
original_text: And Barzillai said unto the king, How long have I to live, that I should go up with the king unto Jerusalem?

translated_text:
I
am this day fourscore years old:
and can I discern between good and evil? can thy servant taste what I eat or what I drink? can I hear any more the voice of singing men and singing women? wherefore then should thy servant be yet a burden unto my lord the king?
original_text:
I
am this day fourscore years old:
and can I discern between good and evil? can thy servant taste what I eat or what I drink? can I hear any more the voice of singing men and singing women? wherefore then should thy servant be yet a burden unto my lord the king?

translated_text: Thy servant will go a little way over Jordan with the king: and why should the king recompense it me with such a reward?
original_text: Thy servant will go a little way over Jordan with the king: and why should the king recompense it me with such a reward?

translated_text:
Let thy servant, I pray thee, turn back again, that I may die in mine own city,
and be buried by the grave of my father and of my mother. But behold thy servant Chimham; let him go over with my lord the king; and do to him what shall seem good unto thee.
original_text:
Let thy servant, I pray thee, turn back again, that I may die in mine own city,
and be buried by the grave of my father and of my mother. But behold thy servant Chimham; let him go over with my lord the king; and do to him what shall seem good unto thee.

translated_text:
And the king answered, Chimham shall go over with me, and I will do to him that which shall seem good unto thee: and whatsoever thou shalt require of me,
that will I do for thee.
original_text:
And the king answered, Chimham shall go over with me, and I will do to him that which shall seem good unto thee: and whatsoever thou shalt require of me,
that will I do for thee.

translated_text: And all the people went over Jordan. And when the king was come over, the king kissed Barzillai, and blessed him; and he returned unto his own place.
original_text: And all the people went over Jordan. And when the king was come over, the king kissed Barzillai, and blessed him; and he returned unto his own place.

translated_text: Then the king went on to Gilgal, and Chimham went on with him: and all the people of Judah conducted the king, and also half the people of Israel.
original_text: Then the king went on to Gilgal, and Chimham went on with him: and all the people of Judah conducted the king, and also half the people of Israel.

translated_text: And, behold, all the men of Israel came to the king, and said unto the king, Why have our brethren the men of Judah stolen thee away, and have brought the king, and his household, and all David’s men with him, over Jordan?
original_text: And, behold, all the men of Israel came to the king, and said unto the king, Why have our brethren the men of Judah stolen thee away, and have brought the king, and his household, and all David’s men with him, over Jordan?

translated_text:
And all the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, Because the king
is near of kin to us: wherefore then be ye angry for this matter? have we eaten at all of the king’s
cost? or hath he given us any gift?
original_text:
And all the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, Because the king
is near of kin to us: wherefore then be ye angry for this matter? have we eaten at all of the king’s
cost? or hath he given us any gift?

translated_text:
And the men of Israel answered the men of Judah, and said, We have ten parts in the king, and we have also more
right in David than ye: why then did ye despise us, that our advice should not be first had in bringing back our king? And the words of the men of Judah were fiercer than the words of the men of Israel.
original_text:
And the men of Israel answered the men of Judah, and said, We have ten parts in the king, and we have also more
right in David than ye: why then did ye despise us, that our advice should not be first had in bringing back our king? And the words of the men of Judah were fiercer than the words of the men of Israel.

translated_text: And it came to pass after this, that the king of the children of Ammon died, and Hanun his son reigned in his stead.
original_text: And it came to pass after this, that the king of the children of Ammon died, and Hanun his son reigned in his stead.

translated_text: Then said David, I will shew kindness unto Hanun the son of Nahash, as his father shewed kindness unto me. And David sent to comfort him by the hand of his servants for his father. And David’s servants came into the land of the children of Ammon.
original_text: Then said David, I will shew kindness unto Hanun the son of Nahash, as his father shewed kindness unto me. And David sent to comfort him by the hand of his servants for his father. And David’s servants came into the land of the children of Ammon.

translated_text:
And the princes of the children of Ammon said unto Hanun their lord, Thinkest thou that David doth honour thy father, that he hath sent comforters unto thee? hath not David
rather sent his servants unto thee, to search the city, and to spy it out, and to overthrow it?
original_text:
And the princes of the children of Ammon said unto Hanun their lord, Thinkest thou that David doth honour thy father, that he hath sent comforters unto thee? hath not David
rather sent his servants unto thee, to search the city, and to spy it out, and to overthrow it?

translated_text:
Wherefore Hanun took David’s servants, and shaved off the one half of their beards, and cut off their garments in the middle,
even to their buttocks, and sent them away.
original_text:
Wherefore Hanun took David’s servants, and shaved off the one half of their beards, and cut off their garments in the middle,
even to their buttocks, and sent them away.

translated_text:
When they told
it unto David, he sent to meet them, because the men were greatly ashamed: and the king said, Tarry at Jericho until your beards be grown, and
then return.
original_text:
When they told
it unto David, he sent to meet them, because the men were greatly ashamed: and the king said, Tarry at Jericho until your beards be grown, and
then return.

translated_text: And when the children of Ammon saw that they stank before David, the children of Ammon sent and hired the Syrians of Beth-rehob, and the Syrians of Zoba, twenty thousand footmen, and of king Maacah a thousand men, and of Ish-tob twelve thousand men.
original_text: And when the children of Ammon saw that they stank before David, the children of Ammon sent and hired the Syrians of Beth-rehob, and the Syrians of Zoba, twenty thousand footmen, and of king Maacah a thousand men, and of Ish-tob twelve thousand men.

translated_text:
And when David heard of
it, he sent Joab, and all the host of the mighty men.
original_text:
And when David heard of
it, he sent Joab, and all the host of the mighty men.

translated_text:
And the children of Ammon came out, and put the battle in array at the entering in of the gate: and the Syrians of Zoba, and of Rehob, and Ish-tob, and Maacah,
were by themselves in the field.
original_text:
And the children of Ammon came out, and put the battle in array at the entering in of the gate: and the Syrians of Zoba, and of Rehob, and Ish-tob, and Maacah,
were by themselves in the field.

translated_text:
When Joab saw that the front of the battle was against him before and behind, he chose of all the choice
men of Israel, and put
them in array against the Syrians:
original_text:
When Joab saw that the front of the battle was against him before and behind, he chose of all the choice
men of Israel, and put
them in array against the Syrians:

translated_text:
And the rest of the people he delivered into the hand of Abishai his brother, that he might put
them in array against the children of Ammon.
original_text:
And the rest of the people he delivered into the hand of Abishai his brother, that he might put
them in array against the children of Ammon.

translated_text: And he said, If the Syrians be too strong for me, then thou shalt help me: but if the children of Ammon be too strong for thee, then I will come and help thee.
original_text: And he said, If the Syrians be too strong for me, then thou shalt help me: but if the children of Ammon be too strong for thee, then I will come and help thee.

translated_text: Be of good courage, and let us play the men for our people, and for the cities of our God: and the LORD do that which seemeth him good.
original_text: Be of good courage, and let us play the men for our people, and for the cities of our God: and the LORD do that which seemeth him good.

translated_text:
And Joab drew nigh, and the people that
were with him, unto the battle against the Syrians: and they fled before him.
original_text:
And Joab drew nigh, and the people that
were with him, unto the battle against the Syrians: and they fled before him.

translated_text: And when the children of Ammon saw that the Syrians were fled, then fled they also before Abishai, and entered into the city. So Joab returned from the children of Ammon, and came to Jerusalem.
original_text: And when the children of Ammon saw that the Syrians were fled, then fled they also before Abishai, and entered into the city. So Joab returned from the children of Ammon, and came to Jerusalem.

translated_text: And when the Syrians saw that they were smitten before Israel, they gathered themselves together.
original_text: And when the Syrians saw that they were smitten before Israel, they gathered themselves together.

translated_text:
And Hadarezer sent, and brought out the Syrians that
were
 beyond the river: and they came to Helam; and Shobach the captain of the host of Hadarezer
went before them.
original_text:
And Hadarezer sent, and brought out the Syrians that
were
 beyond the river: and they came to Helam; and Shobach the captain of the host of Hadarezer
went before them.

translated_text: And when it was told David, he gathered all Israel together, and passed over Jordan, and came to Helam. And the Syrians set themselves in array against David, and fought with him.
original_text: And when it was told David, he gathered all Israel together, and passed over Jordan, and came to Helam. And the Syrians set themselves in array against David, and fought with him.

translated_text:
And the Syrians fled before Israel; and David slew
the men of
 seven hundred chariots of the Syrians, and forty thousand horsemen, and smote Shobach the captain of their host, who died there.
original_text:
And the Syrians fled before Israel; and David slew
the men of
 seven hundred chariots of the Syrians, and forty thousand horsemen, and smote Shobach the captain of their host, who died there.

translated_text:
And when all the kings
that were servants to Hadarezer saw that they were smitten before Israel, they made peace with Israel, and served them. So the Syrians feared to help the children of Ammon any more.
original_text:
And when all the kings
that were servants to Hadarezer saw that they were smitten before Israel, they made peace with Israel, and served them. So the Syrians feared to help the children of Ammon any more.

translated_text: And again the anger of the LORD was kindled against Israel, and he moved David against them to say, Go, number Israel and Judah.
original_text: And again the anger of the LORD was kindled against Israel, and he moved David against them to say, Go, number Israel and Judah.

translated_text:
For the king said to Joab the captain of the host, which
was
 with him, Go now through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan even to Beer-sheba, and number ye the people, that I may know the number of the people.
original_text:
For the king said to Joab the captain of the host, which
was
 with him, Go now through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan even to Beer-sheba, and number ye the people, that I may know the number of the people.

translated_text:
And Joab said unto the king, Now the LORD thy God add unto the people, how many soever they be, an hundredfold, and that the eyes of my lord the king may see
it: but why doth my lord the king delight in this thing?
original_text:
And Joab said unto the king, Now the LORD thy God add unto the people, how many soever they be, an hundredfold, and that the eyes of my lord the king may see
it: but why doth my lord the king delight in this thing?

translated_text: Notwithstanding the king’s word prevailed against Joab, and against the captains of the host. And Joab and the captains of the host went out from the presence of the king, to number the people of Israel.
original_text: Notwithstanding the king’s word prevailed against Joab, and against the captains of the host. And Joab and the captains of the host went out from the presence of the king, to number the people of Israel.

translated_text:
And they passed over Jordan, and pitched in Aroer, on the right side of the city that
lieth in the midst of the river of Gad, and toward Jazer:
original_text:
And they passed over Jordan, and pitched in Aroer, on the right side of the city that
lieth in the midst of the river of Gad, and toward Jazer:

translated_text: Then they came to Gilead, and to the land of Tahtim-hodshi; and they came to Dan-jaan, and about to Zidon,
original_text: Then they came to Gilead, and to the land of Tahtim-hodshi; and they came to Dan-jaan, and about to Zidon,

translated_text:
And came to the strong hold of Tyre, and to all the cities of the Hivites, and of the Canaanites: and they went out to the south of Judah,
even to Beer-sheba.
original_text:
And came to the strong hold of Tyre, and to all the cities of the Hivites, and of the Canaanites: and they went out to the south of Judah,
even to Beer-sheba.

translated_text: So when they had gone through all the land, they came to Jerusalem at the end of nine months and twenty days.
original_text: So when they had gone through all the land, they came to Jerusalem at the end of nine months and twenty days.

translated_text:
And Joab gave up the sum of the number of the people unto the king: and there were in Israel eight hundred thousand valiant men that drew the sword; and the men of Judah
were five hundred thousand men.
original_text:
And Joab gave up the sum of the number of the people unto the king: and there were in Israel eight hundred thousand valiant men that drew the sword; and the men of Judah
were five hundred thousand men.

translated_text: And David’s heart smote him after that he had numbered the people. And David said unto the LORD, I have sinned greatly in that I have done: and now, I beseech thee, O LORD, take away the iniquity of thy servant; for I have done very foolishly.
original_text: And David’s heart smote him after that he had numbered the people. And David said unto the LORD, I have sinned greatly in that I have done: and now, I beseech thee, O LORD, take away the iniquity of thy servant; for I have done very foolishly.

translated_text: For when David was up in the morning, the word of the LORD came unto the prophet Gad, David’s seer, saying,
original_text: For when David was up in the morning, the word of the LORD came unto the prophet Gad, David’s seer, saying,

translated_text:
Go and say unto David, Thus saith the LORD, I offer thee three
things; choose thee one of them, that I may
do it unto thee.
original_text:
Go and say unto David, Thus saith the LORD, I offer thee three
things; choose thee one of them, that I may
do it unto thee.

translated_text: So Gad came to David, and told him, and said unto him, Shall seven years of famine come unto thee in thy land? or wilt thou flee three months before thine enemies, while they pursue thee? or that there be three days’ pestilence in thy land? now advise, and see what answer I shall return to him that sent me.
original_text: So Gad came to David, and told him, and said unto him, Shall seven years of famine come unto thee in thy land? or wilt thou flee three months before thine enemies, while they pursue thee? or that there be three days’ pestilence in thy land? now advise, and see what answer I shall return to him that sent me.

translated_text:
And David said unto Gad, I am in a great strait: let us fall now into the hand of the LORD; for his mercies
are great: and let me not fall into the hand of man.
original_text:
And David said unto Gad, I am in a great strait: let us fall now into the hand of the LORD; for his mercies
are great: and let me not fall into the hand of man.

translated_text: So the LORD sent a pestilence upon Israel from the morning even to the time appointed: and there died of the people from Dan even to Beer-sheba seventy thousand men.
original_text: So the LORD sent a pestilence upon Israel from the morning even to the time appointed: and there died of the people from Dan even to Beer-sheba seventy thousand men.

translated_text: And when the angel stretched out his hand upon Jerusalem to destroy it, the LORD repented him of the evil, and said to the angel that destroyed the people, It is enough: stay now thine hand. And the angel of the LORD was by the threshingplace of Araunah the Jebusite.
original_text: And when the angel stretched out his hand upon Jerusalem to destroy it, the LORD repented him of the evil, and said to the angel that destroyed the people, It is enough: stay now thine hand. And the angel of the LORD was by the threshingplace of Araunah the Jebusite.

translated_text: And David spake unto the LORD when he saw the angel that smote the people, and said, Lo, I have sinned, and I have done wickedly: but these sheep, what have they done? let thine hand, I pray thee, be against me, and against my father’s house.
original_text: And David spake unto the LORD when he saw the angel that smote the people, and said, Lo, I have sinned, and I have done wickedly: but these sheep, what have they done? let thine hand, I pray thee, be against me, and against my father’s house.

translated_text: And Gad came that day to David, and said unto him, Go up, rear an altar unto the LORD in the threshingfloor of Araunah the Jebusite.
original_text: And Gad came that day to David, and said unto him, Go up, rear an altar unto the LORD in the threshingfloor of Araunah the Jebusite.

translated_text: And David, according to the saying of Gad, went up as the LORD commanded.
original_text: And David, according to the saying of Gad, went up as the LORD commanded.

translated_text: And Araunah looked, and saw the king and his servants coming on toward him: and Araunah went out, and bowed himself before the king on his face upon the ground.
original_text: And Araunah looked, and saw the king and his servants coming on toward him: and Araunah went out, and bowed himself before the king on his face upon the ground.

translated_text: And Araunah said, Wherefore is my lord the king come to his servant? And David said, To buy the threshingfloor of thee, to build an altar unto the LORD, that the plague may be stayed from the people.
original_text: And Araunah said, Wherefore is my lord the king come to his servant? And David said, To buy the threshingfloor of thee, to build an altar unto the LORD, that the plague may be stayed from the people.

translated_text:
And Araunah said unto David, Let my lord the king take and offer up what
seemeth good unto him: behold,
here be oxen for burnt sacrifice, and threshing instruments and
other instruments of the oxen for wood.
original_text:
And Araunah said unto David, Let my lord the king take and offer up what
seemeth good unto him: behold,
here be oxen for burnt sacrifice, and threshing instruments and
other instruments of the oxen for wood.

translated_text:
All
these things did Araunah,
as a king, give unto the king. And Araunah said unto the king, The LORD thy God accept thee.
original_text:
All
these things did Araunah,
as a king, give unto the king. And Araunah said unto the king, The LORD thy God accept thee.

translated_text:
And the king said unto Araunah, Nay; but I will surely buy
it
 of thee at a price: neither will I offer burnt offerings unto the LORD my God of that which doth cost me nothing. So David bought the threshingfloor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.
original_text:
And the king said unto Araunah, Nay; but I will surely buy
it
 of thee at a price: neither will I offer burnt offerings unto the LORD my God of that which doth cost me nothing. So David bought the threshingfloor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.

translated_text: And David built there an altar unto the LORD, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. So the LORD was intreated for the land, and the plague was stayed from Israel.
original_text: And David built there an altar unto the LORD, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. So the LORD was intreated for the land, and the plague was stayed from Israel.

translated_text:
Now these
be the last words of David. David the son of Jesse said, and the man
who was raised up on high, the anointed of the God of Jacob, and the sweet psalmist of Israel, said,
original_text:
Now these
be the last words of David. David the son of Jesse said, and the man
who was raised up on high, the anointed of the God of Jacob, and the sweet psalmist of Israel, said,

translated_text:
The Spirit of the LORD spake by me, and his word
was in my tongue.
original_text:
The Spirit of the LORD spake by me, and his word
was in my tongue.

translated_text:
The God of Israel said, the Rock of Israel spake to me, He that ruleth over men
must be just, ruling in the fear of God.
original_text:
The God of Israel said, the Rock of Israel spake to me, He that ruleth over men
must be just, ruling in the fear of God.

translated_text:
And
he shall be as the light of the morning,
when
 the sun riseth,
even a morning without clouds;
as
 the tender grass
springing out of the earth by clear shining after rain.
original_text:
And
he shall be as the light of the morning,
when
 the sun riseth,
even a morning without clouds;
as
 the tender grass
springing out of the earth by clear shining after rain.

translated_text:
Although my house
be not so with God; yet he hath made with me an everlasting covenant, ordered in all
things, and sure: for
this is all my salvation, and all
my desire, although he make
it not to grow.
original_text:
Although my house
be not so with God; yet he hath made with me an everlasting covenant, ordered in all
things, and sure: for
this is all my salvation, and all
my desire, although he make
it not to grow.

translated_text:
But
the sons of Belial
shall be all of them as thorns thrust away, because they cannot be taken with hands:
original_text:
But
the sons of Belial
shall be all of them as thorns thrust away, because they cannot be taken with hands:

translated_text:
But the man
that shall touch them must be fenced with iron and the staff of a spear; and they shall be utterly burned with fire in the
same place.
original_text:
But the man
that shall touch them must be fenced with iron and the staff of a spear; and they shall be utterly burned with fire in the
same place.

translated_text:
These
be the names of the mighty men whom David had: The Tachmonite that sat in the seat, chief among the captains; the same
was Adino the Eznite:
he lift up his spear against eight hundred, whom he slew at one time.
original_text:
These
be the names of the mighty men whom David had: The Tachmonite that sat in the seat, chief among the captains; the same
was Adino the Eznite:
he lift up his spear against eight hundred, whom he slew at one time.

translated_text:
And after him
was Eleazar the son of Dodo the Ahohite,
one of the three mighty men with David, when they defied the Philistines
that were there gathered together to battle, and the men of Israel were gone away:
original_text:
And after him
was Eleazar the son of Dodo the Ahohite,
one of the three mighty men with David, when they defied the Philistines
