translated_text: After these things, when the wrath of king Ahasuerus was appeased, he remembered Vashti, and what she had done, and what was decreed against her.
original_text: After these things, when the wrath of king Ahasuerus was appeased, he remembered Vashti, and what she had done, and what was decreed against her.

translated_text: Then said the king’s servants that ministered unto him, Let there be fair young virgins sought for the king:
original_text: Then said the king’s servants that ministered unto him, Let there be fair young virgins sought for the king:

translated_text:
And let the king appoint officers in all the provinces of his kingdom, that they may gather together all the fair young virgins unto Shushan the palace, to the house of the women unto the custody of Hege the king’s chamberlain, keeper of the women; and let their things for purification be given
them:
original_text:
And let the king appoint officers in all the provinces of his kingdom, that they may gather together all the fair young virgins unto Shushan the palace, to the house of the women unto the custody of Hege the king’s chamberlain, keeper of the women; and let their things for purification be given

translated_text: And let the maiden which pleaseth the king be queen instead of Vashti. And the thing pleased the king; and he did so.
original_text: And let the maiden which pleaseth the king be queen instead of Vashti. And the thing pleased the king; and he did so.

translated_text:
Now in Shushan the palace there was a certain Jew, whose name
was Mordecai, the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, a Benjamite;
original_text:
Now in Shushan the palace there was a certain Jew, whose name
was Mordecai, the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, a Benjamite;

translated_text: Who had been carried away from Jerusalem with the captivity which had been carried away with Jeconiah king of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon had carried away.
original_text: Who had been carried away from Jerusalem with the captivity which had been carried away with Jeconiah king of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon had carried away.

translated_text:
And he brought up Hadassah, that
is, Esther, his uncle’s daughter: for she had neither father nor mother, and the maid
was
 fair and beautiful; whom Mordecai, when her father and mother were dead, took for his own daughter.
original_text:
And he brought up Hadassah, that
is, Esther, his uncle’s daughter: for she had neither father nor mother, and the maid
was
 fair and beautiful; whom Mordecai, when her father and mother were dead, took for his own daughter.

translated_text: So it came to pass, when the king’s commandment and his decree was heard, and when many maidens were gathered together unto Shushan the palace, to the custody of Hegai, that Esther was brought also unto the king’s house, to the custody of Hegai, keeper of the women.

translated_text:
And the maiden pleased him, and she obtained kindness of him; and he speedily gave her her things for purification, with such things as belonged to her, and seven maidens,

place
 of the house of the women.
original_text:

place
 of the house of the women.

translated_text:
Esther had not shewed her people nor her kindred: for Mordecai had charged her that she should not shew
it.
original_text:
Esther had not shewed her people nor her kindred: for Mordecai had charged her that she should not shew

translated_text: And Mordecai walked every day before the court of the women’s house, to know how Esther did, and what should become of her.
original_text: And Mordecai walked every day before the court of the women’s house, to know how Esther did, and what should become of her.

translated_text:
Now when every maid’s turn was come to go in to king Ahasuerus, after that she had been twelve months, according to the manner of the women, (for so were the days of their purifications accomplished,

other things for the purifying of the women;)
original_text:

translated_text:
Then thus came

original_text:
Then thus came
every maiden unto the king; whatsoever she desired was given her to go with her out of the house of the women unto the king’s house.

translated_text: In the evening she went, and on the morrow she returned into the second house of the women, to the custody of Shaashgaz, the king’s chamberlain, which kept the concubines: she came in unto the king no more, except the king delighted in her, and that she were called by name.

translated_text: Now when the turn of Esther, the daughter of Abihail the uncle of Mordecai, who had taken her for his daughter, was come to go in unto the king, she required nothing but what Hegai the king’s chamberlain, the keeper of the women, appointed. translated_text:
So Esther was taken unto king Ahasuerus into his house royal in the tenth month, which
is the month Tebeth, in the seventh year of his reign.
original_text:
So Esther was taken unto king Ahasuerus into his house royal in the tenth month, which
is the month Tebeth, in the seventh year of his reign.

translated_text: And the king loved Esther above all the women, and she obtained grace and favour in his sight more than all the virgins; so that he set the royal crown upon her head, and made her queen instead of Vashti.
original_text: And the king loved Esther above all the women, and she obtained grace and favour in his sight more than all the virgins; so that he set the royal crown upon her head, and made her queen instead of Vashti.

translated_text:
Then the king made a great feast unto all his princes and his servants,
even Esther’s feast; and he made a release to the provinces, and gave gifts, according to the state of the king.
original_text:
Then the king made a great feast unto all his princes and his servants,
even Esther’s feast; and he made a release to the provinces, and gave gifts, according to the state of the king.

translated_text: And when the virgins were gathered together the second time, then Mordecai sat in the king’s gate.
original_text: And when the virgins were gathered together the second time, then Mordecai sat in the king’s gate.

translated_text:
Esther had not
yet shewed her kindred nor her people; as Mordecai had charged her: for Esther did the commandment of Mordecai, like as when she was brought up with him.
original_text:
Esther had not
yet shewed her kindred nor her people; as Mordecai had charged her: for Esther did the commandment of Mordecai, like as when she was brought up with him.

translated_text: In those days, while Mordecai sat in the king’s gate, two of the king’s chamberlains, Bigthan and Teresh, of those which kept the door, were wroth, and sought to lay hand on the king Ahasuerus.
original_text: In those days, while Mordecai sat in the king’s gate, two of the king’s chamberlains, Bigthan and Teresh, of those which kept the door, were wroth, and sought to lay hand on the king Ahasuerus.

translated_text:
And the thing was known to Mordecai, who told it unto Esther the queen; and Esther certified the king
thereof in Mordecai’s name.
original_text:
And the thing was known to Mordecai, who told it unto Esther the queen; and Esther certified the king
thereof in Mordecai’s name.

translated_text: And when inquisition was made of the matter, it was found out; therefore they were both hanged on a tree: and it was written in the book of the chronicles before the king.
original_text: And when inquisition was made of the matter, it was found out; therefore they were both hanged on a tree: and it was written in the book of the chronicles before the king.

translated_text:
After these things did king Ahasuerus promote Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, and advanced him, and set his seat above all the princes that
were with him.
original_text:
After these things did king Ahasuerus promote Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, and advanced him, and set his seat above all the princes that
were with him.

translated_text:
And all the king’s servants, that
were in the king’s gate, bowed, and reverenced Haman: for the king had so commanded concerning him. But Mordecai bowed not, nor did
him reverence.
original_text:
And all the king’s servants, that
were in the king’s gate, bowed, and reverenced Haman: for the king had so commanded concerning him. But Mordecai bowed not, nor did
him reverence.

translated_text:
Then the king’s servants, which
were in the king’s gate, said unto Mordecai, Why transgressest thou the king’s commandment?
original_text:
Then the king’s servants, which
were in the king’s gate, said unto Mordecai, Why transgressest thou the king’s commandment?

translated_text:
Now it came to pass, when they spake daily unto him, and he hearkened not unto them, that they told Haman, to see whether Mordecai’s matters would stand: for he had told them that he
was a Jew.
original_text:
Now it came to pass, when they spake daily unto him, and he hearkened not unto them, that they told Haman, to see whether Mordecai’s matters would stand: for he had told them that he
was a Jew.

translated_text: And when Haman saw that Mordecai bowed not, nor did him reverence, then was Haman full of wrath.
original_text: And when Haman saw that Mordecai bowed not, nor did him reverence, then was Haman full of wrath.

translated_text:
And he thought scorn to lay hands on Mordecai alone; for they had shewed him the people of Mordecai: wherefore Haman sought to destroy all the Jews that
were throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuerus,
even
 the people of Mordecai.
original_text:
And he thought scorn to lay hands on Mordecai alone; for they had shewed him the people of Mordecai: wherefore Haman sought to destroy all the Jews that
were throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuerus,
even
 the people of Mordecai.

translated_text:
In the first month, that
is, the month Nisan, in the twelfth year of king Ahasuerus, they cast Pur, that
is, the lot, before Haman from day to day, and from month to month,
to the twelfth
month, that
is, the month Adar.
original_text:
In the first month, that
is, the month Nisan, in the twelfth year of king Ahasuerus, they cast Pur, that
is, the lot, before Haman from day to day, and from month to month,
to the twelfth
month, that
is, the month Adar.

translated_text:
And Haman said unto king Ahasuerus, There is a certain people scattered abroad and dispersed among the people in all the provinces of thy kingdom; and their laws
are diverse from all people; neither keep they the king’s laws: therefore it
is not for the king’s profit to suffer them.
original_text:
And Haman said unto king Ahasuerus, There is a certain people scattered abroad and dispersed among the people in all the provinces of thy kingdom; and their laws
are diverse from all people; neither keep they the king’s laws: therefore it
is not for the king’s profit to suffer them.

translated_text:
If it please the king, let it be written that they may be destroyed: and I will pay ten thousand talents of silver to the hands of those that have the charge of the business, to bring
it into the king’s treasuries.
original_text:
If it please the king, let it be written that they may be destroyed: and I will pay ten thousand talents of silver to the hands of those that have the charge of the business, to bring
it into the king’s treasuries.

translated_text: And the king took his ring from his hand, and gave it unto Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the Jews’ enemy.
original_text: And the king took his ring from his hand, and gave it unto Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the Jews’ enemy.

translated_text:
And the king said unto Haman, The silver
is given to thee, the people also, to do with them as it seemeth good to thee.
original_text:
And the king said unto Haman, The silver
is given to thee, the people also, to do with them as it seemeth good to thee.

translated_text:
Then were the king’s scribes called on the thirteenth day of the first month, and there was written according to all that Haman had commanded unto the king’s lieutenants, and to the governors that
were over every province, and to the rulers of every people of every province according to the writing thereof, and
to every people after their language; in the name of king Ahasuerus was it written, and sealed with the king’s ring.
original_text:
Then were the king’s scribes called on the thirteenth day of the first month, and there was written according to all that Haman had commanded unto the king’s lieutenants, and to the governors that
were over every province, and to the rulers of every people of every province according to the writing thereof, and
to every people after their language; in the name of king Ahasuerus was it written, and sealed with the king’s ring.

translated_text:
And the letters were sent by posts into all the king’s provinces, to destroy, to kill, and to cause to perish, all Jews, both young and old, little children and women, in one day,
even upon the thirteenth
day
 of the twelfth month, which
is the month Adar, and
to take the spoil of them for a prey.
original_text:
And the letters were sent by posts into all the king’s provinces, to destroy, to kill, and to cause to perish, all Jews, both young and old, little children and women, in one day,
even upon the thirteenth
day
 of the twelfth month, which
is the month Adar, and
to take the spoil of them for a prey.

translated_text: The copy of the writing for a commandment to be given in every province was published unto all people, that they should be ready against that day.
original_text: The copy of the writing for a commandment to be given in every province was published unto all people, that they should be ready against that day.

translated_text: The posts went out, being hastened by the king’s commandment, and the decree was given in Shushan the palace. And the king and Haman sat down to drink; but the city Shushan was perplexed.
original_text: The posts went out, being hastened by the king’s commandment, and the decree was given in Shushan the palace. And the king and Haman sat down to drink; but the city Shushan was perplexed.

translated_text:
Now it came to pass in the days of Ahasuerus, (this
is Ahasuerus which reigned, from India even unto Ethiopia,
over an hundred and seven and twenty provinces:)
original_text:
Now it came to pass in the days of Ahasuerus, (this
is Ahasuerus which reigned, from India even unto Ethiopia,
over an hundred and seven and twenty provinces:)

translated_text:
That in those days, when the king Ahasuerus sat on the throne of his kingdom, which
was in Shushan the palace,
original_text:
That in those days, when the king Ahasuerus sat on the throne of his kingdom, which
was in Shushan the palace,

translated_text:
In the third year of his reign, he made a feast unto all his princes and his servants; the power of Persia and Media, the nobles and princes of the provinces,
being before him:
original_text:
In the third year of his reign, he made a feast unto all his princes and his servants; the power of Persia and Media, the nobles and princes of the provinces,
being before him:

translated_text:
When he shewed the riches of his glorious kingdom and the honour of his excellent majesty many days,
even an hundred and fourscore days.
original_text:
When he shewed the riches of his glorious kingdom and the honour of his excellent majesty many days,
even an hundred and fourscore days.

translated_text: And when these days were expired, the king made a feast unto all the people that were present in Shushan the palace, both unto great and small, seven days, in the court of the garden of the king’s palace;
original_text: And when these days were expired, the king made a feast unto all the people that were present in Shushan the palace, both unto great and small, seven days, in the court of the garden of the king’s palace;

translated_text:
Where were white, green, and blue,
hangings, fastened with cords of fine linen and purple to silver rings and pillars of marble: the beds
were of gold and silver, upon a pavement of red, and blue, and white, and black, marble.
original_text:
Where were white, green, and blue,
hangings, fastened with cords of fine linen and purple to silver rings and pillars of marble: the beds
were of gold and silver, upon a pavement of red, and blue, and white, and black, marble.

translated_text:
And they gave
them drink in vessels of gold, (the vessels being diverse one from another,) and royal wine in abundance, according to the state of the king.
original_text:
And they gave
them drink in vessels of gold, (the vessels being diverse one from another,) and royal wine in abundance, according to the state of the king.

translated_text:
And the drinking
was according to the law; none did compel: for so the king had appointed to all the officers of his house, that they should do according to every man’s pleasure.
original_text:
And the drinking
was according to the law; none did compel: for so the king had appointed to all the officers of his house, that they should do according to every man’s pleasure.

translated_text:
Also Vashti the queen made a feast for the women
in the royal house which
belonged to king Ahasuerus.
original_text:
Also Vashti the queen made a feast for the women
in the royal house which
belonged to king Ahasuerus.

translated_text: On the seventh day, when the heart of the king was merry with wine, he commanded Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, and Abagtha, Zethar, and Carcas, the seven chamberlains that served in the presence of Ahasuerus the king,
original_text: On the seventh day, when the heart of the king was merry with wine, he commanded Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, and Abagtha, Zethar, and Carcas, the seven chamberlains that served in the presence of Ahasuerus the king,

translated_text:
To bring Vashti the queen before the king with the crown royal, to shew the people and the princes her beauty: for she
was fair to look on.
original_text:
To bring Vashti the queen before the king with the crown royal, to shew the people and the princes her beauty: for she
was fair to look on.

translated_text:
But the queen Vashti refused to come at the king’s commandment by
his chamberlains: therefore was the king very wroth, and his anger burned in him.
original_text:
But the queen Vashti refused to come at the king’s commandment by
his chamberlains: therefore was the king very wroth, and his anger burned in him.

translated_text:
Then the king said to the wise men, which knew the times, (for so
was the king’s manner toward all that knew law and judgment:
original_text:
Then the king said to the wise men, which knew the times, (for so
was the king’s manner toward all that knew law and judgment:

translated_text:
And the next unto him
was Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena,
and Memucan, the seven princes of Persia and Media, which saw the king’s face,
and which sat the first in the kingdom;)
original_text:
And the next unto him
was Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena,
and Memucan, the seven princes of Persia and Media, which saw the king’s face,
and which sat the first in the kingdom;)

translated_text: What shall we do unto the queen Vashti according to law, because she hath not performed the commandment of the king Ahasuerus by the chamberlains?
original_text: What shall we do unto the queen Vashti according to law, because she hath not performed the commandment of the king Ahasuerus by the chamberlains?

translated_text:
And Memucan answered before the king and the princes, Vashti the queen hath not done wrong to the king only, but also to all the princes, and to all the people that
are in all the provinces of the king Ahasuerus.
original_text:
And Memucan answered before the king and the princes, Vashti the queen hath not done wrong to the king only, but also to all the princes, and to all the people that
are in all the provinces of the king Ahasuerus.

translated_text:
For
this deed of the queen shall come abroad unto all women, so that they shall despise their husbands in their eyes, when it shall be reported, The king Ahasuerus commanded Vashti the queen to be brought in before him, but she came not.
original_text:
For
this deed of the queen shall come abroad unto all women, so that they shall despise their husbands in their eyes, when it shall be reported, The king Ahasuerus commanded Vashti the queen to be brought in before him, but she came not.

translated_text:
Likewise shall the ladies of Persia and Media say this day unto all the king’s princes, which have heard of the deed of the queen. Thus
shall there arise too much contempt and wrath.
original_text:
Likewise shall the ladies of Persia and Media say this day unto all the king’s princes, which have heard of the deed of the queen. Thus
shall there arise too much contempt and wrath.

translated_text: If it please the king, let there go a royal commandment from him, and let it be written among the laws of the Persians and the Medes, that it be not altered, That Vashti come no more before king Ahasuerus; and let the king give her royal estate unto another that is better than she.
original_text: If it please the king, let there go a royal commandment from him, and let it be written among the laws of the Persians and the Medes, that it be not altered, That Vashti come no more before king Ahasuerus; and let the king give her royal estate unto another that is better than she.

translated_text: And when the king’s decree which he shall make shall be published throughout all his empire, (for it is great,) all the wives shall give to their husbands honour, both to great and small.
original_text: And when the king’s decree which he shall make shall be published throughout all his empire, (for it is great,) all the wives shall give to their husbands honour, both to great and small.

translated_text: And the saying pleased the king and the princes; and the king did according to the word of Memucan:
original_text: And the saying pleased the king and the princes; and the king did according to the word of Memucan:

translated_text:
For he sent letters into all the king’s provinces, into every province according to the writing thereof, and to every people after their language, that every man should bear rule in his own house, and that
it should be published according to the language of every people.
original_text:
For he sent letters into all the king’s provinces, into every province according to the writing thereof, and to every people after their language, that every man should bear rule in his own house, and that
it should be published according to the language of every people.

translated_text:
Knowest thou the time when the wild goats of the rock bring forth?
or canst thou mark when the hinds do calve?
original_text:
Knowest thou the time when the wild goats of the rock bring forth?
or canst thou mark when the hinds do calve?

translated_text:
Canst thou number the months
that they fulfil? or knowest thou the time when they bring forth?
original_text:
Canst thou number the months
that they fulfil? or knowest thou the time when they bring forth?

translated_text: They bow themselves, they bring forth their young ones, they cast out their sorrows.
original_text: They bow themselves, they bring forth their young ones, they cast out their sorrows.

translated_text: Their young ones are in good liking, they grow up with corn; they go forth, and return not unto them.
original_text: Their young ones are in good liking, they grow up with corn; they go forth, and return not unto them.

translated_text: Who hath sent out the wild ass free? or who hath loosed the bands of the wild ass?
original_text: Who hath sent out the wild ass free? or who hath loosed the bands of the wild ass?

translated_text: Whose house I have made the wilderness, and the barren land his dwellings.
original_text: Whose house I have made the wilderness, and the barren land his dwellings.

translated_text: He scorneth the multitude of the city, neither regardeth he the crying of the driver.
original_text: He scorneth the multitude of the city, neither regardeth he the crying of the driver.

translated_text:
The range of the mountains
is his pasture, and he searcheth after every green thing.
original_text:
The range of the mountains
is his pasture, and he searcheth after every green thing.

translated_text: Will the unicorn be willing to serve thee, or abide by thy crib?
original_text: Will the unicorn be willing to serve thee, or abide by thy crib?

translated_text: Canst thou bind the unicorn with his band in the furrow? or will he harrow the valleys after thee?
original_text: Canst thou bind the unicorn with his band in the furrow? or will he harrow the valleys after thee?

translated_text:
Wilt thou trust him, because his strength
is great? or wilt thou leave thy labour to him?
original_text:
Wilt thou trust him, because his strength
is great? or wilt thou leave thy labour to him?

translated_text:
Wilt thou believe him, that he will bring home thy seed, and gather
it into thy barn?
original_text:
Wilt thou believe him, that he will bring home thy seed, and gather
it into thy barn?

translated_text: Gavest thou the goodly wings unto the peacocks? or wings and feathers unto the ostrich?
original_text: Gavest thou the goodly wings unto the peacocks? or wings and feathers unto the ostrich?

translated_text: Which leaveth her eggs in the earth, and warmeth them in dust,
original_text: Which leaveth her eggs in the earth, and warmeth them in dust,

translated_text: And forgetteth that the foot may crush them, or that the wild beast may break them.
original_text: And forgetteth that the foot may crush them, or that the wild beast may break them.

translated_text: Because God hath deprived her of wisdom, neither hath he imparted to her understanding.
original_text: Because God hath deprived her of wisdom, neither hath he imparted to her understanding.

translated_text: What time she lifteth up herself on high, she scorneth the horse and his rider.
original_text: What time she lifteth up herself on high, she scorneth the horse and his rider.

translated_text: Hath thou given the horse strength? hast thou clothed his neck with thunder?
original_text: Hath thou given the horse strength? hast thou clothed his neck with thunder?

translated_text:
Canst thou make him afraid as a grasshopper? the glory of his nostrils
is terrible.
original_text:
Canst thou make him afraid as a grasshopper? the glory of his nostrils
is terrible.

translated_text:
He paweth in the valley, and rejoiceth in
his strength: he goeth on to meet the armed men.
original_text:
He paweth in the valley, and rejoiceth in
his strength: he goeth on to meet the armed men.

translated_text: He mocketh at fear, and is not affrighted; neither turneth he back from the sword.
original_text: He mocketh at fear, and is not affrighted; neither turneth he back from the sword.

translated_text: The quiver rattleth against him, the glittering spear and the shield.
original_text: The quiver rattleth against him, the glittering spear and the shield.

translated_text:
He swalloweth the ground with fierceness and rage: neither believeth he that
it is the sound of the trumpet.
original_text:
He swalloweth the ground with fierceness and rage: neither believeth he that
it is the sound of the trumpet.

translated_text: He saith among the trumpets, Ha, ha; and he smelleth the battle afar off, the thunder of the captains, and the shouting.
original_text: He saith among the trumpets, Ha, ha; and he smelleth the battle afar off, the thunder of the captains, and the shouting.

translated_text:
Doth the hawk fly by thy wisdom,
and stretch her wings toward the south?
original_text:
Doth the hawk fly by thy wisdom,
and stretch her wings toward the south?

translated_text: Doth the eagle mount up at thy command, and make her nest on high?
original_text: Doth the eagle mount up at thy command, and make her nest on high?

translated_text: She dwelleth and abideth on the rock, upon the crag of the rock, and the strong place.
original_text: She dwelleth and abideth on the rock, upon the crag of the rock, and the strong place.

translated_text:
From thence she seeketh the prey,
and her eyes behold afar off.
original_text:
From thence she seeketh the prey,
and her eyes behold afar off.

translated_text:
Her young ones also suck up blood: and where the slain
are,
 there
is she.
original_text:
Her young ones also suck up blood: and where the slain
are,
 there
is she.

translated_text: Furthermore Elihu answered and said,
original_text: Furthermore Elihu answered and said,

translated_text:
Hear my words, O ye wise
men; and give ear unto me, ye that have knowledge.
original_text:
Hear my words, O ye wise
men; and give ear unto me, ye that have knowledge.

translated_text: For the ear trieth words, as the mouth tasteth meat.
original_text: For the ear trieth words, as the mouth tasteth meat.

translated_text:
Let us choose to us judgment: let us know among ourselves what
is good.
original_text:
Let us choose to us judgment: let us know among ourselves what
is good.

translated_text: For Job hath said, I am righteous: and God hath taken away my judgment.
original_text: For Job hath said, I am righteous: and God hath taken away my judgment.

translated_text:
Should I lie against my right? my wound
is incurable without transgression.
original_text:
Should I lie against my right? my wound
is incurable without transgression.

translated_text:
What man
is like Job,
who drinketh up scorning like water?
original_text:
What man
is like Job,
who drinketh up scorning like water?

translated_text: Which goeth in company with the workers of iniquity, and walketh with wicked men.
original_text: Which goeth in company with the workers of iniquity, and walketh with wicked men.

translated_text: For he hath said, It profiteth a man nothing that he should delight himself with God.
original_text: For he hath said, It profiteth a man nothing that he should delight himself with God.

translated_text:
Therefore hearken unto me, ye men of understanding: far be it from God,
that he should do wickedness; and
from the Almighty,
that he should commit iniquity.
original_text:
Therefore hearken unto me, ye men of understanding: far be it from God,
that he should do wickedness; and
from the Almighty,
that he should commit iniquity.

translated_text:
For the work of a man shall he render unto him, and cause every man to find according to
his ways.
original_text:
For the work of a man shall he render unto him, and cause every man to find according to
his ways.

translated_text: Yea, surely God will not do wickedly, neither will the Almighty pervert judgment.
original_text: Yea, surely God will not do wickedly, neither will the Almighty pervert judgment.

translated_text: Who hath given him a charge over the earth? or who hath disposed the whole world?
original_text: Who hath given him a charge over the earth? or who hath disposed the whole world?

translated_text:
If he set his heart upon man,
if he gather unto himself his spirit and his breath;
original_text:
If he set his heart upon man,
if he gather unto himself his spirit and his breath;

translated_text: All flesh shall perish together, and man shall turn again unto dust.
original_text: All flesh shall perish together, and man shall turn again unto dust.

translated_text:
If now
thou hast understanding, hear this: hearken to the voice of my words.
original_text:
If now
thou hast understanding, hear this: hearken to the voice of my words.

translated_text: Shall even he that hateth right govern? and wilt thou condemn him that is most just?
original_text: Shall even he that hateth right govern? and wilt thou condemn him that is most just?

translated_text:
Is it fit to say to a king,
Thou art wicked?
and to princes,
Ye are ungodly?
original_text:
Is it fit to say to a king,
Thou art wicked?
and to princes,
Ye are ungodly?

translated_text:
How much less to him that accepteth not the persons of princes, nor regardeth the rich more than the poor? for they all
are
 the work of his hands.
original_text:
How much less to him that accepteth not the persons of princes, nor regardeth the rich more than the poor? for they all
are
 the work of his hands.

translated_text: In a moment shall they die, and the people shall be troubled at midnight, and pass away: and the mighty shall be taken away without hand.
original_text: In a moment shall they die, and the people shall be troubled at midnight, and pass away: and the mighty shall be taken away without hand.

translated_text:
For his eyes
are upon the ways of man, and he seeth all his goings.
original_text:
For his eyes
are upon the ways of man, and he seeth all his goings.

translated_text: There is no darkness, nor shadow of death, where the workers of iniquity may hide themselves.
original_text: There is no darkness, nor shadow of death, where the workers of iniquity may hide themselves.

translated_text:
For he will not lay upon man more
than right; that he should enter into judgment with God.
original_text:
For he will not lay upon man more
than right; that he should enter into judgment with God.

translated_text: He shall break in pieces mighty men without number, and set others in their stead.
original_text: He shall break in pieces mighty men without number, and set others in their stead.

translated_text:
Therefore he knoweth their works, and he overturneth
them
 in the night, so that they are destroyed.
original_text:
Therefore he knoweth their works, and he overturneth
them
 in the night, so that they are destroyed.

translated_text: He striketh them as wicked men in the open sight of others;
original_text: He striketh them as wicked men in the open sight of others;

translated_text: Because they turned back from him, and would not consider any of his ways:
original_text: Because they turned back from him, and would not consider any of his ways:

translated_text: So that they cause the cry of the poor to come unto him, and he heareth the cry of the afflicted.
original_text: So that they cause the cry of the poor to come unto him, and he heareth the cry of the afflicted.

translated_text:
When he giveth quietness, who then can make trouble? and when he hideth
his face, who then can behold him? whether
it be done
 against a nation, or against a man only:
original_text:
When he giveth quietness, who then can make trouble? and when he hideth
his face, who then can behold him? whether
it be done
 against a nation, or against a man only:

translated_text: That the hypocrite reign not, lest the people be ensnared.
original_text: That the hypocrite reign not, lest the people be ensnared.

translated_text:
Surely it is meet to be said unto God, I have borne
chastisement,
 I will not offend
any more:
original_text:
Surely it is meet to be said unto God, I have borne
chastisement,
 I will not offend
any more:

translated_text: That which I see not teach thou me: if I have done iniquity, I will do no more.
original_text: That which I see not teach thou me: if I have done iniquity, I will do no more.

translated_text: Should it be according to thy mind? he will recompense it, whether thou refuse, or whether thou choose; and not I: therefore speak what thou knowest.
original_text: Should it be according to thy mind? he will recompense it, whether thou refuse, or whether thou choose; and not I: therefore speak what thou knowest.

translated_text: Let men of understanding tell me, and let a wise man hearken unto me.
original_text: Let men of understanding tell me, and let a wise man hearken unto me.

translated_text:
Job hath spoken without knowledge, and his words
were without wisdom.
original_text:
Job hath spoken without knowledge, and his words
were without wisdom.

translated_text:
My desire
is that Job may be tried unto the end because of
his answers for wicked men.
original_text:
My desire
is that Job may be tried unto the end because of
his answers for wicked men.

translated_text:
For he addeth rebellion unto his sin, he clappeth
his hands
 among us, and multiplieth his words against God.
original_text:
For he addeth rebellion unto his sin, he clappeth
his hands
 among us, and multiplieth his words against God.

translated_text: Wherefore, Job, I pray thee, hear my speeches, and hearken to all my words.
original_text: Wherefore, Job, I pray thee, hear my speeches, and hearken to all my words.

translated_text: Behold, now I have opened my mouth, my tongue hath spoken in my mouth.
original_text: Behold, now I have opened my mouth, my tongue hath spoken in my mouth.

translated_text:
My words
shall be of the uprightness of my heart: and my lips shall utter knowledge clearly.
original_text:
My words
shall be of the uprightness of my heart: and my lips shall utter knowledge clearly.

translated_text: The Spirit of God hath made me, and the breath of the Almighty hath given me life.
original_text: The Spirit of God hath made me, and the breath of the Almighty hath given me life.

translated_text:
If thou canst answer me, set
thy words in order before me, stand up.
original_text:
If thou canst answer me, set
thy words in order before me, stand up.

translated_text:
Behold, I
am according to thy wish in God’s stead: I also am formed out of the clay.
original_text:
Behold, I
am according to thy wish in God’s stead: I also am formed out of the clay.

translated_text: Behold, my terror shall not make thee afraid, neither shall my hand be heavy upon thee.
original_text: Behold, my terror shall not make thee afraid, neither shall my hand be heavy upon thee.

translated_text:
Surely thou hast spoken in mine hearing, and I have heard the voice of
thy words,
saying,
original_text:
Surely thou hast spoken in mine hearing, and I have heard the voice of
thy words,
saying,

translated_text:
I am clean without transgression, I
am innocent; neither
is there iniquity in me.
original_text:
I am clean without transgression, I
am innocent; neither
is there iniquity in me.

translated_text: Behold, he findeth occasions against me, he counteth me for his enemy,
original_text: Behold, he findeth occasions against me, he counteth me for his enemy,

translated_text: He putteth my feet in the stocks, he marketh all my paths.
original_text: He putteth my feet in the stocks, he marketh all my paths.

translated_text:
Behold,
in this thou art not just: I will answer thee, that God is greater than man.
original_text:
Behold,
in this thou art not just: I will answer thee, that God is greater than man.

translated_text: Why dost thou strive against him? for he giveth not account of any of his matters.
original_text: Why dost thou strive against him? for he giveth not account of any of his matters.

translated_text:
For God speaketh once, yea twice,
yet man perceiveth it not.
original_text:
For God speaketh once, yea twice,
yet man perceiveth it not.

translated_text: In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falleth upon men, in slumberings upon the bed;
original_text: In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falleth upon men, in slumberings upon the bed;

translated_text: Then he openeth the ears of men, and sealeth their instruction,
original_text: Then he openeth the ears of men, and sealeth their instruction,

translated_text:
That he may withdraw man
from his purpose, and hide pride from man.
original_text:
That he may withdraw man
from his purpose, and hide pride from man.

translated_text: He keepeth back his soul from the pit, and his life from perishing by the sword.
original_text: He keepeth back his soul from the pit, and his life from perishing by the sword.

translated_text:
He is chastened also with pain upon his bed, and the multitude of his bones with strong
pain:
original_text:
He is chastened also with pain upon his bed, and the multitude of his bones with strong
pain:

translated_text: So that his life abhorreth bread, and his soul dainty meat.
original_text: So that his life abhorreth bread, and his soul dainty meat.

translated_text:
His flesh is consumed away, that it cannot be seen; and his bones
that were not seen stick out.
original_text:
His flesh is consumed away, that it cannot be seen; and his bones
that were not seen stick out.

translated_text: Yea, his soul draweth near unto the grave, and his life to the destroyers.
original_text: Yea, his soul draweth near unto the grave, and his life to the destroyers.

translated_text: If there be a messenger with him, an interpreter, one among a thousand, to shew unto man his uprightness:
original_text: If there be a messenger with him, an interpreter, one among a thousand, to shew unto man his uprightness:

translated_text: Then he is gracious unto him, and saith, Deliver him from going down to the pit: I have found a ransom.
original_text: Then he is gracious unto him, and saith, Deliver him from going down to the pit: I have found a ransom.

translated_text: His flesh shall be fresher than a child’s: he shall return to the days of his youth:
original_text: His flesh shall be fresher than a child’s: he shall return to the days of his youth:

translated_text: He shall pray unto God, and he will be favourable unto him: and he shall see his face with joy: for he will render unto man his righteousness.
original_text: He shall pray unto God, and he will be favourable unto him: and he shall see his face with joy: for he will render unto man his righteousness.

translated_text: He will deliver his soul from going into the pit, and his life shall see the light.
original_text: He will deliver his soul from going into the pit, and his life shall see the light.

translated_text:
Lo, all these
things worketh God oftentimes with man,
original_text:
Lo, all these
things worketh God oftentimes with man,

translated_text: To bring back his soul from the pit, to be enlightened with the light of the living.
original_text: To bring back his soul from the pit, to be enlightened with the light of the living.

translated_text: Mark well, O Job, hearken unto me: hold thy peace, and I will speak.
original_text: Mark well, O Job, hearken unto me: hold thy peace, and I will speak.

translated_text: If thou hast any thing to say, answer me: speak, for I desire to justify thee.
original_text: If thou hast any thing to say, answer me: speak, for I desire to justify thee.

translated_text: If not, hearken unto me: hold thy peace, and I shall teach thee wisdom.
original_text: If not, hearken unto me: hold thy peace, and I shall teach thee wisdom.

translated_text:
So these three men ceased to answer Job, because he
was righteous in his own eyes.
original_text:
So these three men ceased to answer Job, because he
was righteous in his own eyes.

translated_text: Then was kindled the wrath of Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the kindred of Ram: against Job was his wrath kindled, because he justified himself rather than God.
original_text: Then was kindled the wrath of Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the kindred of Ram: against Job was his wrath kindled, because he justified himself rather than God.

translated_text: Also against his three friends was his wrath kindled, because they had found no answer, and yet had condemned Job.
original_text: Also against his three friends was his wrath kindled, because they had found no answer, and yet had condemned Job.

translated_text: Now Elihu had waited till Job had spoken, because they were elder than he.
original_text: Now Elihu had waited till Job had spoken, because they were elder than he.

translated_text:
When Elihu saw that
there was no answer in the mouth of
these three men, then his wrath was kindled.
original_text:
When Elihu saw that
there was no answer in the mouth of
these three men, then his wrath was kindled.

translated_text:
And Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said, I
am
 young, and ye
are very old; wherefore I was afraid, and durst not shew you mine opinion.
original_text:
And Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said, I
am
 young, and ye
are very old; wherefore I was afraid, and durst not shew you mine opinion.

translated_text: I said, Days should speak, and multitude of years should teach wisdom.
original_text: I said, Days should speak, and multitude of years should teach wisdom.

translated_text:
But
there is a spirit in man: and the inspiration of the Almighty giveth them understanding.
original_text:
But
there is a spirit in man: and the inspiration of the Almighty giveth them understanding.

translated_text:
Great men are not
always wise: neither do the aged understand judgment.
original_text:
Great men are not
always wise: neither do the aged understand judgment.

translated_text: Therefore I said, Hearken to me; I also will shew mine opinion.
original_text: Therefore I said, Hearken to me; I also will shew mine opinion.

translated_text: Behold, I waited for your words; I gave ear to your reasons, whilst ye searched out what to say.
original_text: Behold, I waited for your words; I gave ear to your reasons, whilst ye searched out what to say.

translated_text:
Yea, I attended unto you, and, behold,
there was none of you that convinced Job, or that answered his words:
original_text:
Yea, I attended unto you, and, behold,
there was none of you that convinced Job, or that answered his words:

translated_text: Lest ye should say, We have found out wisdom: God thrusteth him down, not man.
original_text: Lest ye should say, We have found out wisdom: God thrusteth him down, not man.

translated_text:
Now he hath not directed
his words against me: neither will I answer him with your speeches.
original_text:
Now he hath not directed
his words against me: neither will I answer him with your speeches.

translated_text: They were amazed, they answered no more: they left off speaking.
original_text: They were amazed, they answered no more: they left off speaking.

translated_text:
When I had waited, (for they spake not, but stood still,
and
 answered no more;)
original_text:
When I had waited, (for they spake not, but stood still,
and
 answered no more;)

translated_text: I said, I will answer also my part, I also will shew mine opinion.
original_text: I said, I will answer also my part, I also will shew mine opinion.

translated_text: For I am full of matter, the spirit within me constraineth me.
original_text: For I am full of matter, the spirit within me constraineth me.

translated_text:
Behold, my belly
is as wine
which hath no vent; it is ready to burst like new bottles.
original_text:
Behold, my belly
is as wine
which hath no vent; it is ready to burst like new bottles.

translated_text: I will speak, that I may be refreshed: I will open my lips and answer.
original_text: I will speak, that I may be refreshed: I will open my lips and answer.

translated_text: Let me not, I pray you, accept any man’s person, neither let me give flattering titles unto man.
original_text: Let me not, I pray you, accept any man’s person, neither let me give flattering titles unto man.

translated_text:
For I know not to give flattering titles;
in so doing my maker would soon take me away.
original_text:
For I know not to give flattering titles;
in so doing my maker would soon take me away.

translated_text: I made a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid?
original_text: I made a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid?

translated_text:
For what portion of God
is there from above? and
what
 inheritance of the Almighty from on high?
original_text:
For what portion of God
is there from above? and
what
 inheritance of the Almighty from on high?

translated_text:
Is not destruction to the wicked? and a strange
punishment
 to the workers of iniquity?
original_text:
Is not destruction to the wicked? and a strange
punishment
 to the workers of iniquity?

translated_text: Doth not he see my ways, and count all my steps?
original_text: Doth not he see my ways, and count all my steps?

translated_text: If I have walked with vanity, or if my foot hath hasted to deceit;
original_text: If I have walked with vanity, or if my foot hath hasted to deceit;

translated_text: Let me be weighed in an even balance, that God may know mine integrity.
original_text: Let me be weighed in an even balance, that God may know mine integrity.

translated_text: If my step hath turned out of the way, and mine heart walked after mine eyes, and if any blot hath cleaved to mine hands;
original_text: If my step hath turned out of the way, and mine heart walked after mine eyes, and if any blot hath cleaved to mine hands;

translated_text: Then let me sow, and let another eat; yea, let my offspring be rooted out.
original_text: Then let me sow, and let another eat; yea, let my offspring be rooted out.

translated_text:
If mine heart have been deceived by a woman, or
if I have laid wait at my neighbour’s door;
original_text:
If mine heart have been deceived by a woman, or
if I have laid wait at my neighbour’s door;

translated_text: Then let my wife grind unto another, and let others bow down upon her.
original_text: Then let my wife grind unto another, and let others bow down upon her.

translated_text:
For this
is an heinous crime; yea, it
is an iniquity
to be punished by the judges.
original_text:
For this
is an heinous crime; yea, it
is an iniquity
to be punished by the judges.

translated_text:
For it
is a fire
that consumeth to destruction, and would root out all mine increase.
original_text:
For it
is a fire
that consumeth to destruction, and would root out all mine increase.

translated_text: If I did despise the cause of my manservant or of my maidservant, when they contended with me;
original_text: If I did despise the cause of my manservant or of my maidservant, when they contended with me;

translated_text: What then shall I do when God riseth up? and when he visiteth, what shall I answer him?
original_text: What then shall I do when God riseth up? and when he visiteth, what shall I answer him?

translated_text: Did not he that made me in the womb make him? and did not one fashion us in the womb?
original_text: Did not he that made me in the womb make him? and did not one fashion us in the womb?

translated_text:
If I have withheld the poor from
their desire, or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail;
original_text:
If I have withheld the poor from
their desire, or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail;

translated_text: Or have eaten my morsel myself alone, and the fatherless hath not eaten thereof;
original_text: Or have eaten my morsel myself alone, and the fatherless hath not eaten thereof;

translated_text:
(For from my youth he was brought up with me, as
with a father, and I have guided her from my mother’s womb;)
original_text:
(For from my youth he was brought up with me, as
with a father, and I have guided her from my mother’s womb;)

translated_text: If I have seen any perish for want of clothing, or any poor without covering;
original_text: If I have seen any perish for want of clothing, or any poor without covering;

translated_text:
If his loins have not blessed me, and
if he were
not
 warmed with the fleece of my sheep;
original_text:
If his loins have not blessed me, and
if he were
not
 warmed with the fleece of my sheep;

translated_text: If I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless, when I saw my help in the gate:
original_text: If I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless, when I saw my help in the gate:

translated_text: Then let mine arm fall from my shoulder blade, and mine arm be broken from the bone.
original_text: Then let mine arm fall from my shoulder blade, and mine arm be broken from the bone.

translated_text:
For destruction
from God
was a terror to me, and by reason of his highness I could not endure.
original_text:
For destruction
from God
was a terror to me, and by reason of his highness I could not endure.

translated_text:
If I have made gold my hope, or have said to the fine gold,
Thou art my confidence;
original_text:
If I have made gold my hope, or have said to the fine gold,
Thou art my confidence;

translated_text:
If I rejoiced because my wealth
was great, and because mine hand had gotten much;
original_text:
If I rejoiced because my wealth
was great, and because mine hand had gotten much;

translated_text: And my heart hath been secretly enticed, or my mouth hath kissed my hand:
original_text: And my heart hath been secretly enticed, or my mouth hath kissed my hand:

translated_text:
This also
were an iniquity
to be punished by the judge: for I should have denied the God
that is above.
original_text:
This also
were an iniquity
to be punished by the judge: for I should have denied the God
that is above.

translated_text: If I rejoiced at the destruction of him that hated me, or lifted up myself when evil found him:
original_text: If I rejoiced at the destruction of him that hated me, or lifted up myself when evil found him:

translated_text: Neither have I suffered my mouth to sin by wishing a curse to his soul.
original_text: Neither have I suffered my mouth to sin by wishing a curse to his soul.

translated_text: If the men of my tabernacle said not, Oh that we had of his flesh! we cannot be satisfied.
original_text: If the men of my tabernacle said not, Oh that we had of his flesh! we cannot be satisfied.

translated_text:
The stranger did not lodge in the street:
but I opened my doors to the traveller.
original_text:
The stranger did not lodge in the street:
but I opened my doors to the traveller.

translated_text: If I covered my transgressions as Adam, by hiding mine iniquity in my bosom:
original_text: If I covered my transgressions as Adam, by hiding mine iniquity in my bosom:

translated_text:
Did I fear a great multitude, or did the contempt of families terrify me, that I kept silence,
and went not out of the door?
original_text:
Did I fear a great multitude, or did the contempt of families terrify me, that I kept silence,
and went not out of the door?

translated_text:
Oh that one would hear me! behold, my desire
is, that the Almighty would answer me, and
that mine adversary had written a book.
original_text:
Oh that one would hear me! behold, my desire
is, that the Almighty would answer me, and
that mine adversary had written a book.

translated_text:
Surely I would take it upon my shoulder,
and bind it
as a crown to me.
original_text:
Surely I would take it upon my shoulder,
and bind it
as a crown to me.

translated_text: I would declare unto him the number of my steps; as a prince would I go near unto him.
original_text: I would declare unto him the number of my steps; as a prince would I go near unto him.

translated_text: If my land cry against me, or that the furrows likewise thereof complain;
original_text: If my land cry against me, or that the furrows likewise thereof complain;

translated_text: If I have eaten the fruits thereof without money, or have caused the owners thereof to lose their life:
original_text: If I have eaten the fruits thereof without money, or have caused the owners thereof to lose their life:

translated_text: Let thistles grow instead of wheat, and cockle instead of barley. The words of Job are ended.
original_text: Let thistles grow instead of wheat, and cockle instead of barley. The words of Job are ended.

translated_text: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind, and said,
original_text: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind, and said,

translated_text:
Who
is this that darkeneth counsel by words without knowledge?
original_text:
Who
is this that darkeneth counsel by words without knowledge?

translated_text: Gird up now thy loins like a man; for I will demand of thee, and answer thou me.
original_text: Gird up now thy loins like a man; for I will demand of thee, and answer thou me.

translated_text: Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? declare, if thou hast understanding.
original_text: Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? declare, if thou hast understanding.

translated_text: Who hath laid the measures thereof, if thou knowest? or who hath stretched the line upon it?
original_text: Who hath laid the measures thereof, if thou knowest? or who hath stretched the line upon it?

translated_text: Whereupon are the foundations thereof fastened? or who laid the corner stone thereof;
original_text: Whereupon are the foundations thereof fastened? or who laid the corner stone thereof;

translated_text: When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
original_text: When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?

translated_text:
Or
who shut up the sea with doors, when it brake forth,
as if it had issued out of the womb?
original_text:
Or
who shut up the sea with doors, when it brake forth,
as if it had issued out of the womb?

translated_text: When I made the cloud the garment thereof, and thick darkness a swaddlingband for it,
original_text: When I made the cloud the garment thereof, and thick darkness a swaddlingband for it,

translated_text:
And brake up for it my decreed
place, and set bars and doors,
original_text:
And brake up for it my decreed
place, and set bars and doors,

translated_text: And said, Hitherto shalt thou come, but no further: and here shall thy proud waves be stayed?
original_text: And said, Hitherto shalt thou come, but no further: and here shall thy proud waves be stayed?

translated_text:
Hast thou commanded the morning since thy days;
and caused the dayspring to know his place;
original_text:
Hast thou commanded the morning since thy days;
and caused the dayspring to know his place;

translated_text: That it might take hold of the ends of the earth, that the wicked might be shaken out of it?
original_text: That it might take hold of the ends of the earth, that the wicked might be shaken out of it?

translated_text:
It is turned as clay
to the seal; and they stand as a garment.
original_text:
It is turned as clay
to the seal; and they stand as a garment.

translated_text: And from the wicked their light is withholden, and the high arm shall be broken.
original_text: And from the wicked their light is withholden, and the high arm shall be broken.

translated_text: Hast thou entered into the springs of the sea? or hast thou walked in the search of the depth?
original_text: Hast thou entered into the springs of the sea? or hast thou walked in the search of the depth?

translated_text: Have the gates of death been opened unto thee? or hast thou seen the doors of the shadow of death?
original_text: Have the gates of death been opened unto thee? or hast thou seen the doors of the shadow of death?

translated_text: Hast thou perceived the breadth of the earth? declare if thou knowest it all.
original_text: Hast thou perceived the breadth of the earth? declare if thou knowest it all.

translated_text:
Where
is the way
where light dwelleth? and
as for darkness, where
is the place thereof,
original_text:
Where
is the way
where light dwelleth? and
as for darkness, where
is the place thereof,

translated_text:
That thou shouldest take it to the bound thereof, and that thou shouldest know the paths
to the house thereof?
original_text:
That thou shouldest take it to the bound thereof, and that thou shouldest know the paths
to the house thereof?

translated_text:
Knowest thou
it, because thou wast then born? or
because
 the number of thy days
is great?
original_text:
Knowest thou
it, because thou wast then born? or
because
 the number of thy days
is great?

translated_text: Hast thou entered into the treasures of the snow? or hast thou seen the treasures of the hail,
original_text: Hast thou entered into the treasures of the snow? or hast thou seen the treasures of the hail,

translated_text: Which I have reserved against the time of trouble, against the day of battle and war?
original_text: Which I have reserved against the time of trouble, against the day of battle and war?

translated_text:
By what way is the light parted,
which scattereth the east wind upon the earth?
original_text:
By what way is the light parted,
which scattereth the east wind upon the earth?

translated_text: Who hath divided a watercourse for the overflowing of waters, or a way for the lightning of thunder;
original_text: Who hath divided a watercourse for the overflowing of waters, or a way for the lightning of thunder;

translated_text:
To cause it to rain on the earth,
where no man
is; on
 the wilderness, wherein
there is no man;
original_text:
To cause it to rain on the earth,
where no man
is; on
 the wilderness, wherein
there is no man;

translated_text:
To satisfy the desolate and waste
ground; and to cause the bud of the tender herb to spring forth?
original_text:
To satisfy the desolate and waste
ground; and to cause the bud of the tender herb to spring forth?

translated_text: Hath the rain a father? or who hath begotten the drops of dew?
original_text: Hath the rain a father? or who hath begotten the drops of dew?

translated_text: Out of whose womb came the ice? and the hoary frost of heaven, who hath gendered it?
original_text: Out of whose womb came the ice? and the hoary frost of heaven, who hath gendered it?

translated_text:
The waters are hid as
with a stone, and the face of the deep is frozen.
original_text:
The waters are hid as
with a stone, and the face of the deep is frozen.

translated_text: Canst thou bind the sweet influences of Pleiades, or loose the bands of Orion?
original_text: Canst thou bind the sweet influences of Pleiades, or loose the bands of Orion?

translated_text: Canst thou bring forth Mazzaroth in his season? or canst thou guide Arcturus with his sons?
original_text: Canst thou bring forth Mazzaroth in his season? or canst thou guide Arcturus with his sons?

translated_text: Knowest thou the ordinances of heaven? canst thou set the dominion thereof in the earth?
original_text: Knowest thou the ordinances of heaven? canst thou set the dominion thereof in the earth?

translated_text: Canst thou lift up thy voice to the clouds, that abundance of waters may cover thee?
original_text: Canst thou lift up thy voice to the clouds, that abundance of waters may cover thee?

translated_text:
Canst thou send lightnings, that they may go, and say unto thee, Here we
are?
original_text:
Canst thou send lightnings, that they may go, and say unto thee, Here we
are?

translated_text: Who hath put wisdom in the inward parts? or who hath given understanding to the heart?
original_text: Who hath put wisdom in the inward parts? or who hath given understanding to the heart?

translated_text: Who can number the clouds in wisdom? or who can stay the bottles of heaven,
original_text: Who can number the clouds in wisdom? or who can stay the bottles of heaven,

translated_text: When the dust groweth into hardness, and the clods cleave fast together?
original_text: When the dust groweth into hardness, and the clods cleave fast together?

translated_text: Wilt thou hunt the prey for the lion? or fill the appetite of the young lions,
original_text: Wilt thou hunt the prey for the lion? or fill the appetite of the young lions,

translated_text:
When they couch in
their dens,
and abide in the covert to lie in wait?
original_text:
When they couch in
their dens,
and abide in the covert to lie in wait?

translated_text: Who provideth for the raven his food? when his young ones cry unto God, they wander for lack of meat.
original_text: Who provideth for the raven his food? when his young ones cry unto God, they wander for lack of meat.

translated_text: At this also my heart trembleth, and is moved out of his place.
original_text: At this also my heart trembleth, and is moved out of his place.

translated_text:
Hear attentively the noise of his voice, and the sound
that
 goeth out of his mouth.
original_text:
Hear attentively the noise of his voice, and the sound
that
 goeth out of his mouth.

translated_text: He directeth it under the whole heaven, and his lightning unto the ends of the earth.
original_text: He directeth it under the whole heaven, and his lightning unto the ends of the earth.

translated_text: After it a voice roareth: he thundereth with the voice of his excellency; and he will not stay them when his voice is heard.
original_text: After it a voice roareth: he thundereth with the voice of his excellency; and he will not stay them when his voice is heard.

translated_text: God thundereth marvellously with his voice; great things doeth he, which we cannot comprehend.
original_text: God thundereth marvellously with his voice; great things doeth he, which we cannot comprehend.

translated_text:
For he saith to the snow, Be thou
on the earth; likewise to the small rain, and to the great rain of his strength.
original_text:
For he saith to the snow, Be thou
on the earth; likewise to the small rain, and to the great rain of his strength.

translated_text: He sealeth up the hand of every man; that all men may know his work.
original_text: He sealeth up the hand of every man; that all men may know his work.

translated_text: Then the beasts go into dens, and remain in their places.
original_text: Then the beasts go into dens, and remain in their places.

translated_text: Out of the south cometh the whirlwind: and cold out of the north.
original_text: Out of the south cometh the whirlwind: and cold out of the north.

translated_text: By the breath of God frost is given: and the breadth of the waters is straitened.
original_text: By the breath of God frost is given: and the breadth of the waters is straitened.

translated_text: Also by watering he wearieth the thick cloud: he scattereth his bright cloud:
original_text: Also by watering he wearieth the thick cloud: he scattereth his bright cloud:

translated_text: And it is turned round about by his counsels: that they may do whatsoever he commandeth them upon the face of the world in the earth.
original_text: And it is turned round about by his counsels: that they may do whatsoever he commandeth them upon the face of the world in the earth.

translated_text: He causeth it to come, whether for correction, or for his land, or for mercy.
original_text: He causeth it to come, whether for correction, or for his land, or for mercy.

translated_text: Hearken unto this, O Job: stand still, and consider the wondrous works of God.
original_text: Hearken unto this, O Job: stand still, and consider the wondrous works of God.

translated_text: Dost thou know when God disposed them, and caused the light of his cloud to shine?
original_text: Dost thou know when God disposed them, and caused the light of his cloud to shine?

translated_text: Dost thou know the balancings of the clouds, the wondrous works of him which is perfect in knowledge?
original_text: Dost thou know the balancings of the clouds, the wondrous works of him which is perfect in knowledge?

translated_text:
How thy garments
are warm, when he quieteth the earth by the south
wind?
original_text:
How thy garments
are warm, when he quieteth the earth by the south
wind?

translated_text:
Hast thou with him spread out the sky,
which is strong,
and as a molten looking glass?
original_text:
Hast thou with him spread out the sky,
which is strong,
and as a molten looking glass?

translated_text: Shall it be told him that I speak? if a man speak, surely he shall be swallowed up.
original_text: Shall it be told him that I speak? if a man speak, surely he shall be swallowed up.

translated_text:
And now
men see not the bright light which is in the clouds: but the wind passeth, and cleanseth them.
original_text:
And now
men see not the bright light which is in the clouds: but the wind passeth, and cleanseth them.

translated_text: Fair weather cometh out of the north: with God is terrible majesty.
original_text: Fair weather cometh out of the north: with God is terrible majesty.

translated_text:
Touching the Almighty, we cannot find him out:
he is
 excellent in power, and in judgment, and in plenty of justice: he will not afflict.
original_text:
Touching the Almighty, we cannot find him out:
he is
 excellent in power, and in judgment, and in plenty of justice: he will not afflict.

translated_text:
Men do therefore fear him: he respecteth not any
that are
 wise of heart.
original_text:
Men do therefore fear him: he respecteth not any
that are
 wise of heart.

translated_text: Elihu also proceeded, and said,
original_text: Elihu also proceeded, and said,

translated_text:
Suffer me a little, and I will shew thee that
I have yet to speak on God’s behalf.
original_text:
Suffer me a little, and I will shew thee that
I have yet to speak on God’s behalf.

translated_text: I will fetch my knowledge from afar, and will ascribe righteousness to my Maker.
original_text: I will fetch my knowledge from afar, and will ascribe righteousness to my Maker.

translated_text:
For truly my words
shall not
be false: he that is perfect in knowledge
is with thee.
original_text:
For truly my words
shall not
be false: he that is perfect in knowledge
is with thee.

translated_text:
Behold, God
is mighty, and despiseth not
any: he is
 mighty in strength
and wisdom.
original_text:
Behold, God
is mighty, and despiseth not
any: he is
 mighty in strength
and wisdom.

translated_text: He preserveth not the life of the wicked: but giveth right to the poor.
original_text: He preserveth not the life of the wicked: but giveth right to the poor.

translated_text:
He withdraweth not his eyes from the righteous: but with kings
are they on the throne; yea, he doth establish them for ever, and they are exalted.
original_text:
He withdraweth not his eyes from the righteous: but with kings
are they on the throne; yea, he doth establish them for ever, and they are exalted.

translated_text: Then he sheweth them their work, and their transgressions that they have exceeded.
original_text: Then he sheweth them their work, and their transgressions that they have exceeded.

translated_text: He openeth also their ear to discipline, and commandeth that they return from iniquity.
original_text: He openeth also their ear to discipline, and commandeth that they return from iniquity.

translated_text:
If they obey and serve
him, they shall spend their days in prosperity, and their years in pleasures.
original_text:
If they obey and serve
him, they shall spend their days in prosperity, and their years in pleasures.

translated_text: But if they obey not, they shall perish by the sword, and they shall die without knowledge.
original_text: But if they obey not, they shall perish by the sword, and they shall die without knowledge.

translated_text: But the hypocrites in heart heap up wrath: they cry not when he bindeth them.
original_text: But the hypocrites in heart heap up wrath: they cry not when he bindeth them.

translated_text:
They die in youth, and their life
is among the unclean.
original_text:
They die in youth, and their life
is among the unclean.

translated_text: He delivereth the poor in his affliction, and openeth their ears in oppression.
original_text: He delivereth the poor in his affliction, and openeth their ears in oppression.

translated_text:
Even so would he have removed thee out of the strait
into
 a broad place, where
there is no straitness; and that which
should be set on thy table should be full of fatness.
original_text:
Even so would he have removed thee out of the strait
into
 a broad place, where
there is no straitness; and that which
should be set on thy table should be full of fatness.

translated_text:
But thou hast fulfilled the judgment of the wicked: judgment and justice take hold
on thee.
original_text:
But thou hast fulfilled the judgment of the wicked: judgment and justice take hold
on thee.

translated_text:
Because
there is wrath,
beware lest he take thee away with
his stroke: then a great ransom cannot deliver thee.
original_text:
Because
there is wrath,
beware lest he take thee away with
his stroke: then a great ransom cannot deliver thee.

translated_text:
Will he esteem thy riches?
no, not gold, nor all the forces of strength.
original_text:
Will he esteem thy riches?
no, not gold, nor all the forces of strength.

translated_text: Desire not the night, when people are cut off in their place.
original_text: Desire not the night, when people are cut off in their place.

translated_text: Take heed, regard not iniquity: for this hast thou chosen rather than affliction.
original_text: Take heed, regard not iniquity: for this hast thou chosen rather than affliction.

translated_text: Behold, God exalteth by his power: who teacheth like him?
original_text: Behold, God exalteth by his power: who teacheth like him?

translated_text: Who hath enjoined him his way? or who can say, Thou hast wrought iniquity?
original_text: Who hath enjoined him his way? or who can say, Thou hast wrought iniquity?

translated_text: Remember that thou magnify his work, which men behold.
original_text: Remember that thou magnify his work, which men behold.

translated_text:
Every man may see it; man may behold
it afar off.
original_text:
Every man may see it; man may behold
it afar off.

translated_text:
Behold, God
is great, and we know
him not, neither can the number of his years be searched out.
original_text:
Behold, God
is great, and we know
him not, neither can the number of his years be searched out.

translated_text: For he maketh small the drops of water: they pour down rain according to the vapour thereof:
original_text: For he maketh small the drops of water: they pour down rain according to the vapour thereof:

translated_text:
Which the clouds do drop
and distil upon man abundantly.
original_text:
Which the clouds do drop
and distil upon man abundantly.

translated_text:
Also can
any understand the spreadings of the clouds,
or the noise of his tabernacle?
original_text:
Also can
any understand the spreadings of the clouds,
or the noise of his tabernacle?

translated_text: Behold, he spreadeth his light upon it, and covereth the bottom of the sea.
original_text: Behold, he spreadeth his light upon it, and covereth the bottom of the sea.

translated_text: For by them judgeth he the people; he giveth meat in abundance.
original_text: For by them judgeth he the people; he giveth meat in abundance.

translated_text:
With clouds he covereth the light; and commandeth it
not to shine
 by
the cloud that cometh betwixt.
original_text:
With clouds he covereth the light; and commandeth it
not to shine
 by
the cloud that cometh betwixt.

translated_text: The noise thereof sheweth concerning it, the cattle also concerning the vapour.
original_text: The noise thereof sheweth concerning it, the cattle also concerning the vapour.

translated_text: Elihu spake moreover, and said,
original_text: Elihu spake moreover, and said,

translated_text:
Thinkest thou this to be right,
that thou saidst, My righteousness
is more than God’s?
original_text:
Thinkest thou this to be right,
that thou saidst, My righteousness
is more than God’s?

translated_text:
For thou saidst, What advantage will it be unto thee?
and,
 What profit shall I have,
if I be cleansed from my sin?
original_text:
For thou saidst, What advantage will it be unto thee?
and,
 What profit shall I have,
if I be cleansed from my sin?

translated_text: I will answer thee, and thy companions with thee.
original_text: I will answer thee, and thy companions with thee.

translated_text:
Look unto the heavens, and see; and behold the clouds
which
 are higher than thou.
original_text:
Look unto the heavens, and see; and behold the clouds
which
 are higher than thou.

translated_text:
If thou sinnest, what doest thou against him? or
if thy transgressions be multiplied, what doest thou unto him?
original_text:
If thou sinnest, what doest thou against him? or
if thy transgressions be multiplied, what doest thou unto him?

translated_text: If thou be righteous, what givest thou him? or what receiveth he of thine hand?
original_text: If thou be righteous, what givest thou him? or what receiveth he of thine hand?

translated_text:
Thy wickedness
may hurt a man as thou
art; and thy righteousness
may profit the son of man.
original_text:
Thy wickedness
may hurt a man as thou
art; and thy righteousness
may profit the son of man.

translated_text:
By reason of the multitude of oppressions they make
the oppressed
 to cry: they cry out by reason of the arm of the mighty.
original_text:
By reason of the multitude of oppressions they make
the oppressed
 to cry: they cry out by reason of the arm of the mighty.

translated_text:
But none saith, Where
is God my maker, who giveth songs in the night;
original_text:
But none saith, Where
is God my maker, who giveth songs in the night;

translated_text: Who teacheth us more than the beasts of the earth, and maketh us wiser than the fowls of heaven?
original_text: Who teacheth us more than the beasts of the earth, and maketh us wiser than the fowls of heaven?

translated_text: There they cry, but none giveth answer, because of the pride of evil men.
original_text: There they cry, but none giveth answer, because of the pride of evil men.

translated_text: Surely God will not hear vanity, neither will the Almighty regard it.
original_text: Surely God will not hear vanity, neither will the Almighty regard it.

translated_text:
Although thou sayest thou shalt not see him,
yet judgment
is before him; therefore trust thou in him.
original_text:
Although thou sayest thou shalt not see him,
yet judgment
is before him; therefore trust thou in him.

translated_text:
But now, because
it is not
so, he hath visited in his anger; yet he knoweth
it not in great extremity:
original_text:
But now, because
it is not
so, he hath visited in his anger; yet he knoweth
it not in great extremity:

translated_text: Therefore doth Job open his mouth in vain; he multiplieth words without knowledge.
original_text: Therefore doth Job open his mouth in vain; he multiplieth words without knowledge.

translated_text:
Canst thou draw out leviathan with an hook? or his tongue with a cord
which thou lettest down?
original_text:
Canst thou draw out leviathan with an hook? or his tongue with a cord
which thou lettest down?

translated_text: Canst thou put an hook into his nose? or bore his jaw through with a thorn?
original_text: Canst thou put an hook into his nose? or bore his jaw through with a thorn?

translated_text:
Will he make many supplications unto thee? will he speak soft
words
 unto thee?
original_text:
Will he make many supplications unto thee? will he speak soft
words
 unto thee?

translated_text: Will he make a covenant with thee? wilt thou take him for a servant for ever?
original_text: Will he make a covenant with thee? wilt thou take him for a servant for ever?

translated_text:
Wilt thou play with him as
with a bird? or wilt thou bind him for thy maidens?
original_text:
Wilt thou play with him as
with a bird? or wilt thou bind him for thy maidens?

translated_text: Shall the companions make a banquet of him? shall they part him among the merchants?
original_text: Shall the companions make a banquet of him? shall they part him among the merchants?

translated_text: Canst thou fill his skin with barbed irons? or his head with fish spears?
original_text: Canst thou fill his skin with barbed irons? or his head with fish spears?

translated_text: Lay thine hand upon him, remember the battle, do no more.
original_text: Lay thine hand upon him, remember the battle, do no more.

translated_text:
Behold, the hope of him is in vain: shall not
one be cast down even at the sight of him?
original_text:
Behold, the hope of him is in vain: shall not
one be cast down even at the sight of him?

translated_text:
None
is so fierce that dare stir him up: who then is able to stand before me?
