original_text:
None
is so fierce that dare stir him up: who then is able to stand before me?

translated_text:
Who hath prevented me, that I should repay
him? whatsoever is
 under the whole heaven is mine.
original_text:
Who hath prevented me, that I should repay
him? whatsoever is
 under the whole heaven is mine.

translated_text: I will not conceal his parts, nor his power, nor his comely proportion.
original_text: I will not conceal his parts, nor his power, nor his comely proportion.

translated_text:
Who can discover the face of his garment?
or who can come
to him with his double bridle?
original_text:
Who can discover the face of his garment?
or who can come
to him with his double bridle?

translated_text:
Who can open the doors of his face? his teeth
are terrible round about.
original_text:
Who can open the doors of his face? his teeth
are terrible round about.

translated_text:
His scales
are his pride, shut up together
as with a close seal.
original_text:
His scales
are his pride, shut up together
as with a close seal.

translated_text: One is so near to another, that no air can come between them.
original_text: One is so near to another, that no air can come between them.

translated_text: They are joined one to another, they stick together, that they cannot be sundered.
original_text: They are joined one to another, they stick together, that they cannot be sundered.

translated_text:
By his neesings a light doth shine, and his eyes
are like the eyelids of the morning.
original_text:
By his neesings a light doth shine, and his eyes
are like the eyelids of the morning.

translated_text:
Out of his mouth go burning lamps,
and sparks of fire leap out.
original_text:
Out of his mouth go burning lamps,
and sparks of fire leap out.

translated_text:
Out of his nostrils goeth smoke, as
out of a seething pot or caldron.
original_text:
Out of his nostrils goeth smoke, as
out of a seething pot or caldron.

translated_text: His breath kindleth coals, and a flame goeth out of his mouth.
original_text: His breath kindleth coals, and a flame goeth out of his mouth.

translated_text: In his neck remaineth strength, and sorrow is turned into joy before him.
original_text: In his neck remaineth strength, and sorrow is turned into joy before him.

translated_text: The flakes of his flesh are joined together: they are firm in themselves; they cannot be moved.
original_text: The flakes of his flesh are joined together: they are firm in themselves; they cannot be moved.

translated_text:
His heart is as firm as a stone; yea, as hard as a piece of the nether
millstone.
original_text:
His heart is as firm as a stone; yea, as hard as a piece of the nether
millstone.

translated_text: When he raiseth up himself, the mighty are afraid: by reason of breakings they purify themselves.
original_text: When he raiseth up himself, the mighty are afraid: by reason of breakings they purify themselves.

translated_text: The sword of him that layeth at him cannot hold: the spear, the dart, nor the habergeon.
original_text: The sword of him that layeth at him cannot hold: the spear, the dart, nor the habergeon.

translated_text:
He esteemeth iron as straw,
and brass as rotten wood.
original_text:
He esteemeth iron as straw,
and brass as rotten wood.

translated_text: The arrow cannot make him flee: slingstones are turned with him into stubble.
original_text: The arrow cannot make him flee: slingstones are turned with him into stubble.

translated_text: Darts are counted as stubble: he laugheth at the shaking of a spear.
original_text: Darts are counted as stubble: he laugheth at the shaking of a spear.

translated_text:
Sharp stones
are under him: he spreadeth sharp pointed things upon the mire.
original_text:
Sharp stones
are under him: he spreadeth sharp pointed things upon the mire.

translated_text: He maketh the deep to boil like a pot: he maketh the sea like a pot of ointment.
original_text: He maketh the deep to boil like a pot: he maketh the sea like a pot of ointment.

translated_text: Upon earth there is not his like, who is made without fear.
original_text: Upon earth there is not his like, who is made without fear.

translated_text:
He beholdeth all high
things: he
is a king over all the children of pride.
original_text:
He beholdeth all high
things: he
is a king over all the children of pride.

translated_text: Moreover the LORD answered Job, and said,
original_text: Moreover the LORD answered Job, and said,

translated_text:
Shall he that contendeth with the Almighty instruct
him? he that reproveth God, let him answer it.
original_text:
Shall he that contendeth with the Almighty instruct
him? he that reproveth God, let him answer it.

translated_text: Then Job answered the LORD, and said,
original_text: Then Job answered the LORD, and said,

translated_text: Behold, I am vile; what shall I answer thee? I will lay mine hand upon my mouth.
original_text: Behold, I am vile; what shall I answer thee? I will lay mine hand upon my mouth.

translated_text: Once have I spoken; but I will not answer: yea, twice; but I will proceed no further.
original_text: Once have I spoken; but I will not answer: yea, twice; but I will proceed no further.

translated_text: Then answered the LORD unto Job out of the whirlwind, and said,
original_text: Then answered the LORD unto Job out of the whirlwind, and said,

translated_text: Gird up thy loins now like a man: I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me.
original_text: Gird up thy loins now like a man: I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me.

translated_text: Wilt thou also disannul my judgment? wilt thou condemn me, that thou mayest be righteous?
original_text: Wilt thou also disannul my judgment? wilt thou condemn me, that thou mayest be righteous?

translated_text: Hast thou an arm like God? or canst thou thunder with a voice like him?
original_text: Hast thou an arm like God? or canst thou thunder with a voice like him?

translated_text:
Deck thyself now
with majesty and excellency; and array thyself with glory and beauty.
original_text:
Deck thyself now
with majesty and excellency; and array thyself with glory and beauty.

translated_text:
Cast abroad the rage of thy wrath: and behold every one
that is
 proud, and abase him.
original_text:
Cast abroad the rage of thy wrath: and behold every one
that is
 proud, and abase him.

translated_text:
Look on every one
that is proud,
and bring him low; and tread down the wicked in their place.
original_text:
Look on every one
that is proud,
and bring him low; and tread down the wicked in their place.

translated_text:
Hide them in the dust together;
and bind their faces in secret.
original_text:
Hide them in the dust together;
and bind their faces in secret.

translated_text: Then will I also confess unto thee that thine own right hand can save thee.
original_text: Then will I also confess unto thee that thine own right hand can save thee.

translated_text: Behold now behemoth, which I made with thee; he eateth grass as an ox.
original_text: Behold now behemoth, which I made with thee; he eateth grass as an ox.

translated_text:
Lo now, his strength
is in his loins, and his force
is in the navel of his belly.
original_text:
Lo now, his strength
is in his loins, and his force
is in the navel of his belly.

translated_text: He moveth his tail like a cedar: the sinews of his stones are wrapped together.
original_text: He moveth his tail like a cedar: the sinews of his stones are wrapped together.

translated_text:
His bones
are as strong pieces of brass; his bones
are
 like bars of iron.
original_text:
His bones
are as strong pieces of brass; his bones
are
 like bars of iron.

translated_text:
He
is the chief of the ways of God: he that made him can make his sword to approach
unto him.
original_text:
He
is the chief of the ways of God: he that made him can make his sword to approach
unto him.

translated_text: Surely the mountains bring him forth food, where all the beasts of the field play.
original_text: Surely the mountains bring him forth food, where all the beasts of the field play.

translated_text: He lieth under the shady trees, in the covert of the reed, and fens.
original_text: He lieth under the shady trees, in the covert of the reed, and fens.

translated_text:
The shady trees cover him
with their shadow; the willows of the brook compass him about.
original_text:
The shady trees cover him
with their shadow; the willows of the brook compass him about.

translated_text:
Behold, he drinketh up a river,
and hasteth not: he trusteth that he can draw up Jordan into his mouth.
original_text:
Behold, he drinketh up a river,
and hasteth not: he trusteth that he can draw up Jordan into his mouth.

translated_text:
He taketh it with his eyes:
his nose pierceth through snares.
original_text:
He taketh it with his eyes:
his nose pierceth through snares.

translated_text: Moreover Job continued his parable, and said,
original_text: Moreover Job continued his parable, and said,

translated_text:
Oh that I were as
in months past, as
in the days
when God preserved me;
original_text:
Oh that I were as
in months past, as
in the days
when God preserved me;

translated_text:
When the Almighty
was yet with me,
when my children
were about me;
original_text:
When the Almighty
was yet with me,
when my children
were about me;

translated_text: When I washed my steps with butter, and the rock poured me out rivers of oil;
original_text: When I washed my steps with butter, and the rock poured me out rivers of oil;

translated_text:
When I went out to the gate through the city,
when I prepared my seat in the street!
original_text:
When I went out to the gate through the city,
when I prepared my seat in the street!

translated_text:
The young men saw me, and hid themselves: and the aged arose,
and
 stood up.
original_text:
The young men saw me, and hid themselves: and the aged arose,
and
 stood up.

translated_text:
The princes refrained talking, and laid
their hand on their mouth.
original_text:
The princes refrained talking, and laid
their hand on their mouth.

translated_text: The nobles held their peace, and their tongue cleaved to the roof of their mouth.
original_text: The nobles held their peace, and their tongue cleaved to the roof of their mouth.

translated_text:
When the ear heard
me, then it blessed me; and when the eye saw
me, it gave witness to me:
original_text:
When the ear heard
me, then it blessed me; and when the eye saw
me, it gave witness to me:

translated_text:
Because I delivered the poor that cried, and the fatherless, and
him that had none to help him.
original_text:
Because I delivered the poor that cried, and the fatherless, and
him that had none to help him.

translated_text: The blessing of him that was ready to perish came upon me: and I caused the widow’s heart to sing for joy.
original_text: The blessing of him that was ready to perish came upon me: and I caused the widow’s heart to sing for joy.

translated_text:
I put on righteousness, and it clothed me: my judgment
was
 as a robe and a diadem.
original_text:
I put on righteousness, and it clothed me: my judgment
was
 as a robe and a diadem.

translated_text:
I was eyes to the blind, and feet
was I to the lame.
original_text:
I was eyes to the blind, and feet
was I to the lame.

translated_text:
I
was a father to the poor: and the cause
which
 I knew not I searched out.
original_text:
I
was a father to the poor: and the cause
which
 I knew not I searched out.

translated_text: And I brake the jaws of the wicked, and plucked the spoil out of his teeth.
original_text: And I brake the jaws of the wicked, and plucked the spoil out of his teeth.

translated_text:
Then I said, I shall die in my nest, and I shall multiply
my
 days as the sand.
original_text:
Then I said, I shall die in my nest, and I shall multiply
my
 days as the sand.

translated_text:
My root
was spread out by the waters, and the dew lay all night upon my branch.
original_text:
My root
was spread out by the waters, and the dew lay all night upon my branch.

translated_text:
My glory
was fresh in me, and my bow was renewed in my hand.
original_text:
My glory
was fresh in me, and my bow was renewed in my hand.

translated_text:
Unto me
men gave ear, and waited, and kept silence at my counsel.
original_text:
Unto me
men gave ear, and waited, and kept silence at my counsel.

translated_text: After my words they spake not again; and my speech dropped upon them.
original_text: After my words they spake not again; and my speech dropped upon them.

translated_text:
And they waited for me as for the rain; and they opened their mouth wide
as for the latter rain.
original_text:
And they waited for me as for the rain; and they opened their mouth wide
as for the latter rain.

translated_text:
If I laughed on them, they believed
it not; and the light of my countenance they cast not down.
original_text:
If I laughed on them, they believed
it not; and the light of my countenance they cast not down.

translated_text:
I chose out their way, and sat chief, and dwelt as a king in the army, as one
that comforteth the mourners.
original_text:
I chose out their way, and sat chief, and dwelt as a king in the army, as one
that comforteth the mourners.

translated_text:
Surely there is a vein for the silver, and a place for gold
where
 they fine
it.
original_text:
Surely there is a vein for the silver, and a place for gold
where
 they fine
it.

translated_text:
Iron is taken out of the earth, and brass
is molten
out of the stone.
original_text:
Iron is taken out of the earth, and brass
is molten
out of the stone.

translated_text: He setteth an end to darkness, and searcheth out all perfection: the stones of darkness, and the shadow of death.
original_text: He setteth an end to darkness, and searcheth out all perfection: the stones of darkness, and the shadow of death.

translated_text: As for the earth, out of it cometh bread: and under it is turned up as it were fire.
original_text: As for the earth, out of it cometh bread: and under it is turned up as it were fire.

translated_text:
The stones of it
are the place of sapphires: and it hath dust of gold.
original_text:
The stones of it
are the place of sapphires: and it hath dust of gold.

translated_text: There is a path which no fowl knoweth, and which the vulture’s eye hath not seen:
original_text: There is a path which no fowl knoweth, and which the vulture’s eye hath not seen:

translated_text: The lion’s whelps have not trodden it, nor the fierce lion passed by it.
original_text: The lion’s whelps have not trodden it, nor the fierce lion passed by it.

translated_text: He putteth forth his hand upon the rock; he overturneth the mountains by the roots.
original_text: He putteth forth his hand upon the rock; he overturneth the mountains by the roots.

translated_text: He cutteth out rivers among the rocks; and his eye seeth every precious thing.
original_text: He cutteth out rivers among the rocks; and his eye seeth every precious thing.

translated_text:
He bindeth the floods from overflowing; and
the thing that is
 hid bringeth he forth to light.
original_text:
He bindeth the floods from overflowing; and
the thing that is
 hid bringeth he forth to light.

translated_text:
But where shall wisdom be found? and where
is the place of understanding?
original_text:
But where shall wisdom be found? and where
is the place of understanding?

translated_text: Man knoweth not the price thereof; neither is it found in the land of the living.
original_text: Man knoweth not the price thereof; neither is it found in the land of the living.

translated_text:
The depth saith, It
is not in me: and the sea saith,
It is not with me.
original_text:
The depth saith, It
is not in me: and the sea saith,
It is not with me.

translated_text:
It cannot be gotten for gold, neither shall silver be weighed
for the price thereof.
original_text:
It cannot be gotten for gold, neither shall silver be weighed
for the price thereof.

translated_text: It cannot be valued with the gold of Ophir, with the precious onyx, or the sapphire.
original_text: It cannot be valued with the gold of Ophir, with the precious onyx, or the sapphire.

translated_text:
The gold and the crystal cannot equal it: and the exchange of it
shall not be for jewels of fine gold.
original_text:
The gold and the crystal cannot equal it: and the exchange of it
shall not be for jewels of fine gold.

translated_text:
No mention shall be made of coral, or of pearls: for the price of wisdom
is above rubies.
original_text:
No mention shall be made of coral, or of pearls: for the price of wisdom
is above rubies.

translated_text: The topaz of Ethiopia shall not equal it, neither shall it be valued with pure gold.
original_text: The topaz of Ethiopia shall not equal it, neither shall it be valued with pure gold.

translated_text:
Whence then cometh wisdom? and where
is the place of understanding?
original_text:
Whence then cometh wisdom? and where
is the place of understanding?

translated_text: Seeing it is hid from the eyes of all living, and kept close from the fowls of the air.
original_text: Seeing it is hid from the eyes of all living, and kept close from the fowls of the air.

translated_text: Destruction and death say, We have heard the fame thereof with our ears.
original_text: Destruction and death say, We have heard the fame thereof with our ears.

translated_text: God understandeth the way thereof, and he knoweth the place thereof.
original_text: God understandeth the way thereof, and he knoweth the place thereof.

translated_text:
For he looketh to the ends of the earth,
and seeth under the whole heaven;
original_text:
For he looketh to the ends of the earth,
and seeth under the whole heaven;

translated_text: To make the weight for the winds; and he weigheth the waters by measure.
original_text: To make the weight for the winds; and he weigheth the waters by measure.

translated_text: When he made a decree for the rain, and a way for the lightning of the thunder:
original_text: When he made a decree for the rain, and a way for the lightning of the thunder:

translated_text: Then did he see it, and declare it; he prepared it, yea, and searched it out.
original_text: Then did he see it, and declare it; he prepared it, yea, and searched it out.

translated_text:
And unto man he said, Behold, the fear of the Lord, that
is
 wisdom; and to depart from evil
is understanding.
original_text:
And unto man he said, Behold, the fear of the Lord, that
is
 wisdom; and to depart from evil
is understanding.

translated_text: Then Job answered and said,
original_text: Then Job answered and said,

translated_text:
Even to day
is my complaint bitter: my stroke is heavier than my groaning.
original_text:
Even to day
is my complaint bitter: my stroke is heavier than my groaning.

translated_text:
Oh that I knew where I might find him!
that I might come
even to his seat!
original_text:
Oh that I knew where I might find him!
that I might come
even to his seat!

translated_text:
I would order
my cause before him, and fill my mouth with arguments.
original_text:
I would order
my cause before him, and fill my mouth with arguments.

translated_text:
I would know the words
which he would answer me, and understand what he would say unto me.
original_text:
I would know the words
which he would answer me, and understand what he would say unto me.

translated_text:
Will he plead against me with
his great power? No; but he would put
strength in me.
original_text:
Will he plead against me with
his great power? No; but he would put
strength in me.

translated_text: There the righteous might dispute with him; so should I be delivered for ever from my judge.
original_text: There the righteous might dispute with him; so should I be delivered for ever from my judge.

translated_text:
Behold, I go forward, but he
is not
there; and backward, but I cannot perceive him:
original_text:
Behold, I go forward, but he
is not
there; and backward, but I cannot perceive him:

translated_text:
On the left hand, where he doth work, but I cannot behold
him:
 he hideth himself on the right hand, that I cannot see
him:
original_text:
On the left hand, where he doth work, but I cannot behold
him:
 he hideth himself on the right hand, that I cannot see
him:

translated_text:
But he knoweth the way that I take:
when he hath tried me, I shall come forth as gold.
original_text:
But he knoweth the way that I take:
when he hath tried me, I shall come forth as gold.

translated_text: My foot hath held his steps, his way have I kept, and not declined.
original_text: My foot hath held his steps, his way have I kept, and not declined.

translated_text:
Neither have I gone back from the commandment of his lips; I have esteemed the words of his mouth more than my necessary
food.
original_text:
Neither have I gone back from the commandment of his lips; I have esteemed the words of his mouth more than my necessary
food.

translated_text:
But he
is in one
mind, and who can turn him? and
what his soul desireth, even
that he doeth.
original_text:
But he
is in one
mind, and who can turn him? and
what his soul desireth, even
that he doeth.

translated_text:
For he performeth
the thing that is appointed for me: and many such
things are with him.
original_text:
For he performeth
the thing that is appointed for me: and many such
things are with him.

translated_text: Therefore am I troubled at his presence: when I consider, I am afraid of him.
original_text: Therefore am I troubled at his presence: when I consider, I am afraid of him.

translated_text: For God maketh my heart soft, and the Almighty troubleth me:
original_text: For God maketh my heart soft, and the Almighty troubleth me:

translated_text:
Because I was not cut off before the darkness,
neither hath he covered the darkness from my face.
original_text:
Because I was not cut off before the darkness,
neither hath he covered the darkness from my face.

translated_text: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said,
original_text: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said,

translated_text: Can a man be profitable unto God, as he that is wise may be profitable unto himself?
original_text: Can a man be profitable unto God, as he that is wise may be profitable unto himself?

translated_text:
Is it any pleasure to the Almighty, that thou art righteous? or
is it gain
to him that thou makest thy ways perfect?
original_text:
Is it any pleasure to the Almighty, that thou art righteous? or
is it gain
to him that thou makest thy ways perfect?

translated_text: Will he reprove thee for fear of thee? will he enter with thee into judgment?
original_text: Will he reprove thee for fear of thee? will he enter with thee into judgment?

translated_text: Is not thy wickedness great? and thine iniquities infinite?
original_text: Is not thy wickedness great? and thine iniquities infinite?

translated_text: For thou hast taken a pledge from thy brother for nought, and stripped the naked of their clothing.
original_text: For thou hast taken a pledge from thy brother for nought, and stripped the naked of their clothing.

translated_text: Thou hast not given water to the weary to drink, and thou hast withholden bread from the hungry.
original_text: Thou hast not given water to the weary to drink, and thou hast withholden bread from the hungry.

translated_text:
But
as for the mighty man, he had the earth; and the honourable man dwelt in it.
original_text:
But
as for the mighty man, he had the earth; and the honourable man dwelt in it.

translated_text: Thou hast sent widows away empty, and the arms of the fatherless have been broken.
original_text: Thou hast sent widows away empty, and the arms of the fatherless have been broken.

translated_text:
Therefore snares
are round about thee, and sudden fear troubleth thee;
original_text:
Therefore snares
are round about thee, and sudden fear troubleth thee;

translated_text:
Or darkness,
that thou canst not see; and abundance of waters cover thee.
original_text:
Or darkness,
that thou canst not see; and abundance of waters cover thee.

translated_text: Is not God in the height of heaven? and behold the height of the stars, how high they are!
original_text: Is not God in the height of heaven? and behold the height of the stars, how high they are!

translated_text: And thou sayest, How doth God know? can he judge through the dark cloud?
original_text: And thou sayest, How doth God know? can he judge through the dark cloud?

translated_text:
Thick clouds
are a covering to him, that he seeth not; and he walketh in the circuit of heaven.
original_text:
Thick clouds
are a covering to him, that he seeth not; and he walketh in the circuit of heaven.

translated_text: Hast thou marked the old way which wicked men have trodden?
original_text: Hast thou marked the old way which wicked men have trodden?

translated_text: Which were cut down out of time, whose foundation was overflown with a flood:
original_text: Which were cut down out of time, whose foundation was overflown with a flood:

translated_text: Which said unto God, Depart from us: and what can the Almighty do for them?
original_text: Which said unto God, Depart from us: and what can the Almighty do for them?

translated_text:
Yet he filled their houses with good
things: but the counsel of the wicked is far from me.
original_text:
Yet he filled their houses with good
things: but the counsel of the wicked is far from me.

translated_text:
The righteous see
it, and are glad: and the innocent laugh them to scorn.
original_text:
The righteous see
it, and are glad: and the innocent laugh them to scorn.

translated_text: Whereas our substance is not cut down, but the remnant of them the fire consumeth.
original_text: Whereas our substance is not cut down, but the remnant of them the fire consumeth.

translated_text: Acquaint now thyself with him, and be at peace: thereby good shall come unto thee.
original_text: Acquaint now thyself with him, and be at peace: thereby good shall come unto thee.

translated_text: Receive, I pray thee, the law from his mouth, and lay up his words in thine heart.
original_text: Receive, I pray thee, the law from his mouth, and lay up his words in thine heart.

translated_text: If thou return to the Almighty, thou shalt be built up, thou shalt put away iniquity far from thy tabernacles.
original_text: If thou return to the Almighty, thou shalt be built up, thou shalt put away iniquity far from thy tabernacles.

translated_text:
Then shalt thou lay up gold as dust, and the
gold of Ophir as the stones of the brooks.
original_text:
Then shalt thou lay up gold as dust, and the
gold of Ophir as the stones of the brooks.

translated_text: Yea, the Almighty shall be thy defence, and thou shalt have plenty of silver.
original_text: Yea, the Almighty shall be thy defence, and thou shalt have plenty of silver.

translated_text: For then shalt thou have thy delight in the Almighty, and shalt lift up thy face unto God.
original_text: For then shalt thou have thy delight in the Almighty, and shalt lift up thy face unto God.

translated_text: Thou shalt make thy prayer unto him, and he shall hear thee, and thou shalt pay thy vows.
original_text: Thou shalt make thy prayer unto him, and he shall hear thee, and thou shalt pay thy vows.

translated_text: Thou shalt also decree a thing, and it shall be established unto thee: and the light shall shine upon thy ways.
original_text: Thou shalt also decree a thing, and it shall be established unto thee: and the light shall shine upon thy ways.

translated_text:
When
men are cast down, then thou shalt say,
There is
 lifting up; and he shall save the humble person.
original_text:
When
men are cast down, then thou shalt say,
There is
 lifting up; and he shall save the humble person.

translated_text: He shall deliver the island of the innocent: and it is delivered by the pureness of thine hands.
original_text: He shall deliver the island of the innocent: and it is delivered by the pureness of thine hands.

translated_text: But Job answered and said,
original_text: But Job answered and said,

translated_text: Hear diligently my speech, and let this be your consolations.
original_text: Hear diligently my speech, and let this be your consolations.

translated_text: Suffer me that I may speak; and after that I have spoken, mock on.
original_text: Suffer me that I may speak; and after that I have spoken, mock on.

translated_text:
As for me,
is my complaint to man? and if
it were so,
 why should not my spirit be troubled?
original_text:
As for me,
is my complaint to man? and if
it were so,
 why should not my spirit be troubled?

translated_text:
Mark me, and be astonished, and lay
your hand upon
your
 mouth.
original_text:
Mark me, and be astonished, and lay
your hand upon
your
 mouth.

translated_text: Even when I remember I am afraid, and trembling taketh hold on my flesh.
original_text: Even when I remember I am afraid, and trembling taketh hold on my flesh.

translated_text: Wherefore do the wicked live, become old, yea, are mighty in power?
original_text: Wherefore do the wicked live, become old, yea, are mighty in power?

translated_text: Their seed is established in their sight with them, and their offspring before their eyes.
original_text: Their seed is established in their sight with them, and their offspring before their eyes.

translated_text:
Their houses
are safe from fear, neither
is the rod of God upon them.
original_text:
Their houses
are safe from fear, neither
is the rod of God upon them.

translated_text: Their bull gendereth, and faileth not; their cow calveth, and casteth not her calf.
original_text: Their bull gendereth, and faileth not; their cow calveth, and casteth not her calf.

translated_text: They send forth their little ones like a flock, and their children dance.
original_text: They send forth their little ones like a flock, and their children dance.

translated_text: They take the timbrel and harp, and rejoice at the sound of the organ.
original_text: They take the timbrel and harp, and rejoice at the sound of the organ.

translated_text: They spend their days in wealth, and in a moment go down to the grave.
original_text: They spend their days in wealth, and in a moment go down to the grave.

translated_text: Therefore they say unto God, Depart from us; for we desire not the knowledge of thy ways.
original_text: Therefore they say unto God, Depart from us; for we desire not the knowledge of thy ways.

translated_text:
What
is the Almighty, that we should serve him? and what profit should we have, if we pray unto him?
original_text:
What
is the Almighty, that we should serve him? and what profit should we have, if we pray unto him?

translated_text:
Lo, their good
is not in their hand: the counsel of the wicked is far from me.
original_text:
Lo, their good
is not in their hand: the counsel of the wicked is far from me.

translated_text:
How oft is the candle of the wicked put out! and
how oft
 cometh their destruction upon them!
God distributeth sorrows in his anger.
original_text:
How oft is the candle of the wicked put out! and
how oft
 cometh their destruction upon them!
God distributeth sorrows in his anger.

translated_text: They are as stubble before the wind, and as chaff that the storm carrieth away.
original_text: They are as stubble before the wind, and as chaff that the storm carrieth away.

translated_text:
God layeth up his iniquity for his children: he rewardeth him, and he shall know
it.
original_text:
God layeth up his iniquity for his children: he rewardeth him, and he shall know
it.

translated_text: His eyes shall see his destruction, and he shall drink of the wrath of the Almighty.
original_text: His eyes shall see his destruction, and he shall drink of the wrath of the Almighty.

translated_text:
For what pleasure
hath he in his house after him, when the number of his months is cut off in the midst?
original_text:
For what pleasure
hath he in his house after him, when the number of his months is cut off in the midst?

translated_text:
Shall
any teach God knowledge? seeing he judgeth those that are high.
original_text:
Shall
any teach God knowledge? seeing he judgeth those that are high.

translated_text: One dieth in his full strength, being wholly at ease and quiet.
original_text: One dieth in his full strength, being wholly at ease and quiet.

translated_text: His breasts are full of milk, and his bones are moistened with marrow.
original_text: His breasts are full of milk, and his bones are moistened with marrow.

translated_text: And another dieth in the bitterness of his soul, and never eateth with pleasure.
original_text: And another dieth in the bitterness of his soul, and never eateth with pleasure.

translated_text: They shall lie down alike in the dust, and the worms shall cover them.
original_text: They shall lie down alike in the dust, and the worms shall cover them.

translated_text:
Behold, I know your thoughts, and the devices
which ye wrongfully imagine against me.
original_text:
Behold, I know your thoughts, and the devices
which ye wrongfully imagine against me.

translated_text:
For ye say, Where
is the house of the prince? and where
are the dwelling places of the wicked?
original_text:
For ye say, Where
is the house of the prince? and where
are the dwelling places of the wicked?

translated_text: Have ye not asked them that go by the way? and do ye not know their tokens,
original_text: Have ye not asked them that go by the way? and do ye not know their tokens,

translated_text: That the wicked is reserved to the day of destruction? they shall be brought forth to the day of wrath.
original_text: That the wicked is reserved to the day of destruction? they shall be brought forth to the day of wrath.

translated_text:
Who shall declare his way to his face? and who shall repay him
what he hath done?
original_text:
Who shall declare his way to his face? and who shall repay him
what he hath done?

translated_text: Yet shall he be brought to the grave, and shall remain in the tomb.
original_text: Yet shall he be brought to the grave, and shall remain in the tomb.

translated_text:
The clods of the valley shall be sweet unto him, and every man shall draw after him, as
there are innumerable before him.
original_text:
The clods of the valley shall be sweet unto him, and every man shall draw after him, as
there are innumerable before him.

translated_text: How then comfort ye me in vain, seeing in your answers there remaineth falsehood?
original_text: How then comfort ye me in vain, seeing in your answers there remaineth falsehood?

translated_text: Then answered Zophar the Naamathite, and said,
original_text: Then answered Zophar the Naamathite, and said,

translated_text:
Therefore do my thoughts cause me to answer, and for
this
 I make haste.
original_text:
Therefore do my thoughts cause me to answer, and for
this
 I make haste.

translated_text: I have heard the check of my reproach, and the spirit of my understanding causeth me to answer.
original_text: I have heard the check of my reproach, and the spirit of my understanding causeth me to answer.

translated_text:
Knowest thou
not this of old, since man was placed upon earth,
original_text:
Knowest thou
not this of old, since man was placed upon earth,

translated_text:
That the triumphing of the wicked
is short, and the joy of the hypocrite
but for a moment?
original_text:
That the triumphing of the wicked
is short, and the joy of the hypocrite
but for a moment?

translated_text: Though his excellency mount up to the heavens, and his head reach unto the clouds;
original_text: Though his excellency mount up to the heavens, and his head reach unto the clouds;

translated_text:
Yet he shall perish for ever like his own dung: they which have seen him shall say, Where
is he?
original_text:
Yet he shall perish for ever like his own dung: they which have seen him shall say, Where
is he?

translated_text: He shall fly away as a dream, and shall not be found: yea, he shall be chased away as a vision of the night.
original_text: He shall fly away as a dream, and shall not be found: yea, he shall be chased away as a vision of the night.

translated_text:
The eye also
which saw him shall
see him no more; neither shall his place any more behold him.
original_text:
The eye also
which saw him shall
see him no more; neither shall his place any more behold him.

translated_text: His children shall seek to please the poor, and his hands shall restore their goods.
original_text: His children shall seek to please the poor, and his hands shall restore their goods.

translated_text:
His bones are full
of the sin of his youth, which shall lie down with him in the dust.
original_text:
His bones are full
of the sin of his youth, which shall lie down with him in the dust.

translated_text:
Though wickedness be sweet in his mouth,
though he hide it under his tongue;
original_text:
Though wickedness be sweet in his mouth,
though he hide it under his tongue;

translated_text: Though he spare it, and forsake it not; but keep it still within his mouth:
original_text: Though he spare it, and forsake it not; but keep it still within his mouth:

translated_text:
Yet his meat in his bowels is turned,
it is the gall of asps within him.
original_text:
Yet his meat in his bowels is turned,
it is the gall of asps within him.

translated_text: He hath swallowed down riches, and he shall vomit them up again: God shall cast them out of his belly.
original_text: He hath swallowed down riches, and he shall vomit them up again: God shall cast them out of his belly.

translated_text: He shall suck the poison of asps: the viper’s tongue shall slay him.
original_text: He shall suck the poison of asps: the viper’s tongue shall slay him.

translated_text: He shall not see the rivers, the floods, the brooks of honey and butter.
original_text: He shall not see the rivers, the floods, the brooks of honey and butter.

translated_text:
That which he laboured for shall he restore, and shall not swallow
it down: according to
his substance
shall the restitution
be, and he shall not rejoice
therein.
original_text:
That which he laboured for shall he restore, and shall not swallow
it down: according to
his substance
shall the restitution
be, and he shall not rejoice
therein.

translated_text: Surely he shall not feel quietness in his belly, he shall not save of that which he desired.
original_text: Surely he shall not feel quietness in his belly, he shall not save of that which he desired.

translated_text: There shall none of his meat be left; therefore shall no man look for his goods.
original_text: There shall none of his meat be left; therefore shall no man look for his goods.

translated_text: In the fulness of his sufficiency he shall be in straits: every hand of the wicked shall come upon him.
original_text: In the fulness of his sufficiency he shall be in straits: every hand of the wicked shall come upon him.

translated_text:
When he is about to fill his belly,
God shall cast the fury of his wrath upon him, and shall rain
it upon him while he is eating.
original_text:
When he is about to fill his belly,
God shall cast the fury of his wrath upon him, and shall rain
it upon him while he is eating.

translated_text:
He shall flee from the iron weapon,
and the bow of steel shall strike him through.
original_text:
He shall flee from the iron weapon,
and the bow of steel shall strike him through.

translated_text:
It is drawn, and cometh out of the body; yea, the glittering sword cometh out of his gall: terrors
are upon him.
original_text:
It is drawn, and cometh out of the body; yea, the glittering sword cometh out of his gall: terrors
are upon him.

translated_text:
All darkness
shall be hid in his secret places: a fire not blown shall consume him; it shall go ill with him that is left in his tabernacle.
original_text:
All darkness
shall be hid in his secret places: a fire not blown shall consume him; it shall go ill with him that is left in his tabernacle.

translated_text: The heaven shall reveal his iniquity; and the earth shall rise up against him.
original_text: The heaven shall reveal his iniquity; and the earth shall rise up against him.

translated_text:
The increase of his house shall depart,
and his goods shall flow away in the day of his wrath.
original_text:
The increase of his house shall depart,
and his goods shall flow away in the day of his wrath.

translated_text:
This
is the portion of a wicked man from God, and the heritage appointed unto him by God.
original_text:
This
is the portion of a wicked man from God, and the heritage appointed unto him by God.

translated_text: Moreover Job continued his parable, and said,
original_text: Moreover Job continued his parable, and said,

translated_text: My lips shall not speak wickedness, nor my tongue utter deceit.
original_text: My lips shall not speak wickedness, nor my tongue utter deceit.

translated_text: God forbid that I should justify you: till I die I will not remove mine integrity from me.
original_text: God forbid that I should justify you: till I die I will not remove mine integrity from me.

translated_text:
My righteousness I hold fast, and will not let it go: my heart shall not reproach
me so long as I live.
original_text:
My righteousness I hold fast, and will not let it go: my heart shall not reproach
me so long as I live.

translated_text: Let mine enemy be as the wicked, and he that riseth up against me as the unrighteous.
original_text: Let mine enemy be as the wicked, and he that riseth up against me as the unrighteous.

translated_text:
For what
is the hope of the hypocrite, though he hath gained, when God taketh away his soul?
original_text:
For what
is the hope of the hypocrite, though he hath gained, when God taketh away his soul?

translated_text: Will God hear his cry when trouble cometh upon him?
original_text: Will God hear his cry when trouble cometh upon him?

translated_text: Will he delight himself in the Almighty? will he always call upon God?
original_text: Will he delight himself in the Almighty? will he always call upon God?

translated_text:
I will teach you by the hand of God:
that which
is
 with the Almighty will I not conceal.
original_text:
I will teach you by the hand of God:
that which
is
 with the Almighty will I not conceal.

translated_text:
Behold, all ye yourselves have seen
it; why then are ye thus altogether vain?
original_text:
Behold, all ye yourselves have seen
it; why then are ye thus altogether vain?

translated_text:
This
is the portion of a wicked man with God, and the heritage of oppressors,
which they shall receive of the Almighty.
original_text:
This
is the portion of a wicked man with God, and the heritage of oppressors,
which they shall receive of the Almighty.

translated_text:
If his children be multiplied,
it is for the sword: and his offspring shall not be satisfied with bread.
original_text:
If his children be multiplied,
it is for the sword: and his offspring shall not be satisfied with bread.

translated_text: Those that remain of him shall be buried in death: and his widows shall not weep.
original_text: Those that remain of him shall be buried in death: and his widows shall not weep.

translated_text: Though he heap up silver as the dust, and prepare raiment as the clay;
original_text: Though he heap up silver as the dust, and prepare raiment as the clay;

translated_text:
He may prepare
it, but the just shall put
it on, and the innocent shall divide the silver.
original_text:
He may prepare
it, but the just shall put
it on, and the innocent shall divide the silver.

translated_text:
He buildeth his house as a moth, and as a booth
that the keeper maketh.
original_text:
He buildeth his house as a moth, and as a booth
that the keeper maketh.

translated_text:
The rich man shall lie down, but he shall not be gathered: he openeth his eyes, and he
is not.
original_text:
The rich man shall lie down, but he shall not be gathered: he openeth his eyes, and he
is not.

translated_text: Terrors take hold on him as waters, a tempest stealeth him away in the night.
original_text: Terrors take hold on him as waters, a tempest stealeth him away in the night.

translated_text: The east wind carrieth him away, and he departeth: and as a storm hurleth him out of his place.
original_text: The east wind carrieth him away, and he departeth: and as a storm hurleth him out of his place.

translated_text:
For
God shall cast upon him, and not spare: he would fain flee out of his hand.
original_text:
For
God shall cast upon him, and not spare: he would fain flee out of his hand.

translated_text: Men shall clap their hands at him, and shall hiss him out of his place.
original_text: Men shall clap their hands at him, and shall hiss him out of his place.

translated_text: But Job answered and said,
original_text: But Job answered and said,

translated_text:
How hast thou helped
him that is without power?
how
 savest thou the arm
that hath no strength?
original_text:
How hast thou helped
him that is without power?
how
 savest thou the arm
that hath no strength?

translated_text:
How hast thou counseled
him that hath no wisdom? and
how hast thou plentifully declared the thing as it is?
original_text:
How hast thou counseled
him that hath no wisdom? and
how hast thou plentifully declared the thing as it is?

translated_text: To whom hast thou uttered words? and whose spirit came from thee?
original_text: To whom hast thou uttered words? and whose spirit came from thee?

translated_text:
Dead
things are formed from under the waters, and the inhabitants thereof.
original_text:
Dead
things are formed from under the waters, and the inhabitants thereof.

translated_text:
Hell
is naked before him, and destruction hath no covering.
original_text:
Hell
is naked before him, and destruction hath no covering.

translated_text:
He stretcheth out the north over the empty place,
and hangeth the earth upon nothing.
original_text:
He stretcheth out the north over the empty place,
and hangeth the earth upon nothing.

translated_text: He bindeth up the waters in his thick clouds; and the cloud is not rent under them.
original_text: He bindeth up the waters in his thick clouds; and the cloud is not rent under them.

translated_text:
He holdeth back the face of his throne,
and spreadeth his cloud upon it.
original_text:
He holdeth back the face of his throne,
and spreadeth his cloud upon it.

translated_text: He hath compassed the waters with bounds, until the day and night come to an end.
original_text: He hath compassed the waters with bounds, until the day and night come to an end.

translated_text: The pillars of heaven tremble and are astonished at his reproof.
original_text: The pillars of heaven tremble and are astonished at his reproof.

translated_text: He divideth the sea with his power, and by his understanding he smiteth through the proud.
original_text: He divideth the sea with his power, and by his understanding he smiteth through the proud.

translated_text: By his spirit he hath garnished the heavens; his hand hath formed the crooked serpent.
original_text: By his spirit he hath garnished the heavens; his hand hath formed the crooked serpent.

translated_text:
Lo, these
are parts of his ways: but how little a portion is heard of him? but the thunder of his power who can understand?
original_text:
Lo, these
are parts of his ways: but how little a portion is heard of him? but the thunder of his power who can understand?

translated_text: Then answered Bildad the Shuhite, and said,
original_text: Then answered Bildad the Shuhite, and said,

translated_text:
Dominion and fear
are with him, he maketh peace in his high places.
original_text:
Dominion and fear
are with him, he maketh peace in his high places.

translated_text: Is there any number of his armies? and upon whom doth not his light arise?
original_text: Is there any number of his armies? and upon whom doth not his light arise?

translated_text:
How then can man be justified with God? or how can he be clean
that is born of a woman?
original_text:
How then can man be justified with God? or how can he be clean
that is born of a woman?

translated_text: Behold even to the moon, and it shineth not; yea, the stars are not pure in his sight.
original_text: Behold even to the moon, and it shineth not; yea, the stars are not pure in his sight.

translated_text:
How much less man,
that is a worm? and the son of man,
which is a worm?
original_text:
How much less man,
that is a worm? and the son of man,
which is a worm?

translated_text: Why, seeing times are not hidden from the Almighty, do they that know him not see his days?
original_text: Why, seeing times are not hidden from the Almighty, do they that know him not see his days?

translated_text:
Some remove the landmarks; they violently take away flocks, and feed
thereof.
original_text:
Some remove the landmarks; they violently take away flocks, and feed
thereof.

translated_text: They drive away the ass of the fatherless, they take the widow’s ox for a pledge.
original_text: They drive away the ass of the fatherless, they take the widow’s ox for a pledge.

translated_text: They turn the needy out of the way: the poor of the earth hide themselves together.
original_text: They turn the needy out of the way: the poor of the earth hide themselves together.

translated_text:
Behold,
as wild asses in the desert, go they forth to their work; rising betimes for a prey: the wilderness
yieldeth food for them
and for
their children.
original_text:
Behold,
as wild asses in the desert, go they forth to their work; rising betimes for a prey: the wilderness
yieldeth food for them
and for
their children.

translated_text:
They reap
every one his corn in the field: and they gather the vintage of the wicked.
original_text:
They reap
every one his corn in the field: and they gather the vintage of the wicked.

translated_text:
They cause the naked to lodge without clothing, that
they have
 no covering in the cold.
original_text:
They cause the naked to lodge without clothing, that
they have
 no covering in the cold.

translated_text: They are wet with the showers of the mountains, and embrace the rock for want of a shelter.
original_text: They are wet with the showers of the mountains, and embrace the rock for want of a shelter.

translated_text: They pluck the fatherless from the breast, and take a pledge of the poor.
original_text: They pluck the fatherless from the breast, and take a pledge of the poor.

translated_text:
Which make oil within their walls,
and tread
their winepresses, and suffer thirst.
original_text:
Which make oil within their walls,
and tread
their winepresses, and suffer thirst.

translated_text:
Men groan from out of the city, and the soul of the wounded crieth out: yet God layeth not folly
to them.
original_text:
Men groan from out of the city, and the soul of the wounded crieth out: yet God layeth not folly
to them.

translated_text: They are of those that rebel against the light; they know not the ways thereof, nor abide in the paths thereof.
original_text: They are of those that rebel against the light; they know not the ways thereof, nor abide in the paths thereof.

translated_text: The murderer rising with the light killeth the poor and needy, and in the night is as a thief.
original_text: The murderer rising with the light killeth the poor and needy, and in the night is as a thief.

translated_text:
The eye also of the adulterer waiteth for the twilight, saying, No eye shall see me: and disguiseth
his face.
original_text:
The eye also of the adulterer waiteth for the twilight, saying, No eye shall see me: and disguiseth
his face.

translated_text:
In the dark they dig through houses,
which they had marked for themselves in the daytime: they know not the light.
original_text:
In the dark they dig through houses,
which they had marked for themselves in the daytime: they know not the light.

translated_text:
For the morning
is to them even as the shadow of death: if
one know
them, they are in the terrors of the shadow of death.
original_text:
For the morning
is to them even as the shadow of death: if
one know
them, they are in the terrors of the shadow of death.

translated_text:
He
is swift as the waters; their portion is cursed in the earth: he beholdeth not the way of the vineyards.
original_text:
He
is swift as the waters; their portion is cursed in the earth: he beholdeth not the way of the vineyards.

translated_text:
Drought and heat consume the snow waters:
so doth the grave
those which have sinned.
original_text:
Drought and heat consume the snow waters:
so doth the grave
those which have sinned.

translated_text: The womb shall forget him; the worm shall feed sweetly on him; he shall be no more remembered; and wickedness shall be broken as a tree.
original_text: The womb shall forget him; the worm shall feed sweetly on him; he shall be no more remembered; and wickedness shall be broken as a tree.

translated_text:
He evil entreateth the barren that
beareth not: and doeth not good to the widow.
original_text:
He evil entreateth the barren that
beareth not: and doeth not good to the widow.

translated_text:
He draweth also the mighty with his power: he riseth up, and no
man is sure of life.
original_text:
He draweth also the mighty with his power: he riseth up, and no
man is sure of life.

translated_text:
Though it be given him
to be in safety, whereon he resteth; yet his eyes
are upon their ways.
original_text:
Though it be given him
to be in safety, whereon he resteth; yet his eyes
are upon their ways.

translated_text:
They are exalted for a little while, but are gone and brought low; they are taken out of the way as all
other, and cut off as the tops of the ears of corn.
original_text:
They are exalted for a little while, but are gone and brought low; they are taken out of the way as all
other, and cut off as the tops of the ears of corn.

translated_text:
And if
it be not
so now, who will make me a liar, and make my speech nothing worth?
original_text:
And if
it be not
so now, who will make me a liar, and make my speech nothing worth?

translated_text:
But now
they that are younger than I have me in derision, whose fathers I would have disdained to have set with the dogs of my flock.
original_text:
But now
they that are younger than I have me in derision, whose fathers I would have disdained to have set with the dogs of my flock.

translated_text:
Yea, whereto
might the strength of their hands
profit
 me, in whom old age was perished?
original_text:
Yea, whereto
might the strength of their hands
profit
 me, in whom old age was perished?

translated_text:
For want and famine
they were solitary; fleeing into the wilderness in former time desolate and waste.
original_text:
For want and famine
they were solitary; fleeing into the wilderness in former time desolate and waste.

translated_text:
Who cut up mallows by the bushes, and juniper roots
for their meat.
original_text:
Who cut up mallows by the bushes, and juniper roots
for their meat.

translated_text:
They were driven forth from among
men, (they cried after them as
after a thief;)
original_text:
They were driven forth from among
men, (they cried after them as
after a thief;)

translated_text:
To dwell in the cliffs of the valleys,
in caves of the earth, and
in the rocks.
original_text:
To dwell in the cliffs of the valleys,
in caves of the earth, and
in the rocks.

translated_text: Among the bushes they brayed; under the nettles they were gathered together.
original_text: Among the bushes they brayed; under the nettles they were gathered together.

translated_text: They were children of fools, yea, children of base men: they were viler than the earth.
original_text: They were children of fools, yea, children of base men: they were viler than the earth.

translated_text: And now am I their song, yea, I am their byword.
original_text: And now am I their song, yea, I am their byword.

translated_text: They abhor me, they flee far from me, and spare not to spit in my face.
original_text: They abhor me, they flee far from me, and spare not to spit in my face.

translated_text: Because he hath loosed my cord, and afflicted me, they have also let loose the bridle before me.
original_text: Because he hath loosed my cord, and afflicted me, they have also let loose the bridle before me.

translated_text:
Upon
my right
hand rise the youth; they push away my feet, and they raise up against me the ways of their destruction.
original_text:
Upon
my right
hand rise the youth; they push away my feet, and they raise up against me the ways of their destruction.

translated_text: They mar my path, they set forward my calamity, they have no helper.
original_text: They mar my path, they set forward my calamity, they have no helper.

translated_text:
They came
upon me as a wide breaking in
of waters:
 in the desolation they rolled themselves
upon me.
original_text:
They came
upon me as a wide breaking in
of waters:
 in the desolation they rolled themselves
upon me.

translated_text: Terrors are turned upon me: they pursue my soul as the wind: and my welfare passeth away as a cloud.
original_text: Terrors are turned upon me: they pursue my soul as the wind: and my welfare passeth away as a cloud.

translated_text: And now my soul is poured out upon me; the days of affliction have taken hold upon me.
original_text: And now my soul is poured out upon me; the days of affliction have taken hold upon me.

translated_text: My bones are pierced in me in the night season: and my sinews take no rest.
original_text: My bones are pierced in me in the night season: and my sinews take no rest.

translated_text:
By the great force
of my disease is my garment changed: it bindeth me about as the collar of my coat.
original_text:
By the great force
of my disease is my garment changed: it bindeth me about as the collar of my coat.

translated_text: He hath cast me into the mire, and I am become like dust and ashes.
original_text: He hath cast me into the mire, and I am become like dust and ashes.

translated_text:
I cry unto thee, and thou dost not hear me: I stand up, and thou regardest me
not.
original_text:
I cry unto thee, and thou dost not hear me: I stand up, and thou regardest me
not.

translated_text: Thou art become cruel to me: with thy strong hand thou opposest thyself against me.
original_text: Thou art become cruel to me: with thy strong hand thou opposest thyself against me.

translated_text:
Thou liftest me up to the wind; thou causest me to ride
upon it,
 and dissolvest my substance.
original_text:
Thou liftest me up to the wind; thou causest me to ride
upon it,
 and dissolvest my substance.

translated_text:
For I know
that thou wilt bring me
to death, and
to the house appointed for all living.
original_text:
For I know
that thou wilt bring me
to death, and
to the house appointed for all living.

translated_text:
Howbeit he will not stretch out
his hand to the grave, though they cry in his destruction.
original_text:
Howbeit he will not stretch out
his hand to the grave, though they cry in his destruction.

translated_text:
Did not I weep for him that was in trouble? was
not my soul grieved for the poor?
original_text:
Did not I weep for him that was in trouble? was
not my soul grieved for the poor?

translated_text:
When I looked for good, then evil came
unto me: and when I waited for light, there came darkness.
original_text:
When I looked for good, then evil came
unto me: and when I waited for light, there came darkness.

translated_text: My bowels boiled, and rested not: the days of affliction prevented me.
original_text: My bowels boiled, and rested not: the days of affliction prevented me.

translated_text:
I went mourning without the sun: I stood up,
and I cried in the congregation.
original_text:
I went mourning without the sun: I stood up,
and I cried in the congregation.

translated_text: I am a brother to dragons, and a companion to owls.
original_text: I am a brother to dragons, and a companion to owls.

translated_text: My skin is black upon me, and my bones are burned with heat.
original_text: My skin is black upon me, and my bones are burned with heat.

translated_text:
My harp also is
turned to mourning, and my organ into the voice of them that weep.
original_text:
My harp also is
turned to mourning, and my organ into the voice of them that weep.

translated_text: Then Job answered the LORD, and said,
original_text: Then Job answered the LORD, and said,

translated_text:
I know that thou canst do every
thing, and
that
 no thought can be withholden from thee.
original_text:
I know that thou canst do every
thing, and
that
 no thought can be withholden from thee.

translated_text:
Who
is he that hideth counsel without knowledge? therefore have I uttered that I understood not; things too wonderful for me, which I knew not.
original_text:
Who
is he that hideth counsel without knowledge? therefore have I uttered that I understood not; things too wonderful for me, which I knew not.

translated_text: Hear, I beseech thee, and I will speak: I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me.
original_text: Hear, I beseech thee, and I will speak: I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me.

translated_text: I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye seeth thee.
original_text: I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye seeth thee.

translated_text:
Wherefore I abhor
myself, and repent in dust and ashes.
original_text:
Wherefore I abhor
myself, and repent in dust and ashes.

translated_text:
And it was
so, that after the LORD had spoken these words unto Job, the LORD said to Eliphaz the Temanite, My wrath is kindled against thee, and against thy two friends: for ye have not spoken of me
the thing that is right, as my servant Job
hath.
original_text:
And it was
so, that after the LORD had spoken these words unto Job, the LORD said to Eliphaz the Temanite, My wrath is kindled against thee, and against thy two friends: for ye have not spoken of me
the thing that is right, as my servant Job
hath.

translated_text:
Therefore take unto you now seven bullocks and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering; and my servant Job shall pray for you: for him will I accept: lest I deal with you
after your folly, in that ye have not spoken of me
the thing which is
 right, like my servant Job.
original_text:
Therefore take unto you now seven bullocks and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering; and my servant Job shall pray for you: for him will I accept: lest I deal with you
after your folly, in that ye have not spoken of me
the thing which is
 right, like my servant Job.

translated_text:
So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite
and Zophar the Naamathite went, and did according as the LORD commanded them: the LORD also accepted Job.
original_text:
So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite
and Zophar the Naamathite went, and did according as the LORD commanded them: the LORD also accepted Job.

translated_text: And the LORD turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends: also the LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before.
original_text: And the LORD turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends: also the LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before.

translated_text: Then came there unto him all his brethren, and all his sisters, and all they that had been of his acquaintance before, and did eat bread with him in his house: and they bemoaned him, and comforted him over all the evil that the LORD had brought upon him: every man also gave him a piece of money, and every one an earring of gold.
original_text: Then came there unto him all his brethren, and all his sisters, and all they that had been of his acquaintance before, and did eat bread with him in his house: and they bemoaned him, and comforted him over all the evil that the LORD had brought upon him: every man also gave him a piece of money, and every one an earring of gold.

translated_text: So the LORD blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning: for he had fourteen thousand sheep, and six thousand camels, and a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she asses.
original_text: So the LORD blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning: for he had fourteen thousand sheep, and six thousand camels, and a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she asses.

translated_text: He had also seven sons and three daughters.
original_text: He had also seven sons and three daughters.

translated_text: And he called the name of the first, Jemima; and the name of the second, Kezia; and the name of the third, Keren-happuch.
original_text: And he called the name of the first, Jemima; and the name of the second, Kezia; and the name of the third, Keren-happuch.

translated_text:
And in all the land were no women found
so fair as the daughters of Job: and their father gave them inheritance among their brethren.
original_text:
And in all the land were no women found
so fair as the daughters of Job: and their father gave them inheritance among their brethren.

translated_text:
After this lived Job an hundred and forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons’ sons,
even four generations.
original_text:
After this lived Job an hundred and forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons’ sons,
even four generations.

translated_text:
So Job died,
being old and full of days.
original_text:
So Job died,
being old and full of days.

translated_text: Then Job answered and said,
original_text: Then Job answered and said,

translated_text: How long will ye vex my soul, and break me in pieces with words?
original_text: How long will ye vex my soul, and break me in pieces with words?

translated_text:
These ten times have ye reproached me: ye are not ashamed
that
 ye make yourselves strange to me.
original_text:
These ten times have ye reproached me: ye are not ashamed
that
 ye make yourselves strange to me.

translated_text:
And be it indeed
that I have erred, mine error remaineth with myself.
original_text:
And be it indeed
that I have erred, mine error remaineth with myself.

translated_text:
If indeed ye will magnify
yourselves against me, and plead against me my reproach:
original_text:
If indeed ye will magnify
yourselves against me, and plead against me my reproach:

translated_text: Know now that God hath overthrown me, and hath compassed me with his net.
original_text: Know now that God hath overthrown me, and hath compassed me with his net.

translated_text:
Behold, I cry out of wrong, but I am not heard: I cry aloud, but
there is no judgment.
original_text:
Behold, I cry out of wrong, but I am not heard: I cry aloud, but
there is no judgment.

translated_text: He hath fenced up my way that I cannot pass, and he hath set darkness in my paths.
original_text: He hath fenced up my way that I cannot pass, and he hath set darkness in my paths.

translated_text:
He hath stripped me of my glory, and taken the crown
from
 my head.
original_text:
He hath stripped me of my glory, and taken the crown
from
 my head.

translated_text: He hath destroyed me on every side, and I am gone: and mine hope hath he removed like a tree.
original_text: He hath destroyed me on every side, and I am gone: and mine hope hath he removed like a tree.

translated_text:
He hath also kindled his wrath against me, and he counteth me unto him as
one of his enemies.
original_text:
He hath also kindled his wrath against me, and he counteth me unto him as
one of his enemies.

translated_text: His troops come together, and raise up their way against me, and encamp round about my tabernacle.
original_text: His troops come together, and raise up their way against me, and encamp round about my tabernacle.

translated_text: He hath put my brethren far from me, and mine acquaintance are verily estranged from me.
original_text: He hath put my brethren far from me, and mine acquaintance are verily estranged from me.

translated_text: My kinsfolk have failed, and my familiar friends have forgotten me.
original_text: My kinsfolk have failed, and my familiar friends have forgotten me.

translated_text: They that dwell in mine house, and my maids, count me for a stranger: I am an alien in their sight.
original_text: They that dwell in mine house, and my maids, count me for a stranger: I am an alien in their sight.

translated_text:
I called my servant, and he gave
me no answer; I intreated him with my mouth.
original_text:
I called my servant, and he gave
me no answer; I intreated him with my mouth.

translated_text:
My breath is strange to my wife, though I intreated for the children’s
sake of mine own body.
original_text:
My breath is strange to my wife, though I intreated for the children’s
sake of mine own body.

translated_text: Yea, young children despised me; I arose, and they spake against me.
original_text: Yea, young children despised me; I arose, and they spake against me.

translated_text: All my inward friends abhorred me: and they whom I loved are turned against me.
original_text: All my inward friends abhorred me: and they whom I loved are turned against me.

translated_text: My bone cleaveth to my skin and to my flesh, and I am escaped with the skin of my teeth.
original_text: My bone cleaveth to my skin and to my flesh, and I am escaped with the skin of my teeth.

translated_text: Have pity upon me, have pity upon me, O ye my friends; for the hand of God hath touched me.
original_text: Have pity upon me, have pity upon me, O ye my friends; for the hand of God hath touched me.

translated_text: Why do ye persecute me as God, and are not satisfied with my flesh?
original_text: Why do ye persecute me as God, and are not satisfied with my flesh?

translated_text: Oh that my words were now written! oh that they were printed in a book!
original_text: Oh that my words were now written! oh that they were printed in a book!

translated_text: That they were graven with an iron pen and lead in the rock for ever!
original_text: That they were graven with an iron pen and lead in the rock for ever!

translated_text:
For I know
that my redeemer liveth, and
that he shall stand at the latter
day upon the earth:
original_text:
For I know
that my redeemer liveth, and
that he shall stand at the latter
day upon the earth:

translated_text:
And
though after my skin
worms destroy this
body, yet in my flesh shall I see God:
original_text:
And
though after my skin
worms destroy this
body, yet in my flesh shall I see God:

translated_text:
Whom I shall see for myself, and mine eyes shall behold, and not another;
though my reins be consumed within me.
original_text:
Whom I shall see for myself, and mine eyes shall behold, and not another;
though my reins be consumed within me.

translated_text: But ye should say, Why persecute we him, seeing the root of the matter is found in me?
original_text: But ye should say, Why persecute we him, seeing the root of the matter is found in me?

translated_text:
Be ye afraid of the sword: for wrath
bringeth the punishments of the sword, that ye may know
there is a judgment.
original_text:
Be ye afraid of the sword: for wrath
bringeth the punishments of the sword, that ye may know
there is a judgment.

translated_text: Then answered Bildad the Shuhite, and said,
original_text: Then answered Bildad the Shuhite, and said,

translated_text:
How long
will it be ere ye make an end of words? mark, and afterwards we will speak.
original_text:
How long
will it be ere ye make an end of words? mark, and afterwards we will speak.

translated_text:
Wherefore are we counted as beasts,
and reputed vile in your sight?
original_text:
Wherefore are we counted as beasts,
and reputed vile in your sight?

translated_text: He teareth himself in his anger: shall the earth be forsaken for thee? and shall the rock be removed out of his place?
original_text: He teareth himself in his anger: shall the earth be forsaken for thee? and shall the rock be removed out of his place?

translated_text: Yea, the light of the wicked shall be put out, and the spark of his fire shall not shine.
original_text: Yea, the light of the wicked shall be put out, and the spark of his fire shall not shine.

translated_text: The light shall be dark in his tabernacle, and his candle shall be put out with him.
original_text: The light shall be dark in his tabernacle, and his candle shall be put out with him.

translated_text: The steps of his strength shall be straitened, and his own counsel shall cast him down.
original_text: The steps of his strength shall be straitened, and his own counsel shall cast him down.

translated_text: For he is cast into a net by his own feet, and he walketh upon a snare.
original_text: For he is cast into a net by his own feet, and he walketh upon a snare.

translated_text:
The gin shall take
him by the heel,
and the robber shall prevail against him.
original_text:
The gin shall take
him by the heel,
and the robber shall prevail against him.

translated_text:
The snare
is laid for him in the ground, and a trap for him in the way.
original_text:
The snare
is laid for him in the ground, and a trap for him in the way.

translated_text: Terrors shall make him afraid on every side, and shall drive him to his feet.
original_text: Terrors shall make him afraid on every side, and shall drive him to his feet.

translated_text:
His strength shall be hungerbitten, and destruction
shall be
 ready at his side.
original_text:
His strength shall be hungerbitten, and destruction
shall be
 ready at his side.

translated_text:
It shall devour the strength of his skin:
even the firstborn of death shall devour his strength.
original_text:
It shall devour the strength of his skin:
even the firstborn of death shall devour his strength.

translated_text: His confidence shall be rooted out of his tabernacle, and it shall bring him to the king of terrors.
original_text: His confidence shall be rooted out of his tabernacle, and it shall bring him to the king of terrors.

translated_text:
It shall dwell in his tabernacle, because
it is none of his: brimstone shall be scattered upon his habitation.
original_text:
It shall dwell in his tabernacle, because
it is none of his: brimstone shall be scattered upon his habitation.

translated_text: His roots shall be dried up beneath, and above shall his branch be cut off.
original_text: His roots shall be dried up beneath, and above shall his branch be cut off.

translated_text: His remembrance shall perish from the earth, and he shall have no name in the street.
original_text: His remembrance shall perish from the earth, and he shall have no name in the street.

translated_text: He shall be driven from light into darkness, and chased out of the world.
original_text: He shall be driven from light into darkness, and chased out of the world.

translated_text: He shall neither have son nor nephew among his people, nor any remaining in his dwellings.
original_text: He shall neither have son nor nephew among his people, nor any remaining in his dwellings.

translated_text:
They that come after
him shall be astonied at his day, as they that went before were affrighted.
original_text:
They that come after
him shall be astonied at his day, as they that went before were affrighted.

translated_text:
Surely such
are the dwellings of the wicked, and this
is the place
of him that knoweth not God.
original_text:
Surely such
are the dwellings of the wicked, and this
is the place
of him that knoweth not God.

translated_text:
My breath is corrupt, my days are extinct, the graves
are ready
 for me.
original_text:
My breath is corrupt, my days are extinct, the graves
are ready
 for me.

translated_text: Are there not mockers with me? and doth not mine eye continue in their provocation?
original_text: Are there not mockers with me? and doth not mine eye continue in their provocation?

translated_text:
Lay down now, put me in a surety with thee; who
is he
that will strike hands with me?
original_text:
Lay down now, put me in a surety with thee; who
is he
that will strike hands with me?

translated_text:
For thou hast hid their heart from understanding: therefore shalt thou not exalt
them.
original_text:
For thou hast hid their heart from understanding: therefore shalt thou not exalt
them.

translated_text:
He that speaketh flattery to
his friends, even the eyes of his children shall fail.
original_text:
He that speaketh flattery to
his friends, even the eyes of his children shall fail.

translated_text: He hath made me also a byword of the people; and aforetime I was as a tabret.
original_text: He hath made me also a byword of the people; and aforetime I was as a tabret.

translated_text:
Mine eye also is dim by reason of sorrow, and all my members
are
 as a shadow.
original_text:
Mine eye also is dim by reason of sorrow, and all my members
are
 as a shadow.

translated_text:
Upright
men shall be astonied at this, and the innocent shall stir up himself against the hypocrite.
original_text:
Upright
men shall be astonied at this, and the innocent shall stir up himself against the hypocrite.

translated_text: The righteous also shall hold on his way, and he that hath clean hands shall be stronger and stronger.
original_text: The righteous also shall hold on his way, and he that hath clean hands shall be stronger and stronger.

translated_text:
But as for you all, do ye return, and come now: for I cannot find
one wise
man among you.
original_text:
But as for you all, do ye return, and come now: for I cannot find
one wise
man among you.

translated_text:
My days are past, my purposes are broken off,
even the thoughts of my heart.
original_text:
My days are past, my purposes are broken off,
even the thoughts of my heart.

translated_text:
They change the night into day: the light
is short because of darkness.
original_text:
They change the night into day: the light
is short because of darkness.

translated_text:
If I wait, the grave
is mine house: I have made my bed in the darkness.
original_text:
If I wait, the grave
is mine house: I have made my bed in the darkness.

translated_text:
I have said to corruption, Thou
art my father: to the worm,
Thou art my mother, and my sister.
original_text:
I have said to corruption, Thou
art my father: to the worm,
Thou art my mother, and my sister.

translated_text:
And where
is now my hope? as for my hope, who shall see it?
original_text:
And where
is now my hope? as for my hope, who shall see it?

translated_text:
They shall go down to the bars of the pit, when
our rest together
is in the dust.
original_text:
They shall go down to the bars of the pit, when
our rest together
is in the dust.

translated_text: And Job answered and said,
original_text: And Job answered and said,

translated_text:
No doubt but ye
are the people, and wisdom shall die with you.
original_text:
No doubt but ye
are the people, and wisdom shall die with you.

translated_text:
But I have understanding as well as you; I
am not inferior to you: yea, who knoweth not such things as these?
original_text:
But I have understanding as well as you; I
am not inferior to you: yea, who knoweth not such things as these?

translated_text:
I am
as one mocked of his neighbour, who calleth upon God, and he answereth him: the just upright
man is laughed to scorn.
original_text:
I am
as one mocked of his neighbour, who calleth upon God, and he answereth him: the just upright
man is laughed to scorn.

translated_text:
He that is ready to slip with
his feet
is as a lamp despised in the thought of him that is at ease.
original_text:
He that is ready to slip with
his feet
