translated_text: Let him drink, and forget his poverty, and remember his misery no more.
original_text: Let him drink, and forget his poverty, and remember his misery no more.

translated_text: Open thy mouth for the dumb in the cause of all such as are appointed to destruction.
original_text: Open thy mouth for the dumb in the cause of all such as are appointed to destruction.

translated_text: Open thy mouth, judge righteously, and plead the cause of the poor and needy.
original_text: Open thy mouth, judge righteously, and plead the cause of the poor and needy.

translated_text:
Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price
is far above rubies.
original_text:
Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price
is far above rubies.

translated_text: The heart of her husband doth safely trust in her, so that he shall have no need of spoil.
original_text: The heart of her husband doth safely trust in her, so that he shall have no need of spoil.

translated_text: She will do him good and not evil all the days of her life.
original_text: She will do him good and not evil all the days of her life.

translated_text: She seeketh wool, and flax, and worketh willingly with her hands.
original_text: She seeketh wool, and flax, and worketh willingly with her hands.

translated_text: She is like the merchants’ ships; she bringeth her food from afar.
original_text: She is like the merchants’ ships; she bringeth her food from afar.

translated_text: She riseth also while it is yet night, and giveth meat to her household, and a portion to her maidens.
original_text: She riseth also while it is yet night, and giveth meat to her household, and a portion to her maidens.

translated_text: She considereth a field, and buyeth it: with the fruit of her hands she planteth a vineyard.
original_text: She considereth a field, and buyeth it: with the fruit of her hands she planteth a vineyard.

translated_text: She girdeth her loins with strength, and strengtheneth her arms.
original_text: She girdeth her loins with strength, and strengtheneth her arms.

translated_text:
She perceiveth that her merchandise
is good: her candle goeth not out by night.
original_text:
She perceiveth that her merchandise
is good: her candle goeth not out by night.

translated_text: She layeth her hands to the spindle, and her hands hold the distaff.
original_text: She layeth her hands to the spindle, and her hands hold the distaff.

translated_text: She stretcheth out her hand to the poor; yea, she reacheth forth her hands to the needy.
original_text: She stretcheth out her hand to the poor; yea, she reacheth forth her hands to the needy.

translated_text:
She is not afraid of the snow for her household: for all her household
are clothed with scarlet.
original_text:
She is not afraid of the snow for her household: for all her household
are clothed with scarlet.

translated_text:
She maketh herself coverings of tapestry; her clothing
is
 silk and purple.
original_text:
She maketh herself coverings of tapestry; her clothing
is
 silk and purple.

translated_text: Her husband is known in the gates, when he sitteth among the elders of the land.
original_text: Her husband is known in the gates, when he sitteth among the elders of the land.

translated_text:
She maketh fine linen, and selleth
it; and delivereth girdles unto the merchant.
original_text:
She maketh fine linen, and selleth
it; and delivereth girdles unto the merchant.

translated_text:
Strength and honour
are her clothing; and she shall rejoice in time to come.
original_text:
Strength and honour
are her clothing; and she shall rejoice in time to come.

translated_text:
She openeth her mouth with wisdom; and in her tongue
is the law of kindness.
original_text:
She openeth her mouth with wisdom; and in her tongue
is the law of kindness.

translated_text: She looketh well to the ways of her household, and eateth not the bread of idleness.
original_text: She looketh well to the ways of her household, and eateth not the bread of idleness.

translated_text:
Her children arise up, and call her blessed; her husband
also,
 and he praiseth her.
original_text:
Her children arise up, and call her blessed; her husband
also,
 and he praiseth her.

translated_text: Many daughters have done virtuously, but thou excellest them all.
original_text: Many daughters have done virtuously, but thou excellest them all.

translated_text:
Favour
is deceitful, and beauty
is vain:
but
 a woman
that feareth the LORD, she shall be praised.
original_text:
Favour
is deceitful, and beauty
is vain:
but
 a woman
that feareth the LORD, she shall be praised.

translated_text: Give her of the fruit of her hands; and let her own works praise her in the gates.
original_text: Give her of the fruit of her hands; and let her own works praise her in the gates.

translated_text:
The king’s heart
is in the hand of the LORD,
as
 the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will.
original_text:
The king’s heart
is in the hand of the LORD,
as
 the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will.

translated_text:
Every way of a man
is right in his own eyes: but the LORD pondereth the hearts.
original_text:
Every way of a man
is right in his own eyes: but the LORD pondereth the hearts.

translated_text:
To do justice and judgment
is more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice.
original_text:
To do justice and judgment
is more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice.

translated_text:
An high look, and a proud heart,
and the plowing of the wicked,
is sin.
original_text:
An high look, and a proud heart,
and the plowing of the wicked,
is sin.

translated_text:
The thoughts of the diligent
tend only to plenteousness; but of every one
that is hasty only to want.
original_text:
The thoughts of the diligent
tend only to plenteousness; but of every one
that is hasty only to want.

translated_text:
The getting of treasures by a lying tongue
is a vanity tossed to and fro of them that seek death.
original_text:
The getting of treasures by a lying tongue
is a vanity tossed to and fro of them that seek death.

translated_text: The robbery of the wicked shall destroy them; because they refuse to do judgment.
original_text: The robbery of the wicked shall destroy them; because they refuse to do judgment.

translated_text:
The way of man
is froward and strange: but
as for
 the pure, his work
is right.
original_text:
The way of man
is froward and strange: but
as for
 the pure, his work
is right.

translated_text: It is better to dwell in a corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman in a wide house.
original_text: It is better to dwell in a corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman in a wide house.

translated_text: The soul of the wicked desireth evil: his neighbour findeth no favour in his eyes.
original_text: The soul of the wicked desireth evil: his neighbour findeth no favour in his eyes.

translated_text: When the scorner is punished, the simple is made wise: and when the wise is instructed, he receiveth knowledge.
original_text: When the scorner is punished, the simple is made wise: and when the wise is instructed, he receiveth knowledge.

translated_text:
The righteous
man wisely considereth the house of the wicked:
but God overthroweth the wicked for
their wickedness.
original_text:
The righteous
man wisely considereth the house of the wicked:
but God overthroweth the wicked for
their wickedness.

translated_text: Whoso stoppeth his ears at the cry of the poor, he also shall cry himself, but shall not be heard.
original_text: Whoso stoppeth his ears at the cry of the poor, he also shall cry himself, but shall not be heard.

translated_text: A gift in secret pacifieth anger: and a reward in the bosom strong wrath.
original_text: A gift in secret pacifieth anger: and a reward in the bosom strong wrath.

translated_text:
It is joy to the just to do judgment: but destruction
shall be to the workers of iniquity.
original_text:
It is joy to the just to do judgment: but destruction
shall be to the workers of iniquity.

translated_text: The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.
original_text: The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.

translated_text:
He that loveth pleasure
shall be a poor man: he that loveth wine and oil shall not be rich.
original_text:
He that loveth pleasure
shall be a poor man: he that loveth wine and oil shall not be rich.

translated_text:
The wicked
shall be a ransom for the righteous, and the transgressor for the upright.
original_text:
The wicked
shall be a ransom for the righteous, and the transgressor for the upright.

translated_text: It is better to dwell in the wilderness, than with a contentious and an angry woman.
original_text: It is better to dwell in the wilderness, than with a contentious and an angry woman.

translated_text: There is treasure to be desired and oil in the dwelling of the wise; but a foolish man spendeth it up.
original_text: There is treasure to be desired and oil in the dwelling of the wise; but a foolish man spendeth it up.

translated_text: He that followeth after righteousness and mercy findeth life, righteousness, and honour.
original_text: He that followeth after righteousness and mercy findeth life, righteousness, and honour.

translated_text:
A wise
man scaleth the city of the mighty, and casteth down the strength of the confidence thereof.
original_text:
A wise
man scaleth the city of the mighty, and casteth down the strength of the confidence thereof.

translated_text: Whoso keepeth his mouth and his tongue keepeth his soul from troubles.
original_text: Whoso keepeth his mouth and his tongue keepeth his soul from troubles.

translated_text:
Proud
and haughty scorner
is his name, who dealeth in proud wrath.
original_text:
Proud
and haughty scorner
is his name, who dealeth in proud wrath.

translated_text: The desire of the slothful killeth him; for his hands refuse to labour.
original_text: The desire of the slothful killeth him; for his hands refuse to labour.

translated_text: He coveteth greedily all the day long: but the righteous giveth and spareth not.
original_text: He coveteth greedily all the day long: but the righteous giveth and spareth not.

translated_text:
The sacrifice of the wicked
is abomination: how much more,
when he bringeth it with a wicked mind?
original_text:
The sacrifice of the wicked
is abomination: how much more,
when he bringeth it with a wicked mind?

translated_text: A false witness shall perish: but the man that heareth speaketh constantly.
original_text: A false witness shall perish: but the man that heareth speaketh constantly.

translated_text:
A wicked man hardeneth his face: but
as for the upright, he directeth his way.
original_text:
A wicked man hardeneth his face: but
as for the upright, he directeth his way.

translated_text: There is no wisdom nor understanding nor counsel against the LORD.
original_text: There is no wisdom nor understanding nor counsel against the LORD.

translated_text:
The horse
is prepared against the day of battle: but safety
is of the LORD.
original_text:
The horse
is prepared against the day of battle: but safety
is of the LORD.

translated_text:
Wine
is a mocker, strong drink
is raging: and whosoever is deceived thereby is not wise.
original_text:
Wine
is a mocker, strong drink
is raging: and whosoever is deceived thereby is not wise.

translated_text:
The fear of a king
is as the roaring of a lion:
whoso
 provoketh him to anger sinneth
against his own soul.
original_text:
The fear of a king
is as the roaring of a lion:
whoso
 provoketh him to anger sinneth
against his own soul.

translated_text: It is an honour for a man to cease from strife: but every fool will be meddling.
original_text: It is an honour for a man to cease from strife: but every fool will be meddling.

translated_text:
The sluggard will not plow by reason of the cold;
therefore
 shall he beg in harvest, and
have nothing.
original_text:
The sluggard will not plow by reason of the cold;
therefore
 shall he beg in harvest, and
have nothing.

translated_text:
Counsel in the heart of man
is like deep water; but a man of understanding will draw it out.
original_text:
Counsel in the heart of man
is like deep water; but a man of understanding will draw it out.

translated_text: Most men will proclaim every one his own goodness: but a faithful man who can find?
original_text: Most men will proclaim every one his own goodness: but a faithful man who can find?

translated_text:
The just
man walketh in his integrity: his children
are
 blessed after him.
original_text:
The just
man walketh in his integrity: his children
are
 blessed after him.

translated_text: A king that sitteth in the throne of judgment scattereth away all evil with his eyes.
original_text: A king that sitteth in the throne of judgment scattereth away all evil with his eyes.

translated_text: Who can say, I have made my heart clean, I am pure from my sin?
original_text: Who can say, I have made my heart clean, I am pure from my sin?

translated_text:
Divers weights,
and divers measures, both of them
are
 alike abomination to the LORD.
original_text:
Divers weights,
and divers measures, both of them
are
 alike abomination to the LORD.

translated_text:
Even a child is known by his doings, whether his work
be
 pure, and whether
it be right.
original_text:
Even a child is known by his doings, whether his work
be
 pure, and whether
it be right.

translated_text: The hearing ear, and the seeing eye, the LORD hath made even both of them.
original_text: The hearing ear, and the seeing eye, the LORD hath made even both of them.

translated_text:
Love not sleep, lest thou come to poverty; open thine eyes,
and
 thou shalt be satisfied with bread.
original_text:
Love not sleep, lest thou come to poverty; open thine eyes,
and
 thou shalt be satisfied with bread.

translated_text:
It is naught,
it is naught, saith the buyer: but when he is gone his way, then he boasteth.
original_text:
It is naught,
it is naught, saith the buyer: but when he is gone his way, then he boasteth.

translated_text:
There is gold, and a multitude of rubies: but the lips of knowledge
are a precious jewel.
original_text:
There is gold, and a multitude of rubies: but the lips of knowledge
are a precious jewel.

translated_text:
Take his garment that is surety
for a stranger: and take a pledge of him for a strange woman.
original_text:
Take his garment that is surety
for a stranger: and take a pledge of him for a strange woman.

translated_text:
Bread of deceit
is sweet to a man; but afterwards his mouth shall be filled with gravel.
original_text:
Bread of deceit
is sweet to a man; but afterwards his mouth shall be filled with gravel.

translated_text: Every purpose is established by counsel: and with good advice make war.
original_text: Every purpose is established by counsel: and with good advice make war.

translated_text:
He that goeth about
as a talebearer revealeth secrets: therefore meddle not with him that flattereth with his lips.
original_text:
He that goeth about
as a talebearer revealeth secrets: therefore meddle not with him that flattereth with his lips.

translated_text: Whoso curseth his father or his mother, his lamp shall be put out in obscure darkness.
original_text: Whoso curseth his father or his mother, his lamp shall be put out in obscure darkness.

translated_text:
An inheritance
may be gotten hastily at the beginning; but the end thereof shall not be blessed.
original_text:
An inheritance
may be gotten hastily at the beginning; but the end thereof shall not be blessed.

translated_text:
Say not thou, I will recompense evil;
but wait on the LORD, and he shall save thee.
original_text:
Say not thou, I will recompense evil;
but wait on the LORD, and he shall save thee.

translated_text:
Divers weights
are an abomination unto the LORD; and a false balance
is not good.
original_text:
Divers weights
are an abomination unto the LORD; and a false balance
is not good.

translated_text:
Man’s goings
are of the LORD; how can a man then understand his own way?
original_text:
Man’s goings
are of the LORD; how can a man then understand his own way?

translated_text:
It is a snare to the man
who devoureth
that which is holy, and after vows to make enquiry.
original_text:
It is a snare to the man
who devoureth
that which is holy, and after vows to make enquiry.

translated_text: A wise king scattereth the wicked, and bringeth the wheel over them.
original_text: A wise king scattereth the wicked, and bringeth the wheel over them.

translated_text:
The spirit of man
is the candle of the LORD, searching all the inward parts of the belly.
original_text:
The spirit of man
is the candle of the LORD, searching all the inward parts of the belly.

translated_text: Mercy and truth preserve the king: and his throne is upholden by mercy.
original_text: Mercy and truth preserve the king: and his throne is upholden by mercy.

translated_text:
The glory of young men
is their strength: and the beauty of old men
is the grey head.
original_text:
The glory of young men
is their strength: and the beauty of old men
is the grey head.

translated_text:
The blueness of a wound cleanseth away evil: so
do stripes the inward parts of the belly.
original_text:
The blueness of a wound cleanseth away evil: so
do stripes the inward parts of the belly.

translated_text:
When thou sittest to eat with a ruler, consider diligently what
is before thee:
original_text:
When thou sittest to eat with a ruler, consider diligently what
is before thee:

translated_text:
And put a knife to thy throat, if thou
be a man given to appetite.
original_text:
And put a knife to thy throat, if thou
be a man given to appetite.

translated_text:
Be not desirous of his dainties: for they
are deceitful meat.
original_text:
Be not desirous of his dainties: for they
are deceitful meat.

translated_text: Labour not to be rich: cease from thine own wisdom.
original_text: Labour not to be rich: cease from thine own wisdom.

translated_text:
Wilt thou set thine eyes upon that which is not? for
riches
 certainly make themselves wings; they fly away as an eagle toward heaven.
original_text:
Wilt thou set thine eyes upon that which is not? for
riches
 certainly make themselves wings; they fly away as an eagle toward heaven.

translated_text:
Eat thou not the bread of
him that hath an evil eye, neither desire thou his dainty meats:
original_text:
Eat thou not the bread of
him that hath an evil eye, neither desire thou his dainty meats:

translated_text:
For as he thinketh in his heart, so
is he: Eat and drink, saith he to thee; but his heart
is not with thee.
original_text:
For as he thinketh in his heart, so
is he: Eat and drink, saith he to thee; but his heart
is not with thee.

translated_text:
The morsel
which thou hast eaten shalt thou vomit up, and lose thy sweet words.
original_text:
The morsel
which thou hast eaten shalt thou vomit up, and lose thy sweet words.

translated_text: Speak not in the ears of a fool: for he will despise the wisdom of thy words.
original_text: Speak not in the ears of a fool: for he will despise the wisdom of thy words.

translated_text: Remove not the old landmark; and enter not into the fields of the fatherless:
original_text: Remove not the old landmark; and enter not into the fields of the fatherless:

translated_text:
For their redeemer
is mighty; he shall plead their cause with thee.
original_text:
For their redeemer
is mighty; he shall plead their cause with thee.

translated_text: Apply thine heart unto instruction, and thine ears to the words of knowledge.
original_text: Apply thine heart unto instruction, and thine ears to the words of knowledge.

translated_text:
Withhold not correction from the child: for
if thou beatest him with the rod, he shall not die.
original_text:
Withhold not correction from the child: for
if thou beatest him with the rod, he shall not die.

translated_text: Thou shalt beat him with the rod, and shalt deliver his soul from hell.
original_text: Thou shalt beat him with the rod, and shalt deliver his soul from hell.

translated_text: My son, if thine heart be wise, my heart shall rejoice, even mine.
original_text: My son, if thine heart be wise, my heart shall rejoice, even mine.

translated_text: Yea, my reins shall rejoice, when thy lips speak right things.
original_text: Yea, my reins shall rejoice, when thy lips speak right things.

translated_text:
Let not thine heart envy sinners: but
be thou in the fear of the LORD all the day long.
original_text:
Let not thine heart envy sinners: but
be thou in the fear of the LORD all the day long.

translated_text: For surely there is an end; and thine expectation shall not be cut off.
original_text: For surely there is an end; and thine expectation shall not be cut off.

translated_text: Hear thou, my son, and be wise, and guide thine heart in the way.
original_text: Hear thou, my son, and be wise, and guide thine heart in the way.

translated_text: Be not among winebibbers; among riotous eaters of flesh:
original_text: Be not among winebibbers; among riotous eaters of flesh:

translated_text:
For the drunkard and the glutton shall come to poverty: and drowsiness shall clothe
a man with rags.
original_text:
For the drunkard and the glutton shall come to poverty: and drowsiness shall clothe
a man with rags.

translated_text: Hearken unto thy father that begat thee, and despise not thy mother when she is old.
original_text: Hearken unto thy father that begat thee, and despise not thy mother when she is old.

translated_text:
The father of the righteous shall greatly rejoice: and he that begetteth a wise
child shall have joy of him.
original_text:
The father of the righteous shall greatly rejoice: and he that begetteth a wise
child shall have joy of him.

translated_text: Thy father and thy mother shall be glad, and she that bare thee shall rejoice.
original_text: Thy father and thy mother shall be glad, and she that bare thee shall rejoice.

translated_text: My son, give me thine heart, and let thine eyes observe my ways.
original_text: My son, give me thine heart, and let thine eyes observe my ways.

translated_text:
For a whore
is a deep ditch; and a strange woman
is
 a narrow pit.
original_text:
For a whore
is a deep ditch; and a strange woman
is
 a narrow pit.

translated_text:
She also lieth in wait as
for a prey, and increaseth the transgressors among men.
original_text:
She also lieth in wait as
for a prey, and increaseth the transgressors among men.

translated_text: Who hath woe? who hath sorrow? who hath contentions? who hath babbling? who hath wounds without cause? who hath redness of eyes?
original_text: Who hath woe? who hath sorrow? who hath contentions? who hath babbling? who hath wounds without cause? who hath redness of eyes?

translated_text: They that tarry long at the wine; they that go to seek mixed wine.
original_text: They that tarry long at the wine; they that go to seek mixed wine.

translated_text:
Look not thou upon the wine when it is red, when it giveth his colour in the cup,
when it moveth itself aright.
original_text:
Look not thou upon the wine when it is red, when it giveth his colour in the cup,
when it moveth itself aright.

translated_text: At the last it biteth like a serpent, and stingeth like an adder.
original_text: At the last it biteth like a serpent, and stingeth like an adder.

translated_text: Thine eyes shall behold strange women, and thine heart shall utter perverse things.
original_text: Thine eyes shall behold strange women, and thine heart shall utter perverse things.

translated_text: Yea, thou shalt be as he that lieth down in the midst of the sea, or as he that lieth upon the top of a mast.
original_text: Yea, thou shalt be as he that lieth down in the midst of the sea, or as he that lieth upon the top of a mast.

translated_text:
They have stricken me,
shalt thou say, and I was not sick; they have beaten me,
and I felt
it not: when shall I awake? I will seek it yet again.
original_text:
They have stricken me,
shalt thou say, and I was not sick; they have beaten me,
and I felt
it not: when shall I awake? I will seek it yet again.

translated_text:
A
good name
is rather to be chosen than great riches,
and loving favour rather than silver and gold.
original_text:
A
good name
is rather to be chosen than great riches,
and loving favour rather than silver and gold.

translated_text:
The rich and poor meet together: the LORD
is the maker of them all.
original_text:
The rich and poor meet together: the LORD
is the maker of them all.

translated_text:
A prudent
man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself: but the simple pass on, and are punished.
original_text:
A prudent
man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself: but the simple pass on, and are punished.

translated_text:
By humility
and the fear of the LORD
are riches, and honour, and life.
original_text:
By humility
and the fear of the LORD
are riches, and honour, and life.

translated_text:
Thorns
and snares
are in the way of the froward: he that doth keep his soul shall be far from them.
original_text:
Thorns
and snares
are in the way of the froward: he that doth keep his soul shall be far from them.

translated_text: Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.
original_text: Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.

translated_text:
The rich ruleth over the poor, and the borrower
is servant to the lender.
original_text:
The rich ruleth over the poor, and the borrower
is servant to the lender.

translated_text: He that soweth iniquity shall reap vanity: and the rod of his anger shall fail.
original_text: He that soweth iniquity shall reap vanity: and the rod of his anger shall fail.

translated_text: He that hath a bountiful eye shall be blessed; for he giveth of his bread to the poor.
original_text: He that hath a bountiful eye shall be blessed; for he giveth of his bread to the poor.

translated_text: Cast out the scorner, and contention shall go out; yea, strife and reproach shall cease.
original_text: Cast out the scorner, and contention shall go out; yea, strife and reproach shall cease.

translated_text:
He that loveth pureness of heart,
for the grace of his lips the king
shall be his friend.
original_text:
He that loveth pureness of heart,
for the grace of his lips the king
shall be his friend.

translated_text: The eyes of the LORD preserve knowledge, and he overthroweth the words of the transgressor.
original_text: The eyes of the LORD preserve knowledge, and he overthroweth the words of the transgressor.

translated_text:
The slothful
man saith,
There is a lion without, I shall be slain in the streets.
original_text:
The slothful
man saith,
There is a lion without, I shall be slain in the streets.

translated_text:
The mouth of strange women
is a deep pit: he that is abhorred of the LORD shall fall therein.
original_text:
The mouth of strange women
is a deep pit: he that is abhorred of the LORD shall fall therein.

translated_text:
Foolishness
is bound in the heart of a child;
but
 the rod of correction shall drive it far from him.
original_text:
Foolishness
is bound in the heart of a child;
but
 the rod of correction shall drive it far from him.

translated_text:
He that oppresseth the poor to increase his
riches, and he that giveth to the rich,
shall surely
come to want.
original_text:
He that oppresseth the poor to increase his
riches, and he that giveth to the rich,
shall surely
come to want.

translated_text: Bow down thine ear, and hear the words of the wise, and apply thine heart unto my knowledge.
original_text: Bow down thine ear, and hear the words of the wise, and apply thine heart unto my knowledge.

translated_text:
For
it is a pleasant thing if thou keep them within thee; they shall withal be fitted in thy lips.
original_text:
For
it is a pleasant thing if thou keep them within thee; they shall withal be fitted in thy lips.

translated_text: That thy trust may be in the LORD, I have made known to thee this day, even to thee.
original_text: That thy trust may be in the LORD, I have made known to thee this day, even to thee.

translated_text: Have not I written to thee excellent things in counsels and knowledge,
original_text: Have not I written to thee excellent things in counsels and knowledge,

translated_text: That I might make thee know the certainty of the words of truth; that thou mightest answer the words of truth to them that send unto thee?
original_text: That I might make thee know the certainty of the words of truth; that thou mightest answer the words of truth to them that send unto thee?

translated_text:
Rob not the poor, because he
is poor: neither oppress the afflicted in the gate:
original_text:
Rob not the poor, because he
is poor: neither oppress the afflicted in the gate:

translated_text: For the LORD will plead their cause, and spoil the soul of those that spoiled them.
original_text: For the LORD will plead their cause, and spoil the soul of those that spoiled them.

translated_text: Make no friendship with an angry man; and with a furious man thou shalt not go:
original_text: Make no friendship with an angry man; and with a furious man thou shalt not go:

translated_text: Lest thou learn his ways, and get a snare to thy soul.
original_text: Lest thou learn his ways, and get a snare to thy soul.

translated_text:
Be not thou
one of them that strike hands,
or of them that are sureties for debts.
original_text:
Be not thou
one of them that strike hands,
or of them that are sureties for debts.

translated_text: If thou hast nothing to pay, why should he take away thy bed from under thee?
original_text: If thou hast nothing to pay, why should he take away thy bed from under thee?

translated_text: Remove not the ancient landmark, which thy fathers have set.
original_text: Remove not the ancient landmark, which thy fathers have set.

translated_text:
Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean
men.
original_text:
Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean
men.

translated_text:
These
are also proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.
original_text:
These
are also proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.

translated_text:
It is the glory of God to conceal a thing: but the honour of kings
is to search out a matter.
original_text:
It is the glory of God to conceal a thing: but the honour of kings
is to search out a matter.

translated_text:
The heaven for height, and the earth for depth, and the heart of kings
is unsearchable.
original_text:
The heaven for height, and the earth for depth, and the heart of kings
is unsearchable.

translated_text: Take away the dross from the silver, and there shall come forth a vessel for the finer.
original_text: Take away the dross from the silver, and there shall come forth a vessel for the finer.

translated_text:
Take away the wicked
from before the king, and his throne shall be established in righteousness.
original_text:
Take away the wicked
from before the king, and his throne shall be established in righteousness.

translated_text:
Put not forth thyself in the presence of the king, and stand not in the place of great
men:
original_text:
Put not forth thyself in the presence of the king, and stand not in the place of great
men:

translated_text:
For better
it is that it be said unto thee, Come up hither; than that thou shouldest be put lower in the presence of the prince whom thine eyes have seen.
original_text:
For better
it is that it be said unto thee, Come up hither; than that thou shouldest be put lower in the presence of the prince whom thine eyes have seen.

translated_text:
Go not forth hastily to strive, lest
thou know not what to do in the end thereof, when thy neighbour hath put thee to shame.
original_text:
Go not forth hastily to strive, lest
thou know not what to do in the end thereof, when thy neighbour hath put thee to shame.

translated_text:
Debate thy cause with thy neighbour
himself; and discover not a secret to another:
original_text:
Debate thy cause with thy neighbour
himself; and discover not a secret to another:

translated_text:
Lest he that heareth
it put thee to shame, and thine infamy turn not away.
original_text:
Lest he that heareth
it put thee to shame, and thine infamy turn not away.

translated_text:
A word fitly spoken
is like apples of gold in pictures of silver.
original_text:
A word fitly spoken
is like apples of gold in pictures of silver.

translated_text:
As an earring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold,
so is a wise reprover upon an obedient ear.
original_text:
As an earring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold,
so is a wise reprover upon an obedient ear.

translated_text:
As the cold of snow in the time of harvest,
so is a faithful messenger to them that send him: for he refresheth the soul of his masters.
original_text:
As the cold of snow in the time of harvest,
so is a faithful messenger to them that send him: for he refresheth the soul of his masters.

translated_text:
Whoso boasteth himself of a false gift
is like clouds and wind without rain.
original_text:
Whoso boasteth himself of a false gift
is like clouds and wind without rain.

translated_text: By long forbearing is a prince persuaded, and a soft tongue breaketh the bone.
original_text: By long forbearing is a prince persuaded, and a soft tongue breaketh the bone.

translated_text: Hast thou found honey? eat so much as is sufficient for thee, lest thou be filled therewith, and vomit it.
original_text: Hast thou found honey? eat so much as is sufficient for thee, lest thou be filled therewith, and vomit it.

translated_text:
Withdraw thy foot from thy neighbour’s house; lest he be weary of thee, and
so hate thee.
original_text:
Withdraw thy foot from thy neighbour’s house; lest he be weary of thee, and
so hate thee.

translated_text:
A man that beareth false witness against his neighbour
is
 a maul, and a sword, and a sharp arrow.
original_text:
A man that beareth false witness against his neighbour
is
 a maul, and a sword, and a sharp arrow.

translated_text:
Confidence in an unfaithful man in time of trouble
is like
 a broken tooth, and a foot out of joint.
original_text:
Confidence in an unfaithful man in time of trouble
is like
 a broken tooth, and a foot out of joint.

translated_text:
As he that taketh away a garment in cold weather,
and as
 vinegar upon nitre, so
is he that singeth songs to an heavy heart.
original_text:
As he that taketh away a garment in cold weather,
and as
 vinegar upon nitre, so
is he that singeth songs to an heavy heart.

translated_text: If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink:
original_text: If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink:

translated_text: For thou shalt heap coals of fire upon his head, and the LORD shall reward thee.
original_text: For thou shalt heap coals of fire upon his head, and the LORD shall reward thee.

translated_text:
The north wind driveth away rain: so
doth an angry countenance a backbiting tongue.
original_text:
The north wind driveth away rain: so
doth an angry countenance a backbiting tongue.

translated_text: It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman and in a wide house.
original_text: It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman and in a wide house.

translated_text:
As cold waters to a thirsty soul, so
is good news from a far country.
original_text:
As cold waters to a thirsty soul, so
is good news from a far country.

translated_text:
A righteous man falling down before the wicked
is as a troubled fountain, and a corrupt spring.
original_text:
A righteous man falling down before the wicked
is as a troubled fountain, and a corrupt spring.

translated_text:
It is
not good to eat much honey: so
for men
to search their own glory
is not
glory.
original_text:
It is
not good to eat much honey: so
for men
to search their own glory
is not
glory.

translated_text:
He that
hath no rule over his own spirit
is like
 a city
that is broken down,
and without walls.
original_text:
He that
hath no rule over his own spirit
is like
 a city
that is broken down,
and without walls.

translated_text: Be not thou envious against evil men, neither desire to be with them.
original_text: Be not thou envious against evil men, neither desire to be with them.

translated_text: For their heart studieth destruction, and their lips talk of mischief.
original_text: For their heart studieth destruction, and their lips talk of mischief.

translated_text: Through wisdom is an house builded; and by understanding it is established:
original_text: Through wisdom is an house builded; and by understanding it is established:

translated_text: And by knowledge shall the chambers be filled with all precious and pleasant riches.
original_text: And by knowledge shall the chambers be filled with all precious and pleasant riches.

translated_text:
A wise man
is strong; yea, a man of knowledge increaseth strength.
original_text:
A wise man
is strong; yea, a man of knowledge increaseth strength.

translated_text:
For by wise counsel thou shalt make thy war: and in multitude of counsellors
there is safety.
original_text:
For by wise counsel thou shalt make thy war: and in multitude of counsellors
there is safety.

translated_text:
Wisdom
is too high for a fool: he openeth not his mouth in the gate.
original_text:
Wisdom
is too high for a fool: he openeth not his mouth in the gate.

translated_text: He that deviseth to do evil shall be called a mischievous person.
original_text: He that deviseth to do evil shall be called a mischievous person.

translated_text:
The thought of foolishness
is sin: and the scorner
is
 an abomination to men.
original_text:
The thought of foolishness
is sin: and the scorner
is
 an abomination to men.

translated_text:
If thou faint in the day of adversity, thy strength
is small.
original_text:
If thou faint in the day of adversity, thy strength
is small.

translated_text:
If thou sayest, Behold, we knew it not; doth not he that pondereth the heart consider
it? and he that keepeth thy soul, doth
not
 he know
it? and shall
not he render to
every
 man according to his works?
original_text:
If thou sayest, Behold, we knew it not; doth not he that pondereth the heart consider
it? and he that keepeth thy soul, doth
not
 he know
it? and shall
not he render to
every
 man according to his works?

translated_text:
My son, eat thou honey, because
it is good; and the honeycomb,
which is sweet to thy taste:
original_text:
My son, eat thou honey, because
it is good; and the honeycomb,
which is sweet to thy taste:

translated_text:
So
shall the knowledge of wisdom
be unto thy soul: when thou hast found
it, then there shall be a reward, and thy expectation shall not be cut off.
original_text:
So
shall the knowledge of wisdom
be unto thy soul: when thou hast found
it, then there shall be a reward, and thy expectation shall not be cut off.

translated_text:
Lay not wait, O wicked
man, against the dwelling of the righteous; spoil not his resting place:
original_text:
Lay not wait, O wicked
man, against the dwelling of the righteous; spoil not his resting place:

translated_text:
For a just
man falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief.
original_text:
For a just
man falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief.

translated_text: Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth, and let not thine heart be glad when he stumbleth:
original_text: Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth, and let not thine heart be glad when he stumbleth:

translated_text:
Lest the LORD see
it, and it displease him, and he turn away his wrath from him.
original_text:
Lest the LORD see
it, and it displease him, and he turn away his wrath from him.

translated_text:
Fret not thyself because of evil
men, neither be thou envious at the wicked;
original_text:
Fret not thyself because of evil
men, neither be thou envious at the wicked;

translated_text:
For there shall be no reward to the evil
man; the candle of the wicked shall be put out.
original_text:
For there shall be no reward to the evil
man; the candle of the wicked shall be put out.

translated_text:
My son, fear thou the LORD and the king:
and meddle not with them that are given to change:
original_text:
My son, fear thou the LORD and the king:
and meddle not with them that are given to change:

translated_text: For their calamity shall rise suddenly; and who knoweth the ruin of them both?
original_text: For their calamity shall rise suddenly; and who knoweth the ruin of them both?

translated_text:
These
things also
belong to the wise.
It is
 not good to have respect of persons in judgment.
original_text:
These
things also
belong to the wise.
It is
 not good to have respect of persons in judgment.

translated_text:
He that saith unto the wicked, Thou
art righteous; him shall the people curse, nations shall abhor him:
original_text:
He that saith unto the wicked, Thou
art righteous; him shall the people curse, nations shall abhor him:

translated_text:
But to them that rebuke
him shall be delight, and a good blessing shall come upon them.
original_text:
But to them that rebuke
him shall be delight, and a good blessing shall come upon them.

translated_text:
Every man shall kiss
his lips that giveth a right answer.
original_text:
Every man shall kiss
his lips that giveth a right answer.

translated_text: Prepare thy work without, and make it fit for thyself in the field; and afterwards build thine house.
original_text: Prepare thy work without, and make it fit for thyself in the field; and afterwards build thine house.

translated_text:
Be not a witness against thy neighbour without cause; and deceive
not with thy lips.
original_text:
Be not a witness against thy neighbour without cause; and deceive
not with thy lips.

translated_text: Say not, I will do so to him as he hath done to me: I will render to the man according to his work.
original_text: Say not, I will do so to him as he hath done to me: I will render to the man according to his work.

translated_text: I went by the field of the slothful, and by the vineyard of the man void of understanding;
original_text: I went by the field of the slothful, and by the vineyard of the man void of understanding;

translated_text:
And, lo, it was all grown over with thorns,
and nettles had covered the face thereof, and the stone wall thereof was broken down.
original_text:
And, lo, it was all grown over with thorns,
and nettles had covered the face thereof, and the stone wall thereof was broken down.

translated_text:
Then I saw,
and considered
it well: I looked upon
it, and received instruction.
original_text:
Then I saw,
and considered
it well: I looked upon
it, and received instruction.

translated_text: Yet a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep:
original_text: Yet a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep:

translated_text: So shall thy poverty come as one that travelleth; and thy want as an armed man.
original_text: So shall thy poverty come as one that travelleth; and thy want as an armed man.

translated_text: Boast not thyself of to morrow; for thou knowest not what a day may bring forth.
original_text: Boast not thyself of to morrow; for thou knowest not what a day may bring forth.

translated_text: Let another man praise thee, and not thine own mouth; a stranger, and not thine own lips.
original_text: Let another man praise thee, and not thine own mouth; a stranger, and not thine own lips.

translated_text:
A stone
is heavy, and the sand weighty; but a fool’s wrath
is heavier than them both.
original_text:
A stone
is heavy, and the sand weighty; but a fool’s wrath
is heavier than them both.

translated_text:
Wrath
is cruel, and anger
is outrageous; but who
is able to stand before envy?
original_text:
Wrath
is cruel, and anger
is outrageous; but who
is able to stand before envy?

translated_text:
Open rebuke
is better than secret love.
original_text:
Open rebuke
is better than secret love.

translated_text:
Faithful
are the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy
are deceitful.
original_text:
Faithful
are the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy
are deceitful.

translated_text: The full soul loatheth an honeycomb; but to the hungry soul every bitter thing is sweet.
original_text: The full soul loatheth an honeycomb; but to the hungry soul every bitter thing is sweet.

translated_text:
As a bird that wandereth from her nest, so
is a man that wandereth from his place.
original_text:
As a bird that wandereth from her nest, so
is a man that wandereth from his place.

translated_text:
Ointment and perfume rejoice the heart: so
doth the sweetness of a man’s friend by hearty counsel.
original_text:
Ointment and perfume rejoice the heart: so
doth the sweetness of a man’s friend by hearty counsel.

translated_text:
Thine own friend, and thy father’s friend, forsake not; neither go into thy brother’s house in the day of thy calamity:
for better
is a neighbour
that is near than a brother far off.
original_text:
Thine own friend, and thy father’s friend, forsake not; neither go into thy brother’s house in the day of thy calamity:
for better
is a neighbour
that is near than a brother far off.

translated_text: My son, be wise, and make my heart glad, that I may answer him that reproacheth me.
original_text: My son, be wise, and make my heart glad, that I may answer him that reproacheth me.

translated_text:
A prudent
man foreseeth the evil,
and hideth himself;
but the simple pass on,
and are punished.
original_text:
A prudent
man foreseeth the evil,
and hideth himself;
but the simple pass on,
and are punished.

translated_text: Take his garment that is surety for a stranger, and take a pledge of him for a strange woman.
original_text: Take his garment that is surety for a stranger, and take a pledge of him for a strange woman.

translated_text: He that blesseth his friend with a loud voice, rising early in the morning, it shall be counted a curse to him.
original_text: He that blesseth his friend with a loud voice, rising early in the morning, it shall be counted a curse to him.

translated_text: A continual dropping in a very rainy day and a contentious woman are alike.
original_text: A continual dropping in a very rainy day and a contentious woman are alike.

translated_text:
Whosoever hideth her hideth the wind, and the ointment of his right hand,
which bewrayeth
itself.
original_text:
Whosoever hideth her hideth the wind, and the ointment of his right hand,
which bewrayeth
itself.

translated_text: Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.
original_text: Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.

translated_text: Whoso keepeth the fig tree shall eat the fruit thereof: so he that waiteth on his master shall be honoured.
original_text: Whoso keepeth the fig tree shall eat the fruit thereof: so he that waiteth on his master shall be honoured.

translated_text:
As in water face
answereth to face, so the heart of man to man.
original_text:
As in water face
answereth to face, so the heart of man to man.

translated_text: Hell and destruction are never full; so the eyes of man are never satisfied.
original_text: Hell and destruction are never full; so the eyes of man are never satisfied.

translated_text:
As the fining pot for silver, and the furnace for gold; so
is a man to his praise.
original_text:
As the fining pot for silver, and the furnace for gold; so
is a man to his praise.

translated_text:
Though thou shouldest bray a fool in a mortar among wheat with a pestle,
yet will not his foolishness depart from him.
original_text:
Though thou shouldest bray a fool in a mortar among wheat with a pestle,
yet will not his foolishness depart from him.

translated_text:
Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks,
and look well to thy herds.
original_text:
Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks,
and look well to thy herds.

translated_text:
For riches
are not for ever: and doth the crown
endure
 to every generation?
original_text:
For riches
are not for ever: and doth the crown
endure
 to every generation?

translated_text: The hay appeareth, and the tender grass sheweth itself, and herbs of the mountains are gathered.
original_text: The hay appeareth, and the tender grass sheweth itself, and herbs of the mountains are gathered.

translated_text:
The lambs
are for thy clothing, and the goats
are
 the price of the field.
original_text:
The lambs
are for thy clothing, and the goats
are
 the price of the field.

translated_text:
And
thou shalt have goats’ milk enough for thy food, for the food of thy household, and
for the maintenance for thy maidens.
original_text:
And
thou shalt have goats’ milk enough for thy food, for the food of thy household, and
for the maintenance for thy maidens.

translated_text: As snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, so honour is not seemly for a fool.
original_text: As snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, so honour is not seemly for a fool.

translated_text: As the bird by wandering, as the swallow by flying, so the curse causeless shall not come.
original_text: As the bird by wandering, as the swallow by flying, so the curse causeless shall not come.

translated_text: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the ass, and a rod for the fool’s back.
original_text: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the ass, and a rod for the fool’s back.

translated_text: Answer not a fool according to his folly, lest thou also be like unto him.
original_text: Answer not a fool according to his folly, lest thou also be like unto him.

translated_text: Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he be wise in his own conceit.
original_text: Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he be wise in his own conceit.

translated_text:
He that sendeth a message by the hand of a fool cutteth off the feet,
and drinketh damage.
original_text:
He that sendeth a message by the hand of a fool cutteth off the feet,
and drinketh damage.

translated_text:
The legs of the lame are not equal: so
is a parable in the mouth of fools.
original_text:
The legs of the lame are not equal: so
is a parable in the mouth of fools.

translated_text:
As he that bindeth a stone in a sling, so
is he that giveth honour to a fool.
original_text:
As he that bindeth a stone in a sling, so
is he that giveth honour to a fool.

translated_text:
As a thorn goeth up into the hand of a drunkard, so
is
 a parable in the mouth of fools.
original_text:
As a thorn goeth up into the hand of a drunkard, so
is
 a parable in the mouth of fools.

translated_text:
The great
God that formed all
things both rewardeth the fool, and rewardeth transgressors.
original_text:
The great
God that formed all
things both rewardeth the fool, and rewardeth transgressors.

translated_text:
As a dog returneth to his vomit,
so a fool returneth to his folly.
original_text:
As a dog returneth to his vomit,
so a fool returneth to his folly.

translated_text:
Seest thou a man wise in his own conceit?
there is more hope of a fool than of him.
original_text:
Seest thou a man wise in his own conceit?
there is more hope of a fool than of him.

translated_text:
The slothful
man saith,
There is a lion in the way; a lion
is in the streets.
original_text:
The slothful
man saith,
There is a lion in the way; a lion
is in the streets.

translated_text:
As the door turneth upon his hinges, so
doth the slothful upon his bed.
original_text:
As the door turneth upon his hinges, so
doth the slothful upon his bed.

translated_text:
The slothful hideth his hand in
his bosom; it grieveth him to bring it again to his mouth.
original_text:
The slothful hideth his hand in
his bosom; it grieveth him to bring it again to his mouth.

translated_text:
The sluggard
is wiser in his own conceit than seven men that can render a reason.
original_text:
The sluggard
is wiser in his own conceit than seven men that can render a reason.

translated_text:
He that passeth by,
and meddleth with strife
belonging
 not to him,
is like one that taketh a dog by the ears.
original_text:
He that passeth by,
and meddleth with strife
belonging
 not to him,
is like one that taketh a dog by the ears.

translated_text:
As a mad
man who casteth firebrands, arrows, and death,
original_text:
As a mad
man who casteth firebrands, arrows, and death,

translated_text:
So
is the man
that deceiveth his neighbour, and saith, Am not I in sport?
original_text:
So
is the man
that deceiveth his neighbour, and saith, Am not I in sport?

translated_text:
Where no wood is,
there the fire goeth out: so where
there is no talebearer, the strife ceaseth.
original_text:
Where no wood is,
there the fire goeth out: so where
there is no talebearer, the strife ceaseth.

translated_text:
As coals
are to burning coals, and wood to fire; so
is a contentious man to kindle strife.
original_text:
As coals
are to burning coals, and wood to fire; so
is a contentious man to kindle strife.

translated_text:
The words of a talebearer
are as wounds, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly.
original_text:
The words of a talebearer
are as wounds, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly.

translated_text:
Burning lips and a wicked heart
are like a potsherd covered with silver dross.
original_text:
Burning lips and a wicked heart
are like a potsherd covered with silver dross.

translated_text: He that hateth dissembleth with his lips, and layeth up deceit within him;
original_text: He that hateth dissembleth with his lips, and layeth up deceit within him;

translated_text:
When he speaketh fair, believe him not: for
there are seven abominations in his heart.
original_text:
When he speaketh fair, believe him not: for
there are seven abominations in his heart.

translated_text:
Whose hatred is covered by deceit, his wickedness shall be shewed before the
whole congregation.
original_text:
Whose hatred is covered by deceit, his wickedness shall be shewed before the
whole congregation.

translated_text: Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein: and he that rolleth a stone, it will return upon him.
original_text: Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein: and he that rolleth a stone, it will return upon him.

translated_text:
A lying tongue hateth
those that are afflicted by it; and a flattering mouth worketh ruin.
original_text:
A lying tongue hateth
those that are afflicted by it; and a flattering mouth worketh ruin.

translated_text:
He, that being often reproved hardeneth
his neck, shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy.
original_text:
He, that being often reproved hardeneth
his neck, shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy.

translated_text: When the righteous are in authority, the people rejoice: but when the wicked beareth rule, the people mourn.
original_text: When the righteous are in authority, the people rejoice: but when the wicked beareth rule, the people mourn.

translated_text:
Whoso loveth wisdom rejoiceth his father: but he that keepeth company with harlots spendeth
his substance.
original_text:
Whoso loveth wisdom rejoiceth his father: but he that keepeth company with harlots spendeth
his substance.

translated_text: The king by judgment establisheth the land: but he that receiveth gifts overthroweth it.
original_text: The king by judgment establisheth the land: but he that receiveth gifts overthroweth it.

translated_text: A man that flattereth his neighbour spreadeth a net for his feet.
original_text: A man that flattereth his neighbour spreadeth a net for his feet.

translated_text:
In the transgression of an evil man
there is a snare: but the righteous doth sing and rejoice.
original_text:
In the transgression of an evil man
there is a snare: but the righteous doth sing and rejoice.

translated_text:
The righteous considereth the cause of the poor:
but the wicked regardeth not to know
it.
original_text:
The righteous considereth the cause of the poor:
but the wicked regardeth not to know
it.

translated_text:
Scornful men bring a city into a snare: but wise
men turn away wrath.
original_text:
Scornful men bring a city into a snare: but wise
men turn away wrath.

translated_text:
If a wise man contendeth with a foolish man, whether he rage or laugh,
there is no rest.
original_text:
If a wise man contendeth with a foolish man, whether he rage or laugh,
there is no rest.

translated_text: The bloodthirsty hate the upright: but the just seek his soul.
original_text: The bloodthirsty hate the upright: but the just seek his soul.

translated_text:
A fool uttereth all his mind: but a wise
man keepeth it in till afterwards.
original_text:
A fool uttereth all his mind: but a wise
man keepeth it in till afterwards.

translated_text:
If a ruler hearken to lies, all his servants
are wicked.
original_text:
If a ruler hearken to lies, all his servants
are wicked.

translated_text: The poor and the deceitful man meet together: the LORD lighteneth both their eyes.
original_text: The poor and the deceitful man meet together: the LORD lighteneth both their eyes.

translated_text: The king that faithfully judgeth the poor, his throne shall be established for ever.
original_text: The king that faithfully judgeth the poor, his throne shall be established for ever.

translated_text:
The rod and reproof give wisdom: but a child left
to himself
 bringeth his mother to shame.
original_text:
The rod and reproof give wisdom: but a child left
to himself
 bringeth his mother to shame.

translated_text: When the wicked are multiplied, transgression increaseth: but the righteous shall see their fall.
original_text: When the wicked are multiplied, transgression increaseth: but the righteous shall see their fall.

translated_text: Correct thy son, and he shall give thee rest; yea, he shall give delight unto thy soul.
original_text: Correct thy son, and he shall give thee rest; yea, he shall give delight unto thy soul.

translated_text:
Where
there is no vision, the people perish: but he that keepeth the law, happy
is he.
original_text:
Where
there is no vision, the people perish: but he that keepeth the law, happy
is he.

translated_text: A servant will not be corrected by words: for though he understand he will not answer.
original_text: A servant will not be corrected by words: for though he understand he will not answer.

translated_text:
Seest thou a man
that is hasty in his words?
there is
 more hope of a fool than of him.
original_text:
Seest thou a man
that is hasty in his words?
there is
 more hope of a fool than of him.

translated_text:
He that delicately bringeth up his servant from a child shall have him become
his son at the length.
original_text:
He that delicately bringeth up his servant from a child shall have him become
his son at the length.

translated_text: An angry man stirreth up strife, and a furious man aboundeth in transgression.
original_text: An angry man stirreth up strife, and a furious man aboundeth in transgression.

translated_text: A man’s pride shall bring him low: but honour shall uphold the humble in spirit.
original_text: A man’s pride shall bring him low: but honour shall uphold the humble in spirit.

translated_text:
Whoso is partner with a thief hateth his own soul: he heareth cursing, and bewrayeth
it not.
original_text:
Whoso is partner with a thief hateth his own soul: he heareth cursing, and bewrayeth
it not.

translated_text: The fear of man bringeth a snare: but whoso putteth his trust in the LORD shall be safe.
original_text: The fear of man bringeth a snare: but whoso putteth his trust in the LORD shall be safe.

translated_text:
Many seek the ruler’s favour; but
every man’s judgment
cometh from the LORD.
original_text:
Many seek the ruler’s favour; but
every man’s judgment
cometh from the LORD.

translated_text:
An unjust man
is an abomination to the just: and
he that is upright in the way
is abomination to the wicked.
original_text:
An unjust man
is an abomination to the just: and
he that is upright in the way
is abomination to the wicked.

translated_text: The wicked flee when no man pursueth: but the righteous are bold as a lion.
original_text: The wicked flee when no man pursueth: but the righteous are bold as a lion.

translated_text:
For the transgression of a land many
are the princes thereof: but by a man of understanding
and knowledge the state
thereof
 shall be prolonged.
original_text:
For the transgression of a land many
are the princes thereof: but by a man of understanding
and knowledge the state
thereof
 shall be prolonged.

translated_text:
A poor man that oppresseth the poor
is like a sweeping rain which leaveth no food.
original_text:
A poor man that oppresseth the poor
is like a sweeping rain which leaveth no food.

translated_text: They that forsake the law praise the wicked: but such as keep the law contend with them.
original_text: They that forsake the law praise the wicked: but such as keep the law contend with them.

translated_text:
Evil men understand not judgment: but they that seek the LORD understand all
things.
original_text:
Evil men understand not judgment: but they that seek the LORD understand all
things.

translated_text:
Better
is the poor that walketh in his uprightness, than
he that is perverse
in his ways, though he
be
 rich.
original_text:
Better
is the poor that walketh in his uprightness, than
he that is perverse
in his ways, though he
be
 rich.

translated_text:
Whoso keepeth the law
is a wise son: but he that is a companion of riotous
men shameth his father.
original_text:
Whoso keepeth the law
is a wise son: but he that is a companion of riotous
men shameth his father.

translated_text: He that by usury and unjust gain increaseth his substance, he shall gather it for him that will pity the poor.
original_text: He that by usury and unjust gain increaseth his substance, he shall gather it for him that will pity the poor.

translated_text:
He that turneth away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer
shall be abomination.
original_text:
He that turneth away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer
shall be abomination.

translated_text:
Whoso causeth the righteous to go astray in an evil way, he shall fall himself into his own pit: but the upright shall have good
things
 in possession.
original_text:
Whoso causeth the righteous to go astray in an evil way, he shall fall himself into his own pit: but the upright shall have good
things
 in possession.

translated_text:
The rich man
is wise in his own conceit; but the poor that hath understanding searcheth him out.
original_text:
The rich man
is wise in his own conceit; but the poor that hath understanding searcheth him out.

translated_text:
When righteous
men do rejoice,
there is great glory: but when the wicked rise, a man is hidden.
original_text:
When righteous
men do rejoice,
there is great glory: but when the wicked rise, a man is hidden.

translated_text:
He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh
them shall have mercy.
original_text:
He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh
them shall have mercy.

translated_text:
Happy
is the man that feareth alway: but he that hardeneth his heart shall fall into mischief.
original_text:
Happy
is the man that feareth alway: but he that hardeneth his heart shall fall into mischief.

translated_text:
As a roaring lion, and a ranging bear;
so is a wicked ruler over the poor people.
original_text:
As a roaring lion, and a ranging bear;
so is a wicked ruler over the poor people.

translated_text:
The prince that wanteth understanding
is also a great oppressor:
but he that hateth covetousness shall prolong
his
 days.
original_text:
The prince that wanteth understanding
is also a great oppressor:
but he that hateth covetousness shall prolong
his
 days.

translated_text:
A man that doeth violence to the blood of
any person shall flee to the pit; let no man stay him.
original_text:
A man that doeth violence to the blood of
any person shall flee to the pit; let no man stay him.

translated_text:
Whoso walketh uprightly shall be saved: but
he that is perverse
in his ways shall fall at once.
original_text:
Whoso walketh uprightly shall be saved: but
he that is perverse
in his ways shall fall at once.

translated_text:
He that tilleth his land shall have plenty of bread: but he that followeth after vain
persons shall have poverty enough.
original_text:
He that tilleth his land shall have plenty of bread: but he that followeth after vain
persons shall have poverty enough.

translated_text: A faithful man shall abound with blessings: but he that maketh haste to be rich shall not be innocent.
original_text: A faithful man shall abound with blessings: but he that maketh haste to be rich shall not be innocent.

translated_text:
To have respect of persons
is not good: for for a piece of bread
that man will transgress.
original_text:
To have respect of persons
is not good: for for a piece of bread
that man will transgress.

translated_text:
He that hasteth to be rich
hath an evil eye, and considereth not that poverty shall come upon him.
original_text:
He that hasteth to be rich
hath an evil eye, and considereth not that poverty shall come upon him.

translated_text: He that rebuketh a man afterwards shall find more favour than he that flattereth with the tongue.
original_text: He that rebuketh a man afterwards shall find more favour than he that flattereth with the tongue.

translated_text:
Whoso robbeth his father or his mother, and saith,
It is
 no transgression; the same
is the companion of a destroyer.
original_text:
Whoso robbeth his father or his mother, and saith,
It is
 no transgression; the same
is the companion of a destroyer.

translated_text: He that is of a proud heart stirreth up strife: but he that putteth his trust in the LORD shall be made fat.
original_text: He that is of a proud heart stirreth up strife: but he that putteth his trust in the LORD shall be made fat.

translated_text: He that trusteth in his own heart is a fool: but whoso walketh wisely, he shall be delivered.
original_text: He that trusteth in his own heart is a fool: but whoso walketh wisely, he shall be delivered.

translated_text: He that giveth unto the poor shall not lack: but he that hideth his eyes shall have many a curse.
original_text: He that giveth unto the poor shall not lack: but he that hideth his eyes shall have many a curse.

translated_text: When the wicked rise, men hide themselves: but when they perish, the righteous increase.
original_text: When the wicked rise, men hide themselves: but when they perish, the righteous increase.

translated_text:
Better
is the poor that walketh in his integrity, than
he that is perverse in his lips, and is a fool.
original_text:
Better
is the poor that walketh in his integrity, than
he that is perverse in his lips, and is a fool.

translated_text:
Also,
that the soul
be without knowledge,
it is
 not good; and he that hasteth with
his feet sinneth.
original_text:
Also,
that the soul
be without knowledge,
it is
 not good; and he that hasteth with
his feet sinneth.

translated_text: The foolishness of man perverteth his way: and his heart fretteth against the LORD.
original_text: The foolishness of man perverteth his way: and his heart fretteth against the LORD.

translated_text: Wealth maketh many friends; but the poor is separated from his neighbour.
original_text: Wealth maketh many friends; but the poor is separated from his neighbour.

translated_text:
A false witness shall not be unpunished, and
he that speaketh lies shall not escape.
original_text:
A false witness shall not be unpunished, and
he that speaketh lies shall not escape.

translated_text:
Many will intreat the favour of the prince: and every man
is
 a friend to him that giveth gifts.
original_text:
Many will intreat the favour of the prince: and every man
is
 a friend to him that giveth gifts.

translated_text:
All the brethren of the poor do hate him: how much more do his friends go far from him? he pursueth
them with words,
yet they
are wanting
to him.
original_text:
All the brethren of the poor do hate him: how much more do his friends go far from him? he pursueth
them with words,
yet they
are wanting
to him.

translated_text:
He that getteth wisdom loveth his own soul:
he that keepeth understanding shall find good.
original_text:
He that getteth wisdom loveth his own soul:
he that keepeth understanding shall find good.

translated_text: A false witness shall not be unpunished, and he that speaketh lies shall perish.
original_text: A false witness shall not be unpunished, and he that speaketh lies shall perish.

translated_text: Delight is not seemly for a fool; much less for a servant to have rule over princes.
original_text: Delight is not seemly for a fool; much less for a servant to have rule over princes.

translated_text:
The discretion of a man deferreth his anger; and
it is his glory to pass over a transgression.
original_text:
The discretion of a man deferreth his anger; and
it is his glory to pass over a transgression.

translated_text:
The king’s wrath
is as the roaring of a lion; but his favour
is as dew upon the grass.
original_text:
The king’s wrath
is as the roaring of a lion; but his favour
is as dew upon the grass.

translated_text:
A foolish son
is the calamity of his father: and the contentions of a wife
are a continual dropping.
original_text:
A foolish son
is the calamity of his father: and the contentions of a wife
are a continual dropping.

translated_text:
House and riches
are the inheritance of fathers and a prudent wife
is from the LORD.
original_text:
House and riches
are the inheritance of fathers and a prudent wife
is from the LORD.

translated_text: Slothfulness casteth into a deep sleep; and an idle soul shall suffer hunger.
original_text: Slothfulness casteth into a deep sleep; and an idle soul shall suffer hunger.

translated_text: He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto the LORD; and that which he hath given will he pay him again.
original_text: He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto the LORD; and that which he hath given will he pay him again.

translated_text: Chasten thy son while there is hope, and let not thy soul spare for his crying.
original_text: Chasten thy son while there is hope, and let not thy soul spare for his crying.

translated_text:
A man of great wrath shall suffer punishment: for if thou deliver
him, yet thou must do it again.
original_text:
A man of great wrath shall suffer punishment: for if thou deliver
him, yet thou must do it again.

translated_text: Hear counsel, and receive instruction, that thou mayest be wise in thy latter end.
original_text: Hear counsel, and receive instruction, that thou mayest be wise in thy latter end.

translated_text: There are many devices in a man’s heart; nevertheless the counsel of the LORD, that shall stand.
original_text: There are many devices in a man’s heart; nevertheless the counsel of the LORD, that shall stand.

translated_text:
The desire of a man
is his kindness: and a poor man
is better than a liar.
original_text:
The desire of a man
is his kindness: and a poor man
is better than a liar.

translated_text:
The fear of the LORD
tendeth to life: and
he that hath it shall abide satisfied; he shall not be visited with evil.
original_text:
The fear of the LORD
tendeth to life: and
he that hath it shall abide satisfied; he shall not be visited with evil.

translated_text:
A slothful
man hideth his hand in
his bosom, and will not so much as bring it to his mouth again.
original_text:
A slothful
man hideth his hand in
his bosom, and will not so much as bring it to his mouth again.

translated_text:
Smite a scorner, and the simple will beware: and reprove one that hath understanding,
and he will understand knowledge.
original_text:
Smite a scorner, and the simple will beware: and reprove one that hath understanding,
and he will understand knowledge.

translated_text:
He that wasteth
his father,
and chaseth away
his mother,
is a son that causeth shame, and bringeth reproach.
original_text:
He that wasteth
his father,
and chaseth away
his mother,
is a son that causeth shame, and bringeth reproach.

translated_text:
Cease, my son, to hear the instruction
that causeth to err from the words of knowledge.
original_text:
Cease, my son, to hear the instruction
that causeth to err from the words of knowledge.

translated_text: An ungodly witness scorneth judgment: and the mouth of the wicked devoureth iniquity.
original_text: An ungodly witness scorneth judgment: and the mouth of the wicked devoureth iniquity.

translated_text: Judgments are prepared for scorners, and stripes for the back of fools.
original_text: Judgments are prepared for scorners, and stripes for the back of fools.

translated_text:
So I returned, and considered all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and behold the tears of
such as were oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors
there was power; but they had no comforter.
original_text:
So I returned, and considered all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and behold the tears of
such as were oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors
there was power; but they had no comforter.

translated_text: Wherefore I praised the dead which are already dead more than the living which are yet alive.
original_text: Wherefore I praised the dead which are already dead more than the living which are yet alive.

translated_text:
Yea, better
is he than both they, which hath not yet been, who hath not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.
original_text:
Yea, better
is he than both they, which hath not yet been, who hath not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.

translated_text:
Again, I considered all travail, and every right work, that for this a man is envied of his neighbour. This
is also vanity and vexation of spirit.
original_text:
Again, I considered all travail, and every right work, that for this a man is envied of his neighbour. This
is also vanity and vexation of spirit.

translated_text: The fool foldeth his hands together, and eateth his own flesh.
original_text: The fool foldeth his hands together, and eateth his own flesh.

translated_text:
Better
is an handful
with quietness, than both the hands full
with travail and vexation of spirit.
original_text:
Better
is an handful
with quietness, than both the hands full
with travail and vexation of spirit.

translated_text: Then I returned, and I saw vanity under the sun.
original_text: Then I returned, and I saw vanity under the sun.

translated_text:
There is one
alone, and
there is not a second; yea, he hath neither child nor brother: yet
is there no end of all his labour; neither is his eye satisfied with riches; neither
saith he,
 For whom do I labour, and bereave my soul of good? This
is
 also vanity, yea, it
is a sore travail.
original_text:
There is one
alone, and
there is not a second; yea, he hath neither child nor brother: yet
is there no end of all his labour; neither is his eye satisfied with riches; neither
saith he,
 For whom do I labour, and bereave my soul of good? This
is
 also vanity, yea, it
is a sore travail.

translated_text:
Two
are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour.
original_text:
Two
are better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour.

translated_text:
For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him
that is alone when he falleth; for
he hath not another to help him up.
original_text:
For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him
that is alone when he falleth; for
he hath not another to help him up.

translated_text:
Again, if two lie together, then they have heat: but how can one be warm
alone?
original_text:
Again, if two lie together, then they have heat: but how can one be warm
alone?

translated_text: And if one prevail against him, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
original_text: And if one prevail against him, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.

translated_text:
Better
is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished.
original_text:
Better
is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished.

translated_text:
For out of prison he cometh to reign; whereas also
he that is
 born in his kingdom becometh poor.
original_text:
For out of prison he cometh to reign; whereas also
he that is
 born in his kingdom becometh poor.

translated_text: I considered all the living which walk under the sun, with the second child that shall stand up in his stead.
original_text: I considered all the living which walk under the sun, with the second child that shall stand up in his stead.

translated_text:
There is no end of all the people,
even of all that have been before them: they also that come after shall not rejoice in him. Surely this also
is vanity and vexation of spirit.
original_text:
There is no end of all the people,
even of all that have been before them: they also that come after shall not rejoice in him. Surely this also
is vanity and vexation of spirit.

translated_text:
To every
thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven:
original_text:
To every
thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven:

translated_text:
A time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pluck up
that which is planted;
original_text:
A time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pluck up
that which is planted;

translated_text: A time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to break down, and a time to build up;
original_text: A time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to break down, and a time to build up;

translated_text: A time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;
original_text: A time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;

translated_text: A time to cast away stones, and a time to gather stones together; a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing;
original_text: A time to cast away stones, and a time to gather stones together; a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing;

translated_text: A time to get, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to cast away;
original_text: A time to get, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to cast away;

translated_text: A time to rend, and a time to sew; a time to keep silence, and a time to speak;
original_text: A time to rend, and a time to sew; a time to keep silence, and a time to speak;

translated_text: A time to love, and a time to hate; a time of war, and a time of peace.
original_text: A time to love, and a time to hate; a time of war, and a time of peace.

translated_text: What profit hath he that worketh in that wherein he laboureth?
original_text: What profit hath he that worketh in that wherein he laboureth?

translated_text: I have seen the travail, which God hath given to the sons of men to be exercised in it.
original_text: I have seen the travail, which God hath given to the sons of men to be exercised in it.

translated_text:
He hath made every
