thing beautiful in his time: also he hath set the world in their heart, so that no man can find out the work that God maketh from the beginning to the end.
original_text:
He hath made every
thing beautiful in his time: also he hath set the world in their heart, so that no man can find out the work that God maketh from the beginning to the end.

translated_text:
I know that
there is no good in them, but for
a man
 to rejoice, and to do good in his life.
original_text:
I know that
there is no good in them, but for
a man
 to rejoice, and to do good in his life.

translated_text:
And also that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy the good of all his labour, it
is the gift of God.
original_text:
And also that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy the good of all his labour, it
is the gift of God.

translated_text:
I know that, whatsoever God doeth, it shall be for ever: nothing can be put to it, nor any thing taken from it: and God doeth
it, that
men should fear before him.
original_text:
I know that, whatsoever God doeth, it shall be for ever: nothing can be put to it, nor any thing taken from it: and God doeth
it, that
men should fear before him.

translated_text: That which hath been is now; and that which is to be hath already been; and God requireth that which is past.
original_text: That which hath been is now; and that which is to be hath already been; and God requireth that which is past.

translated_text:
And moreover I saw under the sun the place of judgment,
that
 wickedness
was there; and the place of righteousness,
that iniquity
was there.
original_text:
And moreover I saw under the sun the place of judgment,
that
 wickedness
was there; and the place of righteousness,
that iniquity
was there.

translated_text:
I said in mine heart, God shall judge the righteous and the wicked: for
there is a time there for every purpose and for every work.
original_text:
I said in mine heart, God shall judge the righteous and the wicked: for
there is a time there for every purpose and for every work.

translated_text: I said in mine heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.
original_text: I said in mine heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.

translated_text:
For that which befalleth the sons of men befalleth beasts; even one thing befalleth them: as the one dieth, so dieth the other; yea, they have all one breath; so that a man hath no preeminence above a beast: for all
is vanity.
original_text:
For that which befalleth the sons of men befalleth beasts; even one thing befalleth them: as the one dieth, so dieth the other; yea, they have all one breath; so that a man hath no preeminence above a beast: for all
is vanity.

translated_text: All go unto one place; all are of the dust, and all turn to dust again.
original_text: All go unto one place; all are of the dust, and all turn to dust again.

translated_text: Who knoweth the spirit of man that goeth upward, and the spirit of the beast that goeth downward to the earth?
original_text: Who knoweth the spirit of man that goeth upward, and the spirit of the beast that goeth downward to the earth?

translated_text:
Wherefore I perceive that
there is nothing better, than that a man should rejoice in his own works; for that
is his portion: for who shall bring him to see what shall be after him?
original_text:
Wherefore I perceive that
there is nothing better, than that a man should rejoice in his own works; for that
is his portion: for who shall bring him to see what shall be after him?

translated_text:
There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it
is
 common among men:
original_text:
There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it
is
 common among men:

translated_text:
A man to whom God hath given riches, wealth, and honour, so that he wanteth nothing for his soul of all that he desireth, yet God giveth him not power to eat thereof, but a stranger eateth it: this
is vanity, and it
is an evil disease.
original_text:
A man to whom God hath given riches, wealth, and honour, so that he wanteth nothing for his soul of all that he desireth, yet God giveth him not power to eat thereof, but a stranger eateth it: this
is vanity, and it
is an evil disease.

translated_text:
If a man beget an hundred
children, and live many years, so that the days of his years be many, and his soul be not filled with good, and also
that he have no burial; I say,
that an untimely birth
is better than he.
original_text:
If a man beget an hundred
children, and live many years, so that the days of his years be many, and his soul be not filled with good, and also
that he have no burial; I say,
that an untimely birth
is better than he.

translated_text: For he cometh in with vanity, and departeth in darkness, and his name shall be covered with darkness.
original_text: For he cometh in with vanity, and departeth in darkness, and his name shall be covered with darkness.

translated_text:
Moreover he hath not seen the sun, nor known
any thing: this hath more rest than the other.
original_text:
Moreover he hath not seen the sun, nor known
any thing: this hath more rest than the other.

translated_text:
Yea, though he live a thousand years twice
told, yet hath he seen no good: do not all go to one place?
original_text:
Yea, though he live a thousand years twice
told, yet hath he seen no good: do not all go to one place?

translated_text:
All the labour of man
is for his mouth, and yet the appetite is not filled.
original_text:
All the labour of man
is for his mouth, and yet the appetite is not filled.

translated_text: For what hath the wise more than the fool? what hath the poor, that knoweth to walk before the living?
original_text: For what hath the wise more than the fool? what hath the poor, that knoweth to walk before the living?

translated_text:
Better
is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the desire: this
is also vanity and vexation of spirit.
original_text:
Better
is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the desire: this
is also vanity and vexation of spirit.

translated_text:
That which hath been is named already, and it is known that it
is man: neither may he contend with him that is mightier than he.
original_text:
That which hath been is named already, and it is known that it
is man: neither may he contend with him that is mightier than he.

translated_text:
Seeing there be many things that increase vanity, what
is
 man the better?
original_text:
Seeing there be many things that increase vanity, what
is
 man the better?

translated_text:
For who knoweth what
is good for man in
this life, all the days of his vain life which he spendeth as a shadow? for who can tell a man what shall be after him under the sun?
original_text:
For who knoweth what
is good for man in
this life, all the days of his vain life which he spendeth as a shadow? for who can tell a man what shall be after him under the sun?

translated_text: Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God, and be more ready to hear, than to give the sacrifice of fools: for they consider not that they do evil.
original_text: Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God, and be more ready to hear, than to give the sacrifice of fools: for they consider not that they do evil.

translated_text:
Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thine heart be hasty to utter
any thing before God: for God
is in heaven, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy words be few.
original_text:
Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thine heart be hasty to utter
any thing before God: for God
is in heaven, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy words be few.

translated_text:
For a dream cometh through the multitude of business; and a fool’s voice
is known by multitude of words.
original_text:
For a dream cometh through the multitude of business; and a fool’s voice
is known by multitude of words.

translated_text:
When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for
he hath
 no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed.
original_text:
When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for
he hath
 no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed.

translated_text:
Better
is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.
original_text:
Better
is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.

translated_text:
Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say thou before the angel, that it
was an error: wherefore should God be angry at thy voice, and destroy the work of thine hands?
original_text:
Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say thou before the angel, that it
was an error: wherefore should God be angry at thy voice, and destroy the work of thine hands?

translated_text:
For in the multitude of dreams and many words
there are also
divers vanities: but fear thou God.
original_text:
For in the multitude of dreams and many words
there are also
divers vanities: but fear thou God.

translated_text:
If thou seest the oppression of the poor, and violent perverting of judgment and justice in a province, marvel not at the matter: for
he that is higher than the highest regardeth; and
there be higher than they.
original_text:
If thou seest the oppression of the poor, and violent perverting of judgment and justice in a province, marvel not at the matter: for
he that is higher than the highest regardeth; and
there be higher than they.

translated_text:
Moreover the profit of the earth is for all: the king
himself
 is served by the field.
original_text:
Moreover the profit of the earth is for all: the king
himself
 is served by the field.

translated_text:
He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he that loveth abundance with increase: this
is also vanity.
original_text:
He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he that loveth abundance with increase: this
is also vanity.

translated_text:
When goods increase, they are increased that eat them: and what good
is there to the owners thereof, saving the beholding
of them
 with their eyes?
original_text:
When goods increase, they are increased that eat them: and what good
is there to the owners thereof, saving the beholding
of them
 with their eyes?

translated_text:
The sleep of a labouring man
is sweet, whether he eat little or much: but the abundance of the rich will not suffer him to sleep.
original_text:
The sleep of a labouring man
is sweet, whether he eat little or much: but the abundance of the rich will not suffer him to sleep.

translated_text:
There is a sore evil
which I have seen under the sun,
namely, riches kept for the owners thereof to their hurt.
original_text:
There is a sore evil
which I have seen under the sun,
namely, riches kept for the owners thereof to their hurt.

translated_text:
But those riches perish by evil travail: and he begetteth a son, and
there is nothing in his hand.
original_text:
But those riches perish by evil travail: and he begetteth a son, and
there is nothing in his hand.

translated_text: As he came forth of his mother’s womb, naked shall he return to go as he came, and shall take nothing of his labour, which he may carry away in his hand.
original_text: As he came forth of his mother’s womb, naked shall he return to go as he came, and shall take nothing of his labour, which he may carry away in his hand.

translated_text:
And this also
is a sore evil,
that in all points as he came, so shall he go: and what profit hath he that hath laboured for the wind?
original_text:
And this also
is a sore evil,
that in all points as he came, so shall he go: and what profit hath he that hath laboured for the wind?

translated_text:
All his days also he eateth in darkness, and
he hath much sorrow and wrath with his sickness.
original_text:
All his days also he eateth in darkness, and
he hath much sorrow and wrath with his sickness.

translated_text:
Behold
that which I have seen:
it is good and comely
for one to eat and to drink, and to enjoy the good of all his labour that he taketh under the sun all the days of his life, which God giveth him: for it
is his portion.
original_text:
Behold
that which I have seen:
it is good and comely
for one to eat and to drink, and to enjoy the good of all his labour that he taketh under the sun all the days of his life, which God giveth him: for it
is his portion.

translated_text:
Every man also to whom God hath given riches and wealth, and hath given him power to eat thereof, and to take his portion, and to rejoice in his labour; this
is the gift of God.
original_text:
Every man also to whom God hath given riches and wealth, and hath given him power to eat thereof, and to take his portion, and to rejoice in his labour; this
is the gift of God.

translated_text:
For he shall not much remember the days of his life; because God answereth
him in the joy of his heart.
original_text:
For he shall not much remember the days of his life; because God answereth
him in the joy of his heart.

translated_text:
Who
is as the wise
man? and who knoweth the interpretation of a thing? a man’s wisdom maketh his face to shine, and the boldness of his face shall be changed.
original_text:
Who
is as the wise
man? and who knoweth the interpretation of a thing? a man’s wisdom maketh his face to shine, and the boldness of his face shall be changed.

translated_text:
I
counsel thee to keep the king’s commandment, and
that
 in regard of the oath of God.
original_text:
I
counsel thee to keep the king’s commandment, and
that
 in regard of the oath of God.

translated_text: Be not hasty to go out of his sight: stand not in an evil thing; for he doeth whatsoever pleaseth him.
original_text: Be not hasty to go out of his sight: stand not in an evil thing; for he doeth whatsoever pleaseth him.

translated_text:
Where the word of a king
is, there is power: and who may say unto him, What doest thou?
original_text:
Where the word of a king
is, there is power: and who may say unto him, What doest thou?

translated_text: Whoso keepeth the commandment shall feel no evil thing: and a wise man’s heart discerneth both time and judgment.
original_text: Whoso keepeth the commandment shall feel no evil thing: and a wise man’s heart discerneth both time and judgment.

translated_text:
Because to every purpose there is time and judgment, therefore the misery of man
is great upon him.
original_text:
Because to every purpose there is time and judgment, therefore the misery of man
is great upon him.

translated_text: For he knoweth not that which shall be: for who can tell him when it shall be?
original_text: For he knoweth not that which shall be: for who can tell him when it shall be?

translated_text:
There is no man that hath power over the spirit to retain the spirit; neither
hath he power in the day of death: and
there is no discharge in
that war; neither shall wickedness deliver those that are given to it.
original_text:
There is no man that hath power over the spirit to retain the spirit; neither
hath he power in the day of death: and
there is no discharge in
that war; neither shall wickedness deliver those that are given to it.

translated_text:
All this have I seen, and applied my heart unto every work that is done under the sun:
there is a time wherein one man ruleth over another to his own hurt.
original_text:
All this have I seen, and applied my heart unto every work that is done under the sun:
there is a time wherein one man ruleth over another to his own hurt.

translated_text:
And so I saw the wicked buried, who had come and gone from the place of the holy, and they were forgotten in the city where they had so done: this
is also vanity.
original_text:
And so I saw the wicked buried, who had come and gone from the place of the holy, and they were forgotten in the city where they had so done: this
is also vanity.

translated_text: Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.
original_text: Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.

translated_text:
Though a sinner do evil an hundred times, and his
days be prolonged, yet surely I know that it shall be well with them that fear God, which fear before him:
original_text:
Though a sinner do evil an hundred times, and his
days be prolonged, yet surely I know that it shall be well with them that fear God, which fear before him:

translated_text:
But it shall not be well with the wicked, neither shall he prolong
his days,
which are as a shadow; because he feareth not before God.
original_text:
But it shall not be well with the wicked, neither shall he prolong
his days,
which are as a shadow; because he feareth not before God.

translated_text:
There is a vanity which is done upon the earth; that there be just
men, unto whom it happeneth according to the work of the wicked; again, there be wicked
men, to whom it happeneth according to the work of the righteous: I said that this also
is vanity.
original_text:
There is a vanity which is done upon the earth; that there be just
men, unto whom it happeneth according to the work of the wicked; again, there be wicked
men, to whom it happeneth according to the work of the righteous: I said that this also
is vanity.

translated_text: Then I commended mirth, because a man hath no better thing under the sun, than to eat, and to drink, and to be merry: for that shall abide with him of his labour the days of his life, which God giveth him under the sun.
original_text: Then I commended mirth, because a man hath no better thing under the sun, than to eat, and to drink, and to be merry: for that shall abide with him of his labour the days of his life, which God giveth him under the sun.

translated_text:
When I applied mine heart to know wisdom, and to see the business that is done upon the earth: (for also
there is that neither day nor night seeth sleep with his eyes:)
original_text:
When I applied mine heart to know wisdom, and to see the business that is done upon the earth: (for also
there is that neither day nor night seeth sleep with his eyes:)

translated_text:
Then I beheld all the work of God, that a man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun: because though a man labour to seek
it
 out, yet he shall not find
it; yea further; though a wise
man think to know
it, yet shall he not be able to find
it.
original_text:
Then I beheld all the work of God, that a man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun: because though a man labour to seek
it
 out, yet he shall not find
it; yea further; though a wise
man think to know
it, yet shall he not be able to find
it.

translated_text:
A good name
is better than precious ointment; and the day of death than the day of one’s birth.
original_text:
A good name
is better than precious ointment; and the day of death than the day of one’s birth.

translated_text:
It is better to go to the house of mourning, than to go to the house of feasting: for that is the end of all men; and the living will lay
it to his heart.
original_text:
It is better to go to the house of mourning, than to go to the house of feasting: for that is the end of all men; and the living will lay
it to his heart.

translated_text:
Sorrow
is better than laughter: for by the sadness of the countenance the heart is made better.
original_text:
Sorrow
is better than laughter: for by the sadness of the countenance the heart is made better.

translated_text:
The heart of the wise
is in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools
is in the house of mirth.
original_text:
The heart of the wise
is in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools
is in the house of mirth.

translated_text: It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise, than for a man to hear the song of fools.
original_text: It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise, than for a man to hear the song of fools.

translated_text:
For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so
is the laughter of the fool: this also
is vanity.
original_text:
For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so
is the laughter of the fool: this also
is vanity.

translated_text: Surely oppression maketh a wise man mad; and a gift destroyeth the heart.
original_text: Surely oppression maketh a wise man mad; and a gift destroyeth the heart.

translated_text:
Better
is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof:
and the patient in spirit
is better than the proud in spirit.
original_text:
Better
is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof:
and the patient in spirit
is better than the proud in spirit.

translated_text: Be not hasty in thy spirit to be angry: for anger resteth in the bosom of fools.
original_text: Be not hasty in thy spirit to be angry: for anger resteth in the bosom of fools.

translated_text:
Say not thou, What is
the cause that the former days were better than these? for thou dost not enquire wisely concerning this.
original_text:
Say not thou, What is
the cause that the former days were better than these? for thou dost not enquire wisely concerning this.

translated_text:
Wisdom
is good with an inheritance: and
by it there is
 profit to them that see the sun.
original_text:
Wisdom
is good with an inheritance: and
by it there is
 profit to them that see the sun.

translated_text:
For wisdom
is a defence,
and money
is
 a defence: but the excellency of knowledge
is, that wisdom giveth life to them that have it.
original_text:
For wisdom
is a defence,
and money
is
 a defence: but the excellency of knowledge
is, that wisdom giveth life to them that have it.

translated_text:
Consider the work of God: for who can make
that straight, which he hath made crooked?
original_text:
Consider the work of God: for who can make
that straight, which he hath made crooked?

translated_text: In the day of prosperity be joyful, but in the day of adversity consider: God also hath set the one over against the other, to the end that man should find nothing after him.
original_text: In the day of prosperity be joyful, but in the day of adversity consider: God also hath set the one over against the other, to the end that man should find nothing after him.

translated_text:
All
things have I seen in the days of my vanity: there is a just
man that perisheth in his righteousness, and there is a wicked
man that prolongeth
his life in his wickedness.
original_text:
All
things have I seen in the days of my vanity: there is a just
man that perisheth in his righteousness, and there is a wicked
man that prolongeth
his life in his wickedness.

translated_text: Be not righteous over much; neither make thyself over wise: why shouldest thou destroy thyself?
original_text: Be not righteous over much; neither make thyself over wise: why shouldest thou destroy thyself?

translated_text: Be not over much wicked, neither be thou foolish: why shouldest thou die before thy time?
original_text: Be not over much wicked, neither be thou foolish: why shouldest thou die before thy time?

translated_text: It is good that thou shouldest take hold of this; yea, also from this withdraw not thine hand: for he that feareth God shall come forth of them all.
original_text: It is good that thou shouldest take hold of this; yea, also from this withdraw not thine hand: for he that feareth God shall come forth of them all.

translated_text:
Wisdom strengtheneth the wise more than ten mighty
men which are in the city.
original_text:
Wisdom strengtheneth the wise more than ten mighty
men which are in the city.

translated_text:
For
there is not a just man upon earth, that doeth good, and sinneth not.
original_text:
For
there is not a just man upon earth, that doeth good, and sinneth not.

translated_text: Also take no heed unto all words that are spoken; lest thou hear thy servant curse thee:
original_text: Also take no heed unto all words that are spoken; lest thou hear thy servant curse thee:

translated_text: For oftentimes also thine own heart knoweth that thou thyself likewise hast cursed others.
original_text: For oftentimes also thine own heart knoweth that thou thyself likewise hast cursed others.

translated_text:
All this have I proved by wisdom: I said, I will be wise; but it
was far from me.
original_text:
All this have I proved by wisdom: I said, I will be wise; but it
was far from me.

translated_text: That which is far off, and exceeding deep, who can find it out?
original_text: That which is far off, and exceeding deep, who can find it out?

translated_text:
I applied mine heart to know, and to search, and to seek out wisdom, and the reason
of things, and to know the wickedness of folly, even of foolishness
and madness:
original_text:
I applied mine heart to know, and to search, and to seek out wisdom, and the reason
of things, and to know the wickedness of folly, even of foolishness
and madness:

translated_text:
And I find more bitter than death the woman, whose heart
is
 snares and nets,
and her hands
as bands: whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be taken by her.
original_text:
And I find more bitter than death the woman, whose heart
is
 snares and nets,
and her hands
as bands: whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be taken by her.

translated_text:
Behold, this have I found, saith the preacher,
counting one by one, to find out the account:
original_text:
Behold, this have I found, saith the preacher,
counting one by one, to find out the account:

translated_text: Which yet my soul seeketh, but I find not: one man among a thousand have I found; but a woman among all those have I not found.
original_text: Which yet my soul seeketh, but I find not: one man among a thousand have I found; but a woman among all those have I not found.

translated_text: Lo, this only have I found, that God hath made man upright; but they have sought out many inventions.
original_text: Lo, this only have I found, that God hath made man upright; but they have sought out many inventions.

translated_text:
For all this I considered in my heart even to declare all this, that the righteous, and the wise, and their works, are in the hand of God: no man knoweth either love or hatred
by all
that is before them.
original_text:
For all this I considered in my heart even to declare all this, that the righteous, and the wise, and their works, are in the hand of God: no man knoweth either love or hatred
by all
that is before them.

translated_text:
All
things come alike to all:
there is one event to the righteous, and to the wicked; to the good and to the clean, and to the unclean; to him that sacrificeth, and to him that sacrificeth not: as
is the good, so
is the sinner;
and he that sweareth, as
he that feareth an oath.
original_text:
All
things come alike to all:
there is one event to the righteous, and to the wicked; to the good and to the clean, and to the unclean; to him that sacrificeth, and to him that sacrificeth not: as
is the good, so
is the sinner;
and he that sweareth, as
he that feareth an oath.

translated_text:
This
is an evil among all
things that are done under the sun, that
there is one event unto all: yea, also the heart of the sons of men is full of evil, and madness is in their heart while they live, and after that
they go to the dead.
original_text:
This
is an evil among all
things that are done under the sun, that
there is one event unto all: yea, also the heart of the sons of men is full of evil, and madness is in their heart while they live, and after that
they go to the dead.

translated_text: For to him that is joined to all the living there is hope: for a living dog is better than a dead lion.
original_text: For to him that is joined to all the living there is hope: for a living dog is better than a dead lion.

translated_text: For the living know that they shall die: but the dead know not any thing, neither have they any more a reward; for the memory of them is forgotten.
original_text: For the living know that they shall die: but the dead know not any thing, neither have they any more a reward; for the memory of them is forgotten.

translated_text:
Also their love, and their hatred, and their envy, is now perished; neither have they any more a portion for ever in any
thing that is done under the sun.
original_text:
Also their love, and their hatred, and their envy, is now perished; neither have they any more a portion for ever in any
thing that is done under the sun.

translated_text: Go thy way, eat thy bread with joy, and drink thy wine with a merry heart; for God now accepteth thy works.
original_text: Go thy way, eat thy bread with joy, and drink thy wine with a merry heart; for God now accepteth thy works.

translated_text: Let thy garments be always white; and let thy head lack no ointment.
original_text: Let thy garments be always white; and let thy head lack no ointment.

translated_text:
Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun, all the days of thy vanity: for that
is thy portion in
this life, and in thy labour which thou takest under the sun.
original_text:
Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun, all the days of thy vanity: for that
is thy portion in
this life, and in thy labour which thou takest under the sun.

translated_text:
Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do
it with thy might; for
there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in the grave, whither thou goest.
original_text:
Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do
it with thy might; for
there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in the grave, whither thou goest.

translated_text:
I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race
is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favour to men of skill; but time and chance happeneth to them all.
original_text:
I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race
is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favour to men of skill; but time and chance happeneth to them all.

translated_text:
For man also knoweth not his time: as the fishes that are taken in an evil net, and as the birds that are caught in the snare; so
are
 the sons of men snared in an evil time, when it falleth suddenly upon them.
original_text:
For man also knoweth not his time: as the fishes that are taken in an evil net, and as the birds that are caught in the snare; so
are
 the sons of men snared in an evil time, when it falleth suddenly upon them.

translated_text:
This wisdom have I seen also under the sun, and it
seemed
 great unto me:
original_text:
This wisdom have I seen also under the sun, and it
seemed
 great unto me:

translated_text: There was a little city, and few men within it; and there came a great king against it, and besieged it, and built great bulwarks against it:
original_text: There was a little city, and few men within it; and there came a great king against it, and besieged it, and built great bulwarks against it:

translated_text: Now there was found in it a poor wise man, and he by his wisdom delivered the city; yet no man remembered that same poor man.
original_text: Now there was found in it a poor wise man, and he by his wisdom delivered the city; yet no man remembered that same poor man.

translated_text:
Then said I, Wisdom
is better than strength: nevertheless the poor man’s wisdom
is despised, and his words are not heard.
original_text:
Then said I, Wisdom
is better than strength: nevertheless the poor man’s wisdom
is despised, and his words are not heard.

translated_text:
The words of wise
men are heard in quiet more than the cry of him that ruleth among fools.
original_text:
The words of wise
men are heard in quiet more than the cry of him that ruleth among fools.

translated_text:
Wisdom
is better than weapons of war: but one sinner destroyeth much good.
original_text:
Wisdom
is better than weapons of war: but one sinner destroyeth much good.

translated_text:
I said in mine heart, Go to now, I will prove thee with mirth, therefore enjoy pleasure: and, behold, this also
is vanity.
original_text:
I said in mine heart, Go to now, I will prove thee with mirth, therefore enjoy pleasure: and, behold, this also
is vanity.

translated_text:
I said of laughter,
It is mad: and of mirth, What doeth it?
original_text:
I said of laughter,
It is mad: and of mirth, What doeth it?

translated_text:
I sought in mine heart to give myself unto wine, yet acquainting mine heart with wisdom; and to lay hold on folly, till I might see what
was
 that good for the sons of men, which they should do under the heaven all the days of their life.
original_text:
I sought in mine heart to give myself unto wine, yet acquainting mine heart with wisdom; and to lay hold on folly, till I might see what
was
 that good for the sons of men, which they should do under the heaven all the days of their life.

translated_text: I made me great works; I builded me houses; I planted me vineyards:
original_text: I made me great works; I builded me houses; I planted me vineyards:

translated_text:
I made me gardens and orchards, and I planted trees in them of all
kind of fruits:
original_text:
I made me gardens and orchards, and I planted trees in them of all
kind of fruits:

translated_text: I made me pools of water, to water therewith the wood that bringeth forth trees:
original_text: I made me pools of water, to water therewith the wood that bringeth forth trees:

translated_text:
I got
me servants and maidens, and had servants born in my house; also I had great possessions of great and small cattle above all that were in Jerusalem before me:
original_text:
I got
me servants and maidens, and had servants born in my house; also I had great possessions of great and small cattle above all that were in Jerusalem before me:

translated_text:
I gathered me also silver and gold, and the peculiar treasure of kings and of the provinces: I gat me men singers and women singers, and the delights of the sons of men,
as musical instruments, and that of all sorts.
original_text:
I gathered me also silver and gold, and the peculiar treasure of kings and of the provinces: I gat me men singers and women singers, and the delights of the sons of men,
as musical instruments, and that of all sorts.

translated_text: So I was great, and increased more than all that were before me in Jerusalem: also my wisdom remained with me.
original_text: So I was great, and increased more than all that were before me in Jerusalem: also my wisdom remained with me.

translated_text: And whatsoever mine eyes desired I kept not from them, I withheld not my heart from any joy; for my heart rejoiced in all my labour: and this was my portion of all my labour.
original_text: And whatsoever mine eyes desired I kept not from them, I withheld not my heart from any joy; for my heart rejoiced in all my labour: and this was my portion of all my labour.

translated_text:
Then I looked on all the works that my hands had wrought, and on the labour that I had laboured to do: and, behold, all
was vanity and vexation of spirit, and
there was no profit under the sun.
original_text:
Then I looked on all the works that my hands had wrought, and on the labour that I had laboured to do: and, behold, all
was vanity and vexation of spirit, and
there was no profit under the sun.

translated_text:
And I turned myself to behold wisdom, and madness, and folly: for what
can the man
do that cometh after the king?
even
 that which hath been already done.
original_text:
And I turned myself to behold wisdom, and madness, and folly: for what
can the man
do that cometh after the king?
even
 that which hath been already done.

translated_text: Then I saw that wisdom excelleth folly, as far as light excelleth darkness.
original_text: Then I saw that wisdom excelleth folly, as far as light excelleth darkness.

translated_text:
The wise man’s eyes
are in his head; but the fool walketh in darkness: and I myself perceived also that one event happeneth to them all.
original_text:
The wise man’s eyes
are in his head; but the fool walketh in darkness: and I myself perceived also that one event happeneth to them all.

translated_text:
Then said I in my heart, As it happeneth to the fool, so it happeneth even to me; and why was I then more wise? Then I said in my heart, that this also
is vanity.
original_text:
Then said I in my heart, As it happeneth to the fool, so it happeneth even to me; and why was I then more wise? Then I said in my heart, that this also
is vanity.

translated_text:
For
there is no remembrance of the wise more than of the fool for ever; seeing that which now
is in the days to come shall all be forgotten. And how dieth the wise
man? as the fool.
original_text:
For
there is no remembrance of the wise more than of the fool for ever; seeing that which now
is in the days to come shall all be forgotten. And how dieth the wise
man? as the fool.

translated_text:
Therefore I hated life; because the work that is wrought under the sun is grievous unto me: for all
is vanity and vexation of spirit.
original_text:
Therefore I hated life; because the work that is wrought under the sun is grievous unto me: for all
is vanity and vexation of spirit.

translated_text: Yea, I hated all my labour which I had taken under the sun: because I should leave it unto the man that shall be after me.
original_text: Yea, I hated all my labour which I had taken under the sun: because I should leave it unto the man that shall be after me.

translated_text:
And who knoweth whether he shall be a wise
man or a fool? yet shall he have rule over all my labour wherein I have laboured, and wherein I have shewed myself wise under the sun. This
is also vanity.
original_text:
And who knoweth whether he shall be a wise
man or a fool? yet shall he have rule over all my labour wherein I have laboured, and wherein I have shewed myself wise under the sun. This
is also vanity.

translated_text: Therefore I went about to cause my heart to despair of all the labour which I took under the sun.
original_text: Therefore I went about to cause my heart to despair of all the labour which I took under the sun.

translated_text:
For there is a man whose labour
is in wisdom, and in knowledge, and in equity; yet to a man that hath not laboured therein shall he leave it
for his portion. This also
is vanity and a great evil.
original_text:
For there is a man whose labour
is in wisdom, and in knowledge, and in equity; yet to a man that hath not laboured therein shall he leave it
for his portion. This also
is vanity and a great evil.

translated_text: For what hath man of all his labour, and of the vexation of his heart, wherein he hath laboured under the sun?
original_text: For what hath man of all his labour, and of the vexation of his heart, wherein he hath laboured under the sun?

translated_text:
For all his days
are sorrows, and his travail grief; yea, his heart taketh not rest in the night. This is also vanity.
original_text:
For all his days
are sorrows, and his travail grief; yea, his heart taketh not rest in the night. This is also vanity.

translated_text:
There is nothing better for a man,
than that he should eat and drink, and
that he should make his soul enjoy good in his labour. This also I saw, that it
was from the hand of God.
original_text:
There is nothing better for a man,
than that he should eat and drink, and
that he should make his soul enjoy good in his labour. This also I saw, that it
was from the hand of God.

translated_text:
For who can eat, or who else can hasten
hereunto, more than I?
original_text:
For who can eat, or who else can hasten
hereunto, more than I?

translated_text:
For
God giveth to a man that
is good in his sight wisdom, and knowledge, and joy: but to the sinner he giveth travail, to gather and to heap up, that he may give to
him that is good before God. This also
is vanity and vexation of spirit.
original_text:
For
God giveth to a man that
is good in his sight wisdom, and knowledge, and joy: but to the sinner he giveth travail, to gather and to heap up, that he may give to
him that is good before God. This also
is vanity and vexation of spirit.

translated_text: The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.
original_text: The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.

translated_text:
Vanity of vanities, saith the Preacher, vanity of vanities; all
is vanity.
original_text:
Vanity of vanities, saith the Preacher, vanity of vanities; all
is vanity.

translated_text: What profit hath a man of all his labour which he taketh under the sun?
original_text: What profit hath a man of all his labour which he taketh under the sun?

translated_text:
One generation passeth away, and
another generation cometh: but the earth abideth for ever.
original_text:
One generation passeth away, and
another generation cometh: but the earth abideth for ever.

translated_text: The sun also ariseth, and the sun goeth down, and hasteth to his place where he arose.
original_text: The sun also ariseth, and the sun goeth down, and hasteth to his place where he arose.

translated_text: The wind goeth toward the south, and turneth about unto the north; it whirleth about continually, and the wind returneth again according to his circuits.
original_text: The wind goeth toward the south, and turneth about unto the north; it whirleth about continually, and the wind returneth again according to his circuits.

translated_text:
All the rivers run into the sea; yet the sea
is not full; unto the place from whence the rivers come, thither they return again.
original_text:
All the rivers run into the sea; yet the sea
is not full; unto the place from whence the rivers come, thither they return again.

translated_text:
All things
are full of labour; man cannot utter
it:
 the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.
original_text:
All things
are full of labour; man cannot utter
it:
 the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.

translated_text:
The thing that hath been, it
is that which shall be; and that which is done
is that which shall be done: and
there is
 no new
thing under the sun.
original_text:
The thing that hath been, it
is that which shall be; and that which is done
is that which shall be done: and
there is
 no new
thing under the sun.

translated_text:
Is there
any thing whereof it may be said, See, this
is new? it hath been already of old time, which was before us.
original_text:
Is there
any thing whereof it may be said, See, this
is new? it hath been already of old time, which was before us.

translated_text:
There is no remembrance of former
things; neither shall there be
any remembrance of
things that are to come with
those that shall come after.
original_text:
There is no remembrance of former
things; neither shall there be
any remembrance of
things that are to come with
those that shall come after.

translated_text: I the Preacher was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
original_text: I the Preacher was king over Israel in Jerusalem.

translated_text:
And I gave my heart to seek and search out by wisdom concerning all
things that are done under heaven: this sore travail hath God given to the sons of man to be exercised therewith.
original_text:
And I gave my heart to seek and search out by wisdom concerning all
things that are done under heaven: this sore travail hath God given to the sons of man to be exercised therewith.

translated_text:
I have seen all the works that are done under the sun; and, behold, all
is vanity and vexation of spirit.
original_text:
I have seen all the works that are done under the sun; and, behold, all
is vanity and vexation of spirit.

translated_text: That which is crooked cannot be made straight: and that which is wanting cannot be numbered.
original_text: That which is crooked cannot be made straight: and that which is wanting cannot be numbered.

translated_text:
I communed with mine own heart, saying, Lo, I am come to great estate, and have gotten more wisdom than all
they that have been before me in Jerusalem: yea, my heart had great experience of wisdom and knowledge.
original_text:
I communed with mine own heart, saying, Lo, I am come to great estate, and have gotten more wisdom than all
they that have been before me in Jerusalem: yea, my heart had great experience of wisdom and knowledge.

translated_text: And I gave my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly: I perceived that this also is vexation of spirit.
original_text: And I gave my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly: I perceived that this also is vexation of spirit.

translated_text:
For in much wisdom
is much grief: and he that increaseth knowledge increaseth sorrow.
original_text:
For in much wisdom
is much grief: and he that increaseth knowledge increaseth sorrow.

translated_text:
Dead flies cause the ointment of the apothecary to send forth a stinking savour:
so doth a little folly him that is in reputation for wisdom
and honour.
original_text:
Dead flies cause the ointment of the apothecary to send forth a stinking savour:
so doth a little folly him that is in reputation for wisdom
and honour.

translated_text:
A wise man’s heart
is at his right hand; but a fool’s heart at his left.
original_text:
A wise man’s heart
is at his right hand; but a fool’s heart at his left.

translated_text:
Yea also, when he that is a fool walketh by the way, his wisdom faileth
him, and he saith to every one
that he
is a fool.
original_text:
Yea also, when he that is a fool walketh by the way, his wisdom faileth
him, and he saith to every one
that he
is a fool.

translated_text: If the spirit of the ruler rise up against thee, leave not thy place; for yielding pacifieth great offences.
original_text: If the spirit of the ruler rise up against thee, leave not thy place; for yielding pacifieth great offences.

translated_text:
There is an evil
which I have seen under the sun, as an error
which proceedeth from the ruler:
original_text:
There is an evil
which I have seen under the sun, as an error
which proceedeth from the ruler:

translated_text: Folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in low place.
original_text: Folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in low place.

translated_text: I have seen servants upon horses, and princes walking as servants upon the earth.
original_text: I have seen servants upon horses, and princes walking as servants upon the earth.

translated_text: He that diggeth a pit shall fall into it; and whoso breaketh an hedge, a serpent shall bite him.
original_text: He that diggeth a pit shall fall into it; and whoso breaketh an hedge, a serpent shall bite him.

translated_text:
Whoso removeth stones shall be hurt therewith;
and he that cleaveth wood shall be endangered thereby.
original_text:
Whoso removeth stones shall be hurt therewith;
and he that cleaveth wood shall be endangered thereby.

translated_text:
If the iron be blunt, and he do not whet the edge, then must he put to more strength: but wisdom
is profitable to direct.
original_text:
If the iron be blunt, and he do not whet the edge, then must he put to more strength: but wisdom
is profitable to direct.

translated_text: Surely the serpent will bite without enchantment; and a babbler is no better.
original_text: Surely the serpent will bite without enchantment; and a babbler is no better.

translated_text:
The words of a wise man’s mouth
are gracious; but the lips of a fool will swallow up himself.
original_text:
The words of a wise man’s mouth
are gracious; but the lips of a fool will swallow up himself.

translated_text:
The beginning of the words of his mouth
is foolishness: and the end of his talk
is mischievous madness.
original_text:
The beginning of the words of his mouth
is foolishness: and the end of his talk
is mischievous madness.

translated_text: A fool also is full of words: a man cannot tell what shall be; and what shall be after him, who can tell him?
original_text: A fool also is full of words: a man cannot tell what shall be; and what shall be after him, who can tell him?

translated_text: The labour of the foolish wearieth every one of them, because he knoweth not how to go to the city.
original_text: The labour of the foolish wearieth every one of them, because he knoweth not how to go to the city.

translated_text:
Woe to thee, O land, when thy king
is a child, and thy princes eat in the morning!
original_text:
Woe to thee, O land, when thy king
is a child, and thy princes eat in the morning!

translated_text:
Blessed
art thou, O land, when thy king
is the son of nobles, and thy princes eat in due season, for strength, and not for drunkenness!
original_text:
Blessed
art thou, O land, when thy king
is the son of nobles, and thy princes eat in due season, for strength, and not for drunkenness!

translated_text: By much slothfulness the building decayeth; and through idleness of the hands the house droppeth through.
original_text: By much slothfulness the building decayeth; and through idleness of the hands the house droppeth through.

translated_text:
A feast is made for laughter, and wine maketh merry: but money answereth all
things.
original_text:
A feast is made for laughter, and wine maketh merry: but money answereth all
things.

translated_text: Curse not the king, no not in thy thought; and curse not the rich in thy bedchamber: for a bird of the air shall carry the voice, and that which hath wings shall tell the matter.
original_text: Curse not the king, no not in thy thought; and curse not the rich in thy bedchamber: for a bird of the air shall carry the voice, and that which hath wings shall tell the matter.

translated_text: Cast thy bread upon the waters: for thou shalt find it after many days.
original_text: Cast thy bread upon the waters: for thou shalt find it after many days.

translated_text: Give a portion to seven, and also to eight; for thou knowest not what evil shall be upon the earth.
original_text: Give a portion to seven, and also to eight; for thou knowest not what evil shall be upon the earth.

translated_text:
If the clouds be full of rain, they empty
themselves upon the earth: and if the tree fall toward the south, or toward the north, in the place where the tree falleth, there it shall be.
original_text:
If the clouds be full of rain, they empty
themselves upon the earth: and if the tree fall toward the south, or toward the north, in the place where the tree falleth, there it shall be.

translated_text: He that observeth the wind shall not sow; and he that regardeth the clouds shall not reap.
original_text: He that observeth the wind shall not sow; and he that regardeth the clouds shall not reap.

translated_text:
As thou knowest not what
is the way of the spirit,
nor
 how the bones
do grow in the womb of her that is with child: even so thou knowest not the works of God who maketh all.
original_text:
As thou knowest not what
is the way of the spirit,
nor
 how the bones
do grow in the womb of her that is with child: even so thou knowest not the works of God who maketh all.

translated_text:
In the morning sow thy seed, and in the evening withhold not thine hand: for thou knowest not whether shall prosper, either this or that, or whether they both
shall be alike good.
original_text:
In the morning sow thy seed, and in the evening withhold not thine hand: for thou knowest not whether shall prosper, either this or that, or whether they both
shall be alike good.

translated_text:
Truly the light
is sweet, and a pleasant
thing it is
 for the eyes to behold the sun:
original_text:
Truly the light
is sweet, and a pleasant
thing it is
 for the eyes to behold the sun:

translated_text:
But if a man live many years,
and rejoice in them all; yet let him remember the days of darkness; for they shall be many. All that cometh
is vanity.
original_text:
But if a man live many years,
and rejoice in them all; yet let him remember the days of darkness; for they shall be many. All that cometh
is vanity.

translated_text:
Rejoice, O young man, in thy youth; and let thy heart cheer thee in the days of thy youth, and walk in the ways of thine heart, and in the sight of thine eyes: but know thou, that for all these
things God will bring thee into judgment.
original_text:
Rejoice, O young man, in thy youth; and let thy heart cheer thee in the days of thy youth, and walk in the ways of thine heart, and in the sight of thine eyes: but know thou, that for all these
things God will bring thee into judgment.

translated_text:
Therefore remove sorrow from thy heart, and put away evil from thy flesh: for childhood and youth
are vanity.
original_text:
Therefore remove sorrow from thy heart, and put away evil from thy flesh: for childhood and youth
are vanity.

translated_text: Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth, while the evil days come not, nor the years draw nigh, when thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them;
original_text: Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth, while the evil days come not, nor the years draw nigh, when thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them;

translated_text: While the sun, or the light, or the moon, or the stars, be not darkened, nor the clouds return after the rain:
original_text: While the sun, or the light, or the moon, or the stars, be not darkened, nor the clouds return after the rain:

translated_text: In the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those that look out of the windows be darkened,
original_text: In the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those that look out of the windows be darkened,

translated_text: And the doors shall be shut in the streets, when the sound of the grinding is low, and he shall rise up at the voice of the bird, and all the daughters of musick shall be brought low;
original_text: And the doors shall be shut in the streets, when the sound of the grinding is low, and he shall rise up at the voice of the bird, and all the daughters of musick shall be brought low;

translated_text:
Also
when they shall be afraid of
that which is
 high, and fears
shall be in the way, and the almond tree shall flourish, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail: because man goeth to his long home, and the mourners go about the streets:
original_text:
Also
when they shall be afraid of
that which is
 high, and fears
shall be in the way, and the almond tree shall flourish, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail: because man goeth to his long home, and the mourners go about the streets:

translated_text: Or ever the silver cord be loosed, or the golden bowl be broken, or the pitcher be broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern.
original_text: Or ever the silver cord be loosed, or the golden bowl be broken, or the pitcher be broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern.

translated_text: Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.
original_text: Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.

translated_text:
Vanity of vanities, saith the preacher; all
is vanity.
original_text:
Vanity of vanities, saith the preacher; all
is vanity.

translated_text:
And moreover, because the preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge; yea, he gave good heed, and sought out,
and set in order many proverbs.
original_text:
And moreover, because the preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge; yea, he gave good heed, and sought out,
and set in order many proverbs.

translated_text:
The preacher sought to find out acceptable words: and
that which was written
was upright,
even words of truth.
original_text:
The preacher sought to find out acceptable words: and
that which was written
was upright,
even words of truth.

translated_text:
The words of the wise
are as goads, and as nails fastened by the masters of assemblies,
which are given from one shepherd.
original_text:
The words of the wise
are as goads, and as nails fastened by the masters of assemblies,
which are given from one shepherd.

translated_text:
And further, by these, my son, be admonished: of making many books
there is no end; and much study
is a weariness of the flesh.
original_text:
And further, by these, my son, be admonished: of making many books
there is no end; and much study
is a weariness of the flesh.

translated_text:
Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this
is the whole
duty of man.
original_text:
Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this
is the whole
duty of man.

translated_text:
For God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether
it be good, or whether
it be evil.
original_text:
For God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether
it be good, or whether
it be evil.

translated_text:
How beautiful are thy feet with shoes, O prince’s daughter! the joints of thy thighs
are like jewels, the work of the hands of a cunning workman.
original_text:
How beautiful are thy feet with shoes, O prince’s daughter! the joints of thy thighs
are like jewels, the work of the hands of a cunning workman.

translated_text:
Thy navel
is like a round goblet,
which wanteth not liquor: thy belly
is like an heap of wheat set about with lilies.
original_text:
Thy navel
is like a round goblet,
which wanteth not liquor: thy belly
is like an heap of wheat set about with lilies.

translated_text:
Thy two breasts
are like two young roes
that are
 twins.
original_text:
Thy two breasts
are like two young roes
that are
 twins.

translated_text:
Thy neck
is as a tower of ivory; thine eyes
like
 the fishpools in Heshbon, by the gate of Bath-rabbim: thy nose
is as the tower of Lebanon which looketh toward Damascus.
original_text:
Thy neck
is as a tower of ivory; thine eyes
like
 the fishpools in Heshbon, by the gate of Bath-rabbim: thy nose
is as the tower of Lebanon which looketh toward Damascus.

translated_text:
Thine head upon thee
is like Carmel, and the hair of thine head like purple; the king
is held in the galleries.
original_text:
Thine head upon thee
is like Carmel, and the hair of thine head like purple; the king
is held in the galleries.

translated_text: How fair and how pleasant art thou, O love, for delights!
original_text: How fair and how pleasant art thou, O love, for delights!

translated_text:
This thy stature is like to a palm tree, and thy breasts to clusters
of grapes.
original_text:
This thy stature is like to a palm tree, and thy breasts to clusters
of grapes.

translated_text: I said, I will go up to the palm tree, I will take hold of the boughs thereof: now also thy breasts shall be as clusters of the vine, and the smell of thy nose like apples;
original_text: I said, I will go up to the palm tree, I will take hold of the boughs thereof: now also thy breasts shall be as clusters of the vine, and the smell of thy nose like apples;

translated_text:
And the roof of thy mouth like the best wine for my beloved, that goeth
down sweetly, causing the lips of those that are asleep to speak.
original_text:
And the roof of thy mouth like the best wine for my beloved, that goeth
down sweetly, causing the lips of those that are asleep to speak.

translated_text:
I
am my beloved’s, and his desire
is toward me.
original_text:
I
am my beloved’s, and his desire
is toward me.

translated_text: Come, my beloved, let us go forth into the field; let us lodge in the villages.
original_text: Come, my beloved, let us go forth into the field; let us lodge in the villages.

translated_text:
Let us get up early to the vineyards; let us see if the vine flourish,
whether the tender grape appear,
and the pomegranates bud forth: there will I give thee my loves.
original_text:
Let us get up early to the vineyards; let us see if the vine flourish,
whether the tender grape appear,
and the pomegranates bud forth: there will I give thee my loves.

translated_text:
The mandrakes give a smell, and at our gates
are all manner of pleasant
fruits, new and old,
which I have laid up for thee, O my beloved.
original_text:
The mandrakes give a smell, and at our gates
are all manner of pleasant
fruits, new and old,
which I have laid up for thee, O my beloved.

translated_text: Whither is thy beloved gone, O thou fairest among women? whither is thy beloved turned aside? that we may seek him with thee.
original_text: Whither is thy beloved gone, O thou fairest among women? whither is thy beloved turned aside? that we may seek him with thee.

translated_text: My beloved is gone down into his garden, to the beds of spices, to feed in the gardens, and to gather lilies.
original_text: My beloved is gone down into his garden, to the beds of spices, to feed in the gardens, and to gather lilies.

translated_text:
I
am my beloved’s, and my beloved
is mine: he feedeth among the lilies.
original_text:
I
am my beloved’s, and my beloved
is mine: he feedeth among the lilies.

translated_text:
Thou
art beautiful, O my love, as Tirzah, comely as Jerusalem, terrible as
an army with banners.
original_text:
Thou
art beautiful, O my love, as Tirzah, comely as Jerusalem, terrible as
an army with banners.

translated_text:
Turn away thine eyes from me, for they have overcome me: thy hair
is as a flock of goats that appear from Gilead.
original_text:
Turn away thine eyes from me, for they have overcome me: thy hair
is as a flock of goats that appear from Gilead.

translated_text:
Thy teeth
are as a flock of sheep which go up from the washing, whereof every one beareth twins, and
there is not one barren among them.
original_text:
Thy teeth
are as a flock of sheep which go up from the washing, whereof every one beareth twins, and
there is not one barren among them.

translated_text:
As a piece of a pomegranate
are thy temples within thy locks.
original_text:
As a piece of a pomegranate
are thy temples within thy locks.

translated_text: There are threescore queens, and fourscore concubines, and virgins without number.
original_text: There are threescore queens, and fourscore concubines, and virgins without number.

translated_text:
My dove, my undefiled is
but one; she
is the
only one of her mother, she
is the choice
one
 of her that bare her. The daughters saw her, and blessed her;
yea, the queens and the concubines, and they praised her.
original_text:
My dove, my undefiled is
but one; she
is the
only one of her mother, she
is the choice
one
 of her that bare her. The daughters saw her, and blessed her;
yea, the queens and the concubines, and they praised her.

translated_text:
Who
is she
that looketh forth as the morning, fair as the moon, clear as the sun,
and terrible as
an army
 with banners?
original_text:
Who
is she
that looketh forth as the morning, fair as the moon, clear as the sun,
and terrible as
an army
 with banners?

translated_text:
I went down into the garden of nuts to see the fruits of the valley,
and to see whether the vine flourished,
and the pomegranates budded.
original_text:
I went down into the garden of nuts to see the fruits of the valley,
and to see whether the vine flourished,
and the pomegranates budded.

translated_text:
Or ever I was aware, my soul made me
like the chariots of Amminadib.
original_text:
Or ever I was aware, my soul made me
like the chariots of Amminadib.

translated_text: Return, return, O Shulamite; return, return, that we may look upon thee. What will ye see in the Shulamite? As it were the company of two armies.
original_text: Return, return, O Shulamite; return, return, that we may look upon thee. What will ye see in the Shulamite? As it were the company of two armies.

translated_text:
O that thou
wert as my brother, that sucked the breasts of my mother!
when I should find thee without, I would kiss thee; yea, I should not be despised.
original_text:
O that thou
wert as my brother, that sucked the breasts of my mother!
when I should find thee without, I would kiss thee; yea, I should not be despised.

translated_text:
I would lead thee,
and bring thee into my mother’s house,
who would instruct me: I would cause thee to drink of spiced wine of the juice of my pomegranate.
original_text:
I would lead thee,
and bring thee into my mother’s house,
who would instruct me: I would cause thee to drink of spiced wine of the juice of my pomegranate.

translated_text:
His left hand
should be under my head, and his right hand should embrace me.
original_text:
His left hand
should be under my head, and his right hand should embrace me.

translated_text:
I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, that ye stir not up, nor awake
my love, until he please.
original_text:
I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, that ye stir not up, nor awake
my love, until he please.

translated_text:
Who
is this that cometh up from the wilderness, leaning upon her beloved? I raised thee up under the apple tree: there thy mother brought thee forth: there she brought thee forth
that bare thee.
original_text:
Who
is this that cometh up from the wilderness, leaning upon her beloved? I raised thee up under the apple tree: there thy mother brought thee forth: there she brought thee forth
that bare thee.

translated_text:
Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm: for love
is strong as death; jealousy
is cruel as the grave: the coals thereof
are coals of fire,
which hath a most vehement flame.
original_text:
Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm: for love
is strong as death; jealousy
is cruel as the grave: the coals thereof
are coals of fire,
which hath a most vehement flame.

translated_text:
Many waters cannot quench love, neither can the floods drown it: if
a man would give all the substance of his house for love, it would utterly be contemned.
original_text:
Many waters cannot quench love, neither can the floods drown it: if
a man would give all the substance of his house for love, it would utterly be contemned.

translated_text: We have a little sister, and she hath no breasts: what shall we do for our sister in the day when she shall be spoken for?
original_text: We have a little sister, and she hath no breasts: what shall we do for our sister in the day when she shall be spoken for?

translated_text:
If she
be a wall, we will build upon her a palace of silver: and if she
be a door, we will inclose her with boards of cedar.
original_text:
If she
be a wall, we will build upon her a palace of silver: and if she
be a door, we will inclose her with boards of cedar.

translated_text:
I
am a wall, and my breasts like towers: then was I in his eyes as one that found favour.
original_text:
I
am a wall, and my breasts like towers: then was I in his eyes as one that found favour.

translated_text:
Solomon had a vineyard at Baal-hamon; he let out the vineyard unto keepers; every one for the fruit thereof was to bring a thousand
pieces
 of silver.
original_text:
Solomon had a vineyard at Baal-hamon; he let out the vineyard unto keepers; every one for the fruit thereof was to bring a thousand
pieces
 of silver.

translated_text:
My vineyard, which
is mine,
is before me: thou, O Solomon,
must have a thousand, and those that keep the fruit thereof two hundred.
original_text:
My vineyard, which
is mine,
is before me: thou, O Solomon,
must have a thousand, and those that keep the fruit thereof two hundred.

translated_text:
Thou that dwellest in the gardens, the companions hearken to thy voice: cause me to hear
it.
original_text:
Thou that dwellest in the gardens, the companions hearken to thy voice: cause me to hear
it.

translated_text: Make haste, my beloved, and be thou like to a roe or to a young hart upon the mountains of spices.
original_text: Make haste, my beloved, and be thou like to a roe or to a young hart upon the mountains of spices.

translated_text: By night on my bed I sought him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.
original_text: By night on my bed I sought him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.

translated_text: I will rise now, and go about the city in the streets, and in the broad ways I will seek him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.
original_text: I will rise now, and go about the city in the streets, and in the broad ways I will seek him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.

translated_text:
The watchmen that go about the city found me:
to whom I said,
 Saw ye him whom my soul loveth?
original_text:
The watchmen that go about the city found me:
to whom I said,
 Saw ye him whom my soul loveth?

translated_text: It was but a little that I passed from them, but I found him whom my soul loveth: I held him, and would not let him go, until I had brought him into my mother’s house, and into the chamber of her that conceived me.
original_text: It was but a little that I passed from them, but I found him whom my soul loveth: I held him, and would not let him go, until I had brought him into my mother’s house, and into the chamber of her that conceived me.

translated_text:
I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that ye stir not up, nor awake
my love, till he please.
original_text:
I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that ye stir not up, nor awake
my love, till he please.

translated_text:
Who
is this that cometh out of the wilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all powders of the merchant?
original_text:
Who
is this that cometh out of the wilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all powders of the merchant?

translated_text:
Behold his bed, which
is Solomon’s; threescore valiant men
are about it, of the valiant of Israel.
original_text:
Behold his bed, which
is Solomon’s; threescore valiant men
are about it, of the valiant of Israel.

translated_text:
They all hold swords,
being expert in war: every man
hath his sword upon his thigh because of fear in the night.
original_text:
They all hold swords,
being expert in war: every man
hath his sword upon his thigh because of fear in the night.

translated_text: King Solomon made himself a chariot of the wood of Lebanon.
original_text: King Solomon made himself a chariot of the wood of Lebanon.

translated_text:
He made the pillars thereof
of silver, the bottom thereof
of gold, the covering of it
of purple, the midst thereof being paved
with love, for the daughters of Jerusalem.
original_text:
He made the pillars thereof
of silver, the bottom thereof
of gold, the covering of it
of purple, the midst thereof being paved
with love, for the daughters of Jerusalem.

translated_text: Go forth, O ye daughters of Zion, and behold king Solomon with the crown wherewith his mother crowned him in the day of his espousals, and in the day of the gladness of his heart.
original_text: Go forth, O ye daughters of Zion, and behold king Solomon with the crown wherewith his mother crowned him in the day of his espousals, and in the day of the gladness of his heart.

translated_text:
I
am the rose of Sharon,
and the lily of the valleys.
original_text:
I
am the rose of Sharon,
and the lily of the valleys.

translated_text:
As the lily among thorns, so
is my love among the daughters.
original_text:
As the lily among thorns, so
is my love among the daughters.

translated_text:
As the apple tree among the trees of the wood, so
is my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow with great delight, and his fruit
was sweet to my taste.
original_text:
As the apple tree among the trees of the wood, so
is my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow with great delight, and his fruit
was sweet to my taste.

translated_text:
He brought me to the banqueting house, and his banner over me
was
 love.
original_text:
He brought me to the banqueting house, and his banner over me
was
 love.

translated_text:
Stay me with flagons, comfort me with apples: for I
am sick of love.
original_text:
Stay me with flagons, comfort me with apples: for I
am sick of love.

translated_text:
His left hand
is under my head, and his right hand doth embrace me.
original_text:
His left hand
is under my head, and his right hand doth embrace me.

translated_text:
I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that ye stir not up, nor awake
my love, till he please.
original_text:
I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that ye stir not up, nor awake
my love, till he please.

translated_text: The voice of my beloved! behold, he cometh leaping upon the mountains, skipping upon the hills.
original_text: The voice of my beloved! behold, he cometh leaping upon the mountains, skipping upon the hills.

translated_text: My beloved is like a roe or a young hart: behold, he standeth behind our wall, he looketh forth at the windows, shewing himself through the lattice.
original_text: My beloved is like a roe or a young hart: behold, he standeth behind our wall, he looketh forth at the windows, shewing himself through the lattice.

translated_text: My beloved spake, and said unto me, Rise up, my love, my fair one, and come away.
original_text: My beloved spake, and said unto me, Rise up, my love, my fair one, and come away.

translated_text:
For, lo, the winter is past, the rain is over
and gone;
original_text:
For, lo, the winter is past, the rain is over
and gone;

translated_text:
The fig tree putteth forth her green figs, and the vines
with
 the tender grape give a
good smell. Arise, my love, my fair one, and come away.
original_text:
The fig tree putteth forth her green figs, and the vines
with
 the tender grape give a
good smell. Arise, my love, my fair one, and come away.

translated_text:
O my dove,
that art in the clefts of the rock, in the secret
places of the stairs, let me see thy countenance, let me hear thy voice; for sweet
is thy voice, and thy countenance
is
 comely.
original_text:
O my dove,
that art in the clefts of the rock, in the secret
places of the stairs, let me see thy countenance, let me hear thy voice; for sweet
is thy voice, and thy countenance
is
 comely.

translated_text:
Take us the foxes, the little foxes, that spoil the vines: for our vines
have tender grapes.
original_text:
Take us the foxes, the little foxes, that spoil the vines: for our vines
have tender grapes.

translated_text:
My beloved
is mine, and I
am his: he feedeth among the lilies.
original_text:
My beloved
is mine, and I
am his: he feedeth among the lilies.

translated_text: Until the day break, and the shadows flee away, turn, my beloved, and be thou like a roe or a young hart upon the mountains of Bether.
original_text: Until the day break, and the shadows flee away, turn, my beloved, and be thou like a roe or a young hart upon the mountains of Bether.

translated_text:
I am come into my garden, my sister,
my spouse: I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk: eat, O friends; drink, yea, drink abundantly, O beloved.
original_text:
I am come into my garden, my sister,
my spouse: I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk: eat, O friends; drink, yea, drink abundantly, O beloved.

translated_text:
I sleep, but my heart waketh:
it is the voice of my beloved that knocketh,
saying, Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled: for my head is filled with dew,
and my locks with the drops of the night.
original_text:
I sleep, but my heart waketh:
it is the voice of my beloved that knocketh,
saying, Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled: for my head is filled with dew,
and my locks with the drops of the night.

translated_text: I have put off my coat; how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet; how shall I defile them?
original_text: I have put off my coat; how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet; how shall I defile them?

translated_text:
My beloved put in his hand by the hole
of the door, and my bowels were moved for him.
original_text:
My beloved put in his hand by the hole
of the door, and my bowels were moved for him.

translated_text:
I rose up to open to my beloved; and my hands dropped
with
 myrrh, and my fingers
with sweet smelling myrrh, upon the handles of the lock.
original_text:
I rose up to open to my beloved; and my hands dropped
with
 myrrh, and my fingers
with sweet smelling myrrh, upon the handles of the lock.

translated_text:
I opened to my beloved; but my beloved had withdrawn himself,
and
 was gone: my soul failed when he spake: I sought him, but I could not find him; I called him, but he gave me no answer.
original_text:
I opened to my beloved; but my beloved had withdrawn himself,
and
 was gone: my soul failed when he spake: I sought him, but I could not find him; I called him, but he gave me no answer.

translated_text: The watchmen that went about the city found me, they smote me, they wounded me; the keepers of the walls took away my veil from me.
original_text: The watchmen that went about the city found me, they smote me, they wounded me; the keepers of the walls took away my veil from me.

translated_text:
I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, if ye find my beloved, that ye tell him, that I
am sick of love.
original_text:
I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, if ye find my beloved, that ye tell him, that I
am sick of love.

translated_text:
What
is thy beloved more than
another beloved, O thou fairest among women? what
is thy beloved more than
another
 beloved, that thou dost so charge us?
original_text:
What
is thy beloved more than
another beloved, O thou fairest among women? what
is thy beloved more than
another
 beloved, that thou dost so charge us?

translated_text:
My beloved
is white and ruddy, the chiefest among ten thousand.
original_text:
My beloved
is white and ruddy, the chiefest among ten thousand.

translated_text:
His head
is as the most fine gold, his locks
are
 bushy,
and black as a raven.
original_text:
His head
is as the most fine gold, his locks
are
 bushy,
and black as a raven.

translated_text:
His eyes
are as
the eyes of doves by the rivers of waters, washed with milk,
and fitly set.
original_text:
His eyes
are as
the eyes of doves by the rivers of waters, washed with milk,
and fitly set.

translated_text:
His cheeks
are as a bed of spices,
as sweet flowers: his lips
like lilies, dropping sweet smelling myrrh.
original_text:
His cheeks
are as a bed of spices,
as sweet flowers: his lips
like lilies, dropping sweet smelling myrrh.

translated_text:
His hands
are as gold rings set with the beryl: his belly
is as bright ivory overlaid
with sapphires.
original_text:
His hands
are as gold rings set with the beryl: his belly
is as bright ivory overlaid
with sapphires.

translated_text:
His legs
are as pillars of marble, set upon sockets of fine gold: his countenance
is as Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.
original_text:
His legs
are as pillars of marble, set upon sockets of fine gold: his countenance
is as Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.

translated_text:
His mouth
is most sweet: yea, he
is altogether lovely. This
